title: Enforce streaming limits on ingest and artifact uploads
description:
## Problem
_IngestBodyLimit in server/http.py:108-130 checks only Content-Length, so chunked ingest bypasses the 8 MiB limit and is buffered/parsing-bound. Artifact PUT streams to disk without any ceiling (http.py:322-344), and upload-before-declaration can retain arbitrary unknown blobs. This is reachable anonymously under the current default server launch.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Stream a /ingest request larger than 8 MiB without Content-Length.
2. Observe that _IngestBodyLimit does not return 413 before parsing.
3. Stream an oversized artifact PUT and observe bytes are written until client EOF without a configured ceiling.

## Proposed Change
count actual ASGI receive bytes for ingest; configure an artifact maximum; stop declared uploads as soon as actual/declared size is exceeded; bound or reject upload-before-declaration; clean temporary and metadata state on rejection.

## Acceptance Criteria
chunked ingest over 8 MiB and oversized declared/undeclared artifacts return 413 without consuming the full stream or leaving files/DB state; exact-limit requests succeed.
close_reason: Completed: _IngestBodyLimit meters actual ASGI receive bytes (buffer+replay) so chunked bodies cannot bypass 8 MiB; put_artifact closes over min(max_artifact_bytes[default 2 GiB], stored-blob/declared size) and fails fast 413 in-loop, tmp unlinked, no DB writes; undeclared uploads stay accepted but bounded. 12 new tests; live-verified on uvicorn: 17.9 MiB chunked -> 413, 2048B>1024 cap -> 413 with zero leftover files, exact-cap -> 202. Merged as 55a46e2; just check: 1309 passed, 6 skipped.

title: Centralize the selection token wire contract
description:
## Problem
dashboard/selection_tokens.py explicitly reimplements the client selection-token codec byte-for-byte. Drift silently breaks dashboard/notebook handoff even though jernerics-schema is already the shared v3 wire-contract package.

## Proposed Change
move encode/decode and SelectionTokenError into jernerics-schema, migrate both consumers, and delete the duplicate implementation with no compatibility alias.

## Acceptance Criteria
existing client/server round-trip tests pass against the shared implementation and no independent base64/token codec remains in dashboard or client production code.

## Design notes (locked 2026-08-30, user-approved)

- Shared codec lives in a new `jernerics-schema` module and stays dumb:
  encode/decode + one error type only.
- The dashboard's `project` scope check on decode is a view concern, not
  wire format — it stays in the dashboard, wrapping the shared decode.
- `SelectionTokenError` is the name that survives into the schema package.
  The client's token paths (`encode_selection`/`decode_selection`,
  `tracking/client.py:97-139`) raise/propagate it where they currently raise
  `TrackingClientError`; callers catching `TrackingClientError` for token
  errors are migrated in the same change. No compat alias for either name.
close_reason: Selection-token codec centralized in jernerics-schema (selection_tokens.py); client and dashboard migrated with clean cutover, no shims

comments.author: jerry
comments.text: 2026-08-22 validity sweep: duplicate codecs remain byte-identical and both consumers already depend on jernerics-schema. One design decision is unresolved: literal 'no compatibility alias' would break the public jernerics.tracking encode_selection/decode_selection imports used by docs and tests. Recommended minimal cutover is one schema implementation with the client package re-exporting the shared functions at its existing public surface; delete the server duplicate module.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Triage verification (2026-08-30, at HEAD): confirmed. Client codec at tracking/client.py:97-139 (encode_selection/decode_selection); dashboard reimplements the same wire format at jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/selection_tokens.py — sorted compact JSON {"v":..,"selection":..}, unpadded urlsafe base64, altchars+validate decode — differing only in exception types (TrackingClientError vs SelectionTokenError) and the dashboard's project-scope check. jernerics-schema has Selection (selection.py) but no token codec. Migration target is real.

title: interactive: surface mutagen sync conflicts instead of silent freeze
description:
## Problem

Live HPC session confirmed: mutagen two-way-safe sessions accumulate conflicts across jernerics session churn (every terminate+create wipes the baseline; any file differing across endpoints at recreation becomes a permanent '<non-existent> -> File' conflict). Conflicted files propagate in neither direction. Both is_converged() and the reconnect check in _ensure_interactive_sync ignore the conflict count, so the CLI reports sync as live/running while files are frozen.

## Locked design (user-approved)

Surface-only, never overwrite:
- Parse {{len .Conflicts}} into SessionInfo; is_converged requires conflicts == 0; is_idle keeps the old Watching+connected semantics and gates start() (must NOT trigger the tar/scp one-shot fallback on conflicts).
- Reconnect path: 'already running' only when healthy; otherwise print status/connected/conflicts + conflicted paths + remediation, no restart.
- Fresh path: warn + list paths after start when conflicts > 0.
- conflicted_paths(name) via dedicated sync list template.
- Add .direnv/ to INTERACTIVE_EXCLUDES (absolute nix-store symlinks cause scan problems).
close_reason: Completed: conflict-aware SessionInfo/is_converged/is_idle split, conflicted_paths(), report-only _warn_sync_unhealthy in reconnect+fresh paths, .direnv/ excluded. Verified: 122 tests, just lint, just format-check exit 0; live daemon probe parses conflicts=0, is_converged=True; production reconnect path prints 'already running' against real session.

title: Dashboard UX: should roll-up pills become scope filter chips (vs a dedicated sweep-selection panel)?
description:
Follow-on from jernerics-sdt6 (only the failed roll-up pill is interactive). Two related open questions about how sweeps are narrowed in the dashboard.

Current state (grounded):
- Narrowing already exists in three places: the sidebar workspace grid (sweep-grid: quick filter, ag-grid column filters via filterModel, sort, pick-rows-to-scope), the scope line ("Scope: All sweeps" vs picked names, workspace.py:251), and the overview tab's own overview-sweep-grid (click-to-inspect, workspace.py:1281).
- State/health-based narrowing ("show me the failing sweeps") exists only buried in sidebar ag-grid column menus. The overview roll-up's pills (state, health, monitoring counts) are read-only aggregates over the scope — except failed, which opens a triage panel.

Question: which direction for "select sweeps by tag"?
- Option A — pills as filter chips: state/health/monitoring pills narrow the overview scope when clicked, with an explicit All/clear chip for the default view. Reuses the existing scope model (picks + include-archived/invalid flags), adds no chrome, and extends the precedent the failed pill already set. Cost: the roll-up changes meaning from read-only aggregate to interactive control; needs a clear active-filter representation.
- Option B — dedicated sweep-selection panel: a first-class panel for browsing/selecting sweeps. Cost: duplicates the sidebar grid's browse role and creates a second selection surface competing with the scope line; current design (sidebar = browse/pick, overview = aggregate + in-scope grid) would need rework to avoid two sources of truth for scope.

Leaning: A (chips on the roll-up) as the incremental path; B only if sidebar+overview prove insufficient for real workflows. Blocked from deciding until someone exercises the dashboard against a multi-sweep project.
close_reason: Superseded by epic jernerics-g5rw (Investigations overhaul): the locked IA rebuilds the Overview surface — every tile uniformly interactive as a filter (prototype overview.html ?f= pattern) and tab navigation Overview·Investigations·Exceptions provides the explicit way back; the pills-vs-panel question is answered by the validated prototype (filter tiles + sweep-table row selection, no dedicated panel). No independent fix under the old surface.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Concrete defect motivating this: jernerics-sdt6 (one interactive pill among identical static pills; failure view has no explicit way back).

title: Fail closed on unauthenticated public server binds
description:
## Problem
packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/__main__.py:16-18 defaults --host to [::], while http.py:136-146 installs no auth dependency when JERNERICS_API_KEY is absent. A default launch therefore exposes query, ingest, artifact, read, and dashboard surfaces to every reachable peer. The NixOS module's loopback default does not protect direct CLI launches.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Unset JERNERICS_API_KEY.
2. Run `python -m jernerics_server` with defaults.
3. From another reachable host, POST a read query or request a dashboard/read endpoint.
4. Observe the all-interface bind and successful anonymous access.

## Proposed Change
default the CLI to loopback; reject non-loopback keyless binds unless an explicit insecure-development override is provided; emit an unmistakable auth-disabled warning.

## Acceptance Criteria
default keyless launch binds loopback; keyless [::]/0.0.0.0 fails without the override; public keyed launch returns 401 without the token and succeeds with it. Add behavioral CLI/server tests.
close_reason: Completed: default bind now 127.0.0.1; keyless non-loopback binds exit 1 without --allow-unauthenticated; loud DISABLED warnings; keyed 401/200 covered by existing TestQueryAuth. New tests/test_main.py (truth table + 4 main() paths). Merged as 22bef44 on main; just check: 1281 passed, 6 skipped. Live-verified refusal (exit 1) and loopback default.

title: Migrate the example trial to the script API
description:
## Problem
example/trial.py:10 still defines def trial(config, tracker) and has no executable entry point. The runner executes the file as a subprocess script (runner.py:115-118), so the example exits 0 without running or logging anything. example/E2E.md directs users through this stale file. Reproduced with `nix develop -c python3 example/trial.py`: exit 0, no output. The example workspace lock is also pinned to an older git revision.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `nix develop -c python3 example/trial.py`.
2. Observe exit status 0 with no output, trial execution, or tracking because the file only defines a function.

## Proposed Change
rewrite trial.py as a flat script using trial_config()/trial_tracker(), align E2E.md, and refresh the example dependency pin so the walkthrough exercises the current CLI/API.

## Acceptance Criteria
the documented local example executes the configured trials and tracked values are visible through the current tracking commands; the example lock check is current.
close_reason: Completed: example/trial.py is now a flat script (trial_config(defaults=...)+trial_tracker(), tracker.finish) executed directly by runner.py; example uv.lock pins refreshed to current main (uv lock --check passes); agent verified full local pipeline: 5-trial sweep via real runner, 69 events replayed to in-process server, tracking runs/summary/trace show trials+values. Orchestrator re-ran standalone smoke: exit 0 with params/values/artifact/results printed. Unblocks jernerics-log. Merged as e7371cb; just check: 1329 passed, 6 skipped.

title: e2e test_first_trial_materializes_live_without_replay fails (pre-existing, reproducible on clean tree)
description:
## Evidence (2026-08-27, orchestration session)
- `just test`: `tests/e2e/test_tracking_v3.py::TestSubmissionEvents::test_first_trial_materializes_live_without_replay` fails with `assert 0 == 1`; 1392 passed, 6 skipped otherwise.
- Reproduced in isolation twice, identical assertion.
- Reproduced with ALL packages/ changes stashed (`git stash push -- packages/`) on c55f967 — fails on the clean tree, so it is NOT caused by jernerics-l6r/jernerics-ykh.
- Remaining tree mods at test time (.beads/, justfile install-skills removal, skills/) do not touch code paths.

## Symptom
From the run log: trial 0.jsonl shows 24/24 events replayed, but the assertion expecting a live-materialized trial count of 1 gets 0 — looks like the first trial does not materialize without replay in this environment. Deterministic, not order-dependent within the file.

## Next step
Needs investigation: run with `-x` and inspect server state between deploy and first trial; suspect timing/environment (server startup grace) or a regression from an earlier change.
close_reason: No longer reproduces: test_first_trial_materializes_live_without_replay passes at current HEAD (2026-08-30, 1 passed in 3.69s). Root cause was the live-ship 409 stall family fixed by 4c912a8/e0fe36f.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Root cause now observable thanks to jernerics-ship-batch-log-response-body-02n (merged): re-running this test with the error-body logging live shows the first batch rejected with HTTP 409 {"error":"validation","event_index":0,"detail":"execution 1de826e5-... references unknown trial fa677616-..."} and deterministic retries thereafter (trials stays 0). So the sweep/submission rows land fine (fixture asserts ship ok); the runner's live batch itself is invalid — an ExecutionStartEvent references a trial_id the server has not applied when the execution row is inserted. Investigate batch composition / canonical ordering (_canonical_order in ingest.py vs the runner's emission order in trial_environment): either the execution leads its trial snapshot within one batch, or the trial snapshot sits in a later batch behind the cursor.

title: remote_dir {project_name} template never substituted in assemble_infrastructure and adapter from_config
description:
Symptom: 'jernerics backend build -b hpc' submits a job whose script dies at: cd /home/jez21005/projects/{project_name}: No such file or directory (SLURM job 28148009, pyrimel consumer).

Root cause: {project_name}/{project-name} templating was applied to cache_dir (PathResolver.resolve_cache) and build_dir (resolve_build_dir), but NOT to remote_dir. Three sites replaced only '~' and passed the template through verbatim:
- backend/submission.py assemble_infrastructure (feeds PathResolver.remote_dir -> build script 'cd', syncer)
- backend/slurm/adapter.py SlurmAdapter.from_config (renders _format_array_script, checker script, and submit_sweep 'cd {self.remote_dir}' — sweeps would fail the same way)
- backend/pueue/adapter.py PueueAdapter.from_config

Escaped detection because unit tests only use concrete remote_dir values (~/experiments/proj) and the symlab reference consumer pins a concrete remote_dir (~/projects/symlab-overfit).

Also surfaced: uv 0.8.14 will not move a git dependency pin when the upstream version is unchanged (5f601af 1.1.0 -> 9978863 1.1.0 stayed pinned through --upgrade-package, --refresh, cache nuke, fresh clone). Consumers must be bumped explicitly; jernerics bumped to 1.1.1 (aa05d33).
close_reason: Fixed in 9978863 (substitute_project_name applied to remote_dir in all three sites, project_name threaded through make_adapter -> from_config; regression test test_remote_dir_project_template_substituted in packages/jernerics/tests/unit/backend/test_submission.py). Verified: 763+172 unit tests pass, ruff clean; pyrimel rebuilt on HPC — build job 28148821 proceeds past the failing cd. Version bump to 1.1.1 in aa05d33 so uv consumers can pick up the pin.

title: e2e live-replay overlap test exceeded IngestRequest 100-event wire cap
description:
Symptom: tests/e2e/test_tracking_v3.py::TestLiveReplayOverlap::test_second_pass_changes_no_state_and_records_the_overlap failed with pydantic ValidationError: IngestRequest.events 'List should have at most 100 items', 165 received (146 in another run — count is timing-dependent via 0.05s heartbeats). Blocked all pushes (just test must pass).

Root cause: the test re-applied scenario.live_events as ONE IngestRequest. The schema caps events at MAX_EVENTS_PER_REQUEST=100 (defended by test_ingest_models.py::test_ingest_request_event_bound), and production shippers chunk at that cap (batch_sync._replay_file, stream_client). The test outgrew the cap when the scenario's live event count rose past 100; a single oversized request was never the real wire behavior for 'a replay with a lost cursor'.

Fix: tests/e2e/test_tracking_v3.py — apply live_events in MAX_EVENTS_PER_REQUEST-sized batches via IngestService.apply, summing duplicates and concatenating conflicts across batches (IngestResult aggregates cleanly). Assertions unchanged.

Verified: tests/e2e/test_tracking_v3.py 16/16 pass; full suite 1364 passed, 6 skipped (remote); just lint + format-check clean.
close_reason: Completed: chunked the overlap test at MAX_EVENTS_PER_REQUEST. Full suite green.

title: Mirror remote project deletions during sync
description:
## Problem
ProjectSync collects only current included files and extracts its tar over the existing remote directory (backend/project_sync.py:41-82). Deleted, renamed, or newly ignored local modules remain executable under the remote /work mount, violating the project's local/HPC equivalence and reproducibility goal. Related to jernerics-wlf's sync subsystem but not its timeout symptom.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Sync a project containing an importable module to an SSH backend.
2. Delete or newly ignore that module locally.
3. Sync again to the same remote project directory.
4. Observe the old module still exists and imports from /work.

## Proposed Change
implement constrained mirror semantics using a prior manifest deletion pass or staging + atomic source swap, while preserving backend-owned state such as container images. Confine deletions beneath the resolved project root.

## Acceptance Criteria
after two syncs, a locally deleted or newly ignored module is absent remotely and cannot import inside /work; current files update; backend-owned artifacts remain.
close_reason: Completed: ProjectSync keeps a remote .jernerics-sync-manifest of the synced set; each sync deletes prior-minus-current paths (shlex-quoted, batches of 100, path-safety filter rejects absolute/../ entries) before tar overlay, then rewrites the manifest; dry_run reports would-delete count. 7 new tests incl. two-sync deletion, new-ignore deletion, manifest tamper, container.sif survival, batching. Merged as e39bbe2; just check: 1329 passed, 6 skipped.

title: Reconcile stale executions so sweeps can become terminal
description:
Split from jernerics-iiv.

Verified failure mode: sweep completeness is currently waiting trials > 0, running trials > 0, or started executions > terminal executions. A dead execution that emits neither execution_end nor a terminal trial snapshot therefore keeps its sweep incomplete forever. Heartbeat-derived stale monitoring is read-time display state only and does not reconcile durable lifecycle facts. Consequences include permanent workspace polling, curated active sweeps remaining visible indefinitely, and retry/observability state disagreeing about whether work ended.

Design decision required: choose the authority that turns a demonstrably dead execution into durable terminal facts. Prefer explicit post-hook/retry/scheduler reconciliation that emits one idempotent execution_end with the appropriate failure kind and a terminal trial snapshot; do not make the read-time stale label itself silently equal terminal, because a stale execution can potentially resume.

Acceptance after the authority is chosen: a confirmed-dead execution produces exactly one durable terminal execution fact and matching terminal trial state; replay/reconciliation is idempotent; active or merely quiet work is never terminalized; the sweep completeness query eventually becomes false without weakening the rule that incomplete curated sweeps remain discoverable.
close_reason: Completed: post-hook reconciliation is the authority — reconcile_study emits one idempotent ExecutionEndEvent (uuid5 reconcile-end:{execution_id}, journal-derived ended_at, FAILURE + STALE_HEARTBEAT) per started-unended execution whose trial is terminal in the journal, into append-only reconcile-executions.jsonl shipped in both RETRY_SUBMITTED and SWEEP_COMPLETE paths; running/quiet trials never terminalized; server unchanged (ingest idempotency verified). Proofs: 26a4fe3, f3d3856; TestReconciledExecutionCompleteness flips incomplete->false, full suite 1937 passed.

title: e2e tracking_v3 first-trial test fails deterministically with ingest 409 storms (environment-dependent)
description:
PROBLEM: tests/e2e/test_tracking_v3.py::TestSubmissionEvents::test_first_trial_materializes_live_without_replay fails with assert 0 == 1 (rows['trials']) - the runner's live event ships all get HTTP 409 from /ingest (10 retries each with backoff), so only the deploy-time events land; the post-hook replay later succeeds ('25 events sent, 0 failures'), confirming the events are valid but the live window conflicts.

EVIDENCE (2026-08-28 evening session): the test PASSED in the full-suite run at commit 9bd029d (1714 passed incl. this test) and began failing deterministically ~40 minutes later with zero relevant code changes: verified failing with the session's uncommitted dashboard changes stashed (same failure at the same commit), and the dashboard work touches no tracking/ingest path. Fails both isolated (62s) and in-class. The scenario is in-process (run_trial + uvicorn on a random port + fresh tmp_path store), so no cross-run state should exist - yet something environmental flipped it. Suspects: ingest conflict rules around repeated snapshots (sweep/submission snapshots re-shipped by the trial differing from deploy-time ones), or retry/backoff timing under load.

NOT the dashboard session's work - filed so it is not lost. Reproduce: pytest 'tests/e2e/test_tracking_v3.py::TestSubmissionEvents::test_first_trial_materializes_live_without_replay' -q and inspect the 409 response bodies the shipper retries on.
close_reason:
Root cause: StreamClient._ship_batch retried a frozen request body. When the first batch closed its 0.5s batch_window before the runner appended trial_snapshot (a single-event [execution_start] batch), ingest correctly 409'd with error=validation (references unknown trial), and the retry loop re-POSTed the same body forever - the snapshot that would clear it sat in the file behind the cursor, unreachable until the 60s flush timeout abandoned the whole stream (24 events) to replay. Load-dependent: fired whenever ask/config exceeded the window; passed on an idle machine.

Fix (packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/stream_client.py): on a 409 whose body parses as IngestError error=validation, re-scan the file from the durable cursor and rebuild the batch with events appended since (bounded by batch_size, immediate retry). Server-side _canonical_order already tiers trial snapshots above executions within one request, so the grown batch validates. Conflicts and other failures keep the frozen-body backoff. _ship_batch now returns the shipped (possibly grown) batch so the loop advances pending/offset past everything actually acked.

Proof: 2 new unit tests (validation-409 absorbs late event and advances cursor; conflict-409 keeps frozen body and leaves cursor). e2e test 4/4 under 2x CPU hogs, ~2s each (was 60-120s wedged). Full suite: 1717 passed, 6 skipped, 48.5s - was 1714+1 failed at ~290s.

title: Container build provides no progress feedback during jernerics run
description:
## Problem

During `jernerics run`, the container build step (Apptainer/Docker) can take 10-20 minutes. There is no progress feedback — the command appears to hang. This is especially bad for agents that need to decide whether to keep waiting or investigate.

## What happens

```
$ jernerics run trial.py config.py --backend hpc
Syncing project...
Building container...   # <- hangs here for 10-20 min with no output
Submitting job...
```

The Apptainer build runs over SSH and its output isn't streamed back.

## Proposed solution

Stream the container build output (or at least progress milestones) back to the caller. Options:

1. Stream SSH stdout/stderr line-by-line during build
2. Print periodic status: "Building container... (3/8 steps)" 
3. Add a `--verbose` flag that enables full output streaming

Even knowing "the build is at step 3 of 8" would prevent agents and humans from thinking the process is hung.
close_reason: Implemented in commit bf10602

title: Post-hook: replace optuna-failed deterministic trials from journal facts
description:
Split out of jernerics-bmo per its decision comment (id 42): the payload-contract work and the post-hook's handling of deterministic failed trials are separate concerns.

CONTEXT:
- Grid-mode (jernerics-s27) and other deterministic sweeps re-run the identical trial when a trial is recorded FAIL in optuna, burning a full compute cycle to reproduce the same result (bmo REPRO: 84/252 tasks failed at finish(results) after 35-51 min of completed compute; retry re-ran identical deterministic work).
- The bmo hardening (oversize error names the artifact remedy; artifacts own durable snapshot bytes) removes the original trigger, but the general problem stands: for deterministic configs, a FAILed trial's retry is guaranteed to reproduce, not explore.

SCOPE:
- Post-hook / retry orchestration: when a sweep config is deterministic (grid mode; no stochastic search_space), decide what the retry system should do with FAILed trials — skip re-enqueue (treat failure as terminal, surface to the user), or re-run deliberately with a recorded reason. Do not layer heuristics onto stochastic sweeps.
- Coordinate with jernerics-43q reconciliation: 43q terminalizes dead executions from journal facts; this bead is about not re-scheduling deterministic FAILs in the first place.

OUT OF SCOPE: ValueEvent size caps, artifact API shape (both settled in bmo).

title: Eliminate wall-clock waits from client tests
description:
## Problem
A measured 80.27-second full-suite run spends about 14 seconds in client tests waiting on real network backoff, polling deadlines, or thread timeouts rather than executing assertions. `TestRetryCheckerUsesSubmitSweep::test_loads_tracking_server` takes 3.29s because it accidentally reaches real `ship_events_file` for `https://track.example.com`. Five batch replay failure cases burn roughly 6 seconds in exponential `time.sleep`; three Mutagen timeout cases burn about 3 seconds; two StreamClient lifecycle cases consume another roughly 2 seconds. These tests protect useful contracts and should not be deleted.

## Proposed Change
Keep every assertion but remove wall-clock dependence: mock `ship_events_file` in the retry-checker test; use a deterministic sleeper/fake clock for batch retry and Mutagen deadline tests; use explicit synchronization or bounded fake time for StreamClient lifecycle tests. Do not weaken retry-count, byte-identical-body, cursor, file-retention, or thread-shutdown assertions, and do not solve this by enabling xdist.

## Acceptance Criteria
The named tests retain their current behavioral assertions and perform no external network access. Their aggregate measured call time falls by at least 10 seconds relative to the recorded profile (3.29s retry checker; 3.01s + four approximately 1s replay cases; three approximately 1s Mutagen cases; 1.01s and 0.93s StreamClient cases). Focused repetitions and the full suite pass without arbitrary longer sleeps. Record before/after `--durations` output in the close reason.
close_reason: Completed in bd8eb98. Focused four-module profile: 128 passed in 7.98s versus revalidated 23.39s baseline, a 15.41s reduction; retry_checker network path is mocked and replay/Mutagen/StreamClient deadlines use deterministic local clock seams without changing production policy. Full nix develop -c just check: lint/format/typecheck green, 1345 passed and 6 skipped in 61.88s.

title: pueue and local backends silently ignore unknown --set keys
description:
## Problem
Discovered while triaging jernerics-ykh. On the slurm backend, unknown `\-\-set` keys render as invalid sbatch directives and (per jernerics-l6r) the failure is swallowed. On pueue and local the failure mode is different but still silent: unknown keys are simply dropped.

- pueue adapter (backend/pueue/adapter.py) consumes only `max_parallel` (popped earlier in submission.py:215); every other key in `params.overrides` is ignored — `--set partition=foo` on a pueue backend is a silent no-op.
- LocalBackend (backend/local_backend.py) has no override handling at all.

## Proposed Direction (not yet designed)
Either validate `--set` keys per backend (each adapter declares its supported keys, mirroring the slurm allowlist from jernerics-ykh) or warn on unused keys at submission time. Needs a design decision before implementation — do not dispatch as-is.
close_reason: Closed after design review (2026-08-30, user decision). Three parts: (1) slurm half already fixed by e85887f — _render_overrides validates against SBATCH_OVERRIDE_KEYS and raises with valid keys listed. (2) Local backend: silent-drop is by design — local exists as a debug surface, not a production run target; leniency over validation. (3) Pueue: deferred until the backend sees real use — no speculative validation for an unused backend (vision.md: grow with real need). Reopen scoped to pueue only when it becomes a real target.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Triage verification (2026-08-30, at HEAD): confirmed. submission.py:215 pops max_parallel only; pueue adapter reads nothing else from params.overrides (pueue/adapter.py:116 is the sole consumption); local_backend.py has no override handling at all; slurm validates against SBATCH_OVERRIDE_KEYS and raises (slurm/adapter.py:312-316). The silent-drop asymmetry across backends is exactly as filed.

title: Cancelled jobs leave orphan checker dependencies pending
description:
## Problem
When `jernerics cancel -b hpc <job_id>` cancels a SLURM job, it cancels the
main array job but leaves the checker dependency job (submitted with
`--dependency=afterany:$ARRAY_JOB_ID`) in PENDING state forever.

## Evidence
On 2026-08-06, ~12 orphan checker jobs accumulated as PENDING with reason
`QOSMinGRES` after multiple experiment cancellations. Each jernerics run
submits two jobs: the array job + a checker job with `--dependency=afterany`.
Cancelling via `jernerics cancel` only kills the array job.

## Fix
`jernerics cancel` should cancel the entire job chain — both the array job
and any checker/dependency jobs associated with it. Options:
1. Track both job IDs at submission time and cancel both
2. Look up dependent jobs via `squeue --dependency` and cancel them
3. Cancel by job name pattern (the checker jobs share the study name)

## Location
The cancel command is in `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/cli.py`.
The job submission (array + checker) is in
`packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/slurm/adapter.py`.
close_reason: Completed: commit c56d699. cancel() now finds and kills dependent checker jobs via squeue dependency lookup.

title: test_join_drains_pending_events flakes under concurrent load
description:
## Problem
`TestShutdown::test_join_drains_pending_events` in packages/jernerics/tests/unit/tracking/test_stream_client.py flakes under concurrent CPU/load. A full-suite run failed with `assert 0 == 1` for transport.requests, while the test passed 10/10 alone and the immediate full-suite rerun passed. The assertion depends on background-thread scheduling rather than a deterministic drain signal.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run the full suite while CPU-heavy Nix/build/browser work runs concurrently.
2. Observe intermittent failure in `test_join_drains_pending_events` because join returns before the transport request is recorded.
3. Run the test repeatedly alone and observe it usually passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
Shutdown exposes or waits on a deterministic drain-complete condition rather than an assumed scheduling window; at least 50 focused repetitions under concurrent load and the full suite pass without increasing arbitrary sleeps or weakening the assertion.
close_reason: Completed: _ship_loop performs one final post-stop scan before returning, so an event written after an empty scan but before join() set stop still ships; deterministic barrier regression test test_event_written_between_empty_scan_and_stop_still_ships demonstrated failing on old code (0 requests) and passing after (1 request, cursor advanced). Focused: 21 passed; full gate: 1359 passed, 6 skipped.

comments.author: jerry
comments.text: 2026-08-22 validity sweep: confirmed as a production shutdown race, not only a flaky assertion. join() gates Thread.join on thread.ident, which can still be None immediately after start() while the new thread is unscheduled; join then returns without waiting and the test observes zero requests. Fix with an explicit client-owned started/drain synchronization condition rather than Thread private fields or longer sleeps; also preserve a final readable-file drain after stop.

comments.author: jerry
comments.text: Correction after runtime inspection of Python 3.12 threading.Thread.start: start() waits on the private _started latch, and _bootstrap_inner sets ident before that latch, so ident is not the observed race. The actual source race is _ship_loop scanning no events just before the writer lands them, then seeing _stop set and returning at lines 119-121 without a final rescan. join() is called after the write completes, so shutdown must force one final post-stop scan before declaring drain complete. Do not use Thread private fields.

title: Script-as-trial: runner executes scripts via subprocess + remove old trial() function path
description:
## Scope

Replace the runner's trial execution model: instead of `from trial import trial; trial(config, tracker)`, the runner writes the resolved config to JSON, sets `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG`, and executes the script via subprocess.

## CRITICAL: No backward compatibility

Do NOT add backward compatibility. Do NOT add a fallback that tries `from trial import trial` first. Do NOT add deprecation warnings. The old entry point is gone — the ONLY execution path is subprocess execution of the script.

## Depends on

- `jernerics-rs5` (trial context API must exist first)

## Changes

### runner.py
- Before executing the trial, write the resolved config dict to a JSON file in the cache dir (e.g., `{cache_dir}/configs/trial_{config_index}.json`)
- Set `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` env var to point at this file
- Execute via `subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(trial_file)])` instead of importing and calling a function
- The trial file is the first positional argument to `jernerics run` (or `jernerics local`)
- Read trial results: the script calls `tracker.finish(results)` which writes to the tracker. The runner reads results from the tracker output (JSONL or whatever the tracker writes).

### Remove old path
- Remove the code path that does `from trial import trial; trial(config, tracker)`
- Remove any tests that mock `trial(config, tracker)` or test the function-call execution model
- Update ALL existing tests in the test suite that assume the function-call model

### CLI changes
- `jernerics run` and `jernerics local` already take a trial file as the first positional arg. This does not change.
- The trial file is now executed as a script, not imported

## Test updates

This is the high-effort part. All tests that currently:
- Mock `trial(config, tracker)` 
- Assert the runner calls a trial function
- Test config injection via function arguments

...must be rewritten to:
- Use subprocess execution model
- Assert env var is set
- Assert script is executed
- Mock or provide a simple trial script for E2E tests

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Runner writes resolved config JSON and sets env var
- [ ] Runner executes trial scripts via subprocess
- [ ] Old `from trial import trial` path completely removed
- [ ] All tests updated and passing
- [ ] No backward compatibility shims
close_reason: Completed: commit d5bb4e4. Runner executes trial scripts via subprocess, sets JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG env var. Old trial() function path removed. 643 tests pass.

title: Points tab: long point values (JSON) are truncated with no way to expand
description:
User report: a value that is too long, such as a JSON value, gets truncated and there is no way to expand it.

Evidence: the Points tab builds every cell as one flat string — _cell() in packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/analysis.py:1566 joins all logged payloads for a (trial, key) with newline --- separators and _format_payload() str()s JSON payloads. AG Grid then clips the cell: no wrap, no tooltip, no expansion affordance. A multi-line or multi-KiB JSON payload is unreadable and the full payload is unreachable in the UI. The Params table on the same tab renders plain strings and has the same clipping behavior.

Fix direction: clamp cell text and offer expansion (click-to-open detail panel/inspector section, or tooltip for moderate sizes); consider wrapText plus autoHeight for bounded payloads. Keep enableCellTextSelection working so values stay copyable.

Acceptance: a trial with a large JSON point value renders a readable cell; the full payload is reachable with one interaction; horizontal layout is not blown out.
close_reason: Completed: Points/Params cells render via ClampedCell (single-line clamp + ellipsis + title); one click opens the full payload in a dismissible popover; full text stays in rowData so cell text selection still copies it. Proofs: 820f4d8; TestClampPolicy + TestPointsTable green, full suite 1896 passed.

title: Console ReferenceError (analysis-expand) every time the user leaves the analysis page
description:
Browser walkthrough on atlas (2026-08-21), reproducible 2x per navigation: leaving /dashboard/analysis (e.g. clicking the brand link to /dashboard/) logs two console errors:

  ReferenceError: A nonexistent object was used in an `Output` of a Dash callback. The id of this object is `analysis-expand` and the property is `value`. ...

Mechanism: callbacks._mint_selection_url (Input analysis-sweep-grid.selectedRows, analysis-family-grid.selectedRows, analysis-expand.value; duplicate Output url.search) is registered globally. When _clear_search_off_analysis strips ?sel= on pathname change, Dash touches the duplicated url.search output and revalidates the callback's inputs against the current layout — the analysis-only components (analysis-expand etc.) are unmounted on every non-analysis page, so validation raises. Navigation still completes; nothing functional broke in testing, but the errors are noisy, fire on every analysis exit, and can mask real client errors.

Candidate fixes to weigh at design time: move minting into a clientside callback; make the mint callback conditional on pathname (State) and no-op without writing url.search when off analysis; or mount the analysis stores/grid stubs in the shell so ids always exist. Decide approach before implementing (repo decision-point rule).

## Decision (locked 2026-08-21, user): always-mounted stores

Chosen approach: move the selection state the mint callback reads into always-mounted shell-level dcc.Stores (present on every page), and have ONE callback own Output url.search — minting ?sel= while on the analysis page and clearing it off-analysis (absorbing _clear_search_off_analysis into that owner). The url.search owner must reference ONLY component ids that exist in the shell on every page: no analysis-only ids (grids, analysis-expand) among its Inputs/States; the analysis grids write their selection into the shell stores instead. Do NOT implement the clientside-callback or pathname-conditional-no-op variants — the ReferenceError fires at Dash's layout-revalidation time, so those leave the error in place.
close_reason: Fixed in 78ee73f + f977850 (merged to main). Root cause (sharper than the bead hypothesis, confirmed against dash-renderer 4.4.1): ReferenceError fires when an everywhere-firable dispatched callback has MIXED present/missing outputs — _hydrate_analysis_tray wrote page-local analysis-expand.value/analysis-error.children. Rewire per locked design: _sync_selection_url is sole owner of url.search referencing only shell ids (mint on tray-edit on analysis, strip on navigation off analysis, never mint on navigation); hydration writes selection-store + new shell analysis-message-store; expand/error fed by page-local callbacks (silently pruned off-page). Regression found in orchestrator verification and fixed in f977850: loaders' initial empty selectedRows write echoed through _edit_analysis_tray and wiped a just-hydrated tray (pre-picked-project deep link lost ?sel= — pre-8c9 main kept it); fixed by skipping empty selectedRows writes on initial call (analysis.mounted_selection + is_initial) and tray_from_edit making only the triggered control's dimension authoritative. Orchestrator browser-verified on worktree harness: analysis exit via brand link + back = zero console errors; mint byte-compatible; pre-picked-project deep link through wh2 login keeps ?sel=, restores sweep checkbox, tray 1 sweep(s), strip on leave; real uncheck still clears. Gates: 1257 passed, 6 skipped.

comments.author: jerry
comments.text: Implemented on fix/8c9 (worktree wt-8c9): always-mounted-store design per locked decision. ONE callback (_sync_selection_url) owns Output url.search — Inputs url.pathname + selection-store.data, States url.search + project-store.data (shell ids only); navigations strip the token, tray edits mint it, navigations never mint (protects deep links from a stale session tray). _hydrate_analysis_tray rewritten to shell-only outputs (selection-store.data + new shell dcc.Store analysis-message-store) — its analysis-expand/analysis-error outputs were the actual ReferenceError source (mixed shell/page-local outputs on a navigation-dispatched callback). Expand checklist + error div now fed by page-local callbacks reading the shell stores. Analysis grids write selection-store only. Token format/hydration byte-compatible (browser-verified identical tokens; fresh-context deep link restores checks/families/expand). Browser (headless chromium): analysis exit via brand AND back logs zero console errors; wh2 login round-trip re-verified. Gates: lint/format-check/typecheck/test all green (1253 passed). Regression tests: callback_map walk asserting no everywhere-firable callback mixes shell and page-local outputs + url.search single-ownership, mirrored in journeys e2e against the mounted app.

title: Show study_name in jernerics jobs output (bridge job to tracking)
description:
## Problem

Job metadata (`save_job_meta`) does not store `study_name`. Without it, there is no bridge from a scheduler job to its tracking data. The overnight OMP run exposed this: the agent could see jobs were RUNNING but had to SSH and parse `.out` files to know what study or step they were at.

## Scope (revised after discussion with Jerry)

**Only add `study_name` to job meta + display it as a column in `jernerics jobs`.** Do NOT add metrics to jobs — that is `jernerics summary`'s job. Clean separation:

- `jernerics jobs` → scheduler view (job_id, study_name, status)
- `jernerics summary <study>` → metrics view (loss, step, params)

```
JOB_ID      STUDY                       STATUS
26887165    overfit_seed42              RUNNING
26887168    overfit_seed123             RUNNING
```

Then `jernerics summary overfit_seed42` takes you to the metrics.

## Implementation

1. `save_job_meta` — add `study_name` field at submission time
2. `cli.py::jobs()` — add STUDY column, read from job meta
3. Update `JobInfo` model if needed

## Test plan

- Unit: job meta includes study_name after submission
- Unit: jobs table renders study column
- Backward compat: old job meta without study_name shows blank

## Definition of done

1. `just check` passes
2. `just typecheck` passes
3. Commit: `feat(cli): show study_name in jobs output (jernerics-8g8)`
close_reason: Done — committed 7a72bdc, merged to beads-test, pushed

title: Remote e2e build_backend signals completion before the sif copy lands
description:
## Problem
build_backend's completion signal (image/.build_marker mtime change) fires while the apptainer build's final sif copy is still in flight. During the jernerics-log repin run the fixture's one-shot server exec'd the partial file (image format not recognized) and the first test_retry_hpc attempt failed in SETUP; a rerun seconds later passed untouched. Suite-level flake in _build_state, not an assertion problem.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger an image rebuild via build_backend on a remote backend (or the e2e fixture).
2. Poll for the marker-mtime change and immediately apptainer exec the sif the instant it flips.
3. Observe intermittent 'image format not recognized' on first use after a rebuild.

## Acceptance Criteria
build_backend never reports completion while the sif is mid-write (stable-size window or marker touched only after the final copy/rename completes); a rebuild-then-immediately-start sequence cannot observe a partial image.
close_reason: Completed: _build_state now reports only the .build_marker mtime (written after the build command exits under set -e); the image fingerprint is excluded because sif/docker timestamps move mid-build and caused premature completion. build_backend wait logic unchanged. Verified: pytest collection 6 tests, read-only SSH probes return clean marker mtimes on scimlab (1787420727) and hpc (1787444169), full gate 1362 passed, 6 skipped. No remote jobs were submitted.

comments.author: jerry
comments.text: 2026-08-22 validity sweep: still actionable, but the production .build_marker is already safe: backend.py writes it only after the container build command exits under set -e. The race is tests/e2e_remote/_helpers.py::_build_state returning changed when container.sif mtime (or Docker Created) changes before the marker. Narrow fix: poll the marker completion token specifically, then inspect/use the image; do not add a production stable-size heuristic.

title: e2e live-replay overlap test exceeded IngestRequest 100-event wire cap
description:
Symptom: tests/e2e/test_tracking_v3.py::TestLiveReplayOverlap::test_second_pass_changes_no_state_and_records_the_overlap failed with pydantic ValidationError: IngestRequest.events 'List should have at most 100 items', 165 received (146 in another run — count is timing-dependent via 0.05s heartbeats). Blocked all pushes (just test must pass).

Root cause: the test re-applied scenario.live_events as ONE IngestRequest. The schema caps events at MAX_EVENTS_PER_REQUEST=100 (defended by test_ingest_models.py::test_ingest_request_event_bound), and production shippers chunk at that cap (batch_sync._replay_file, stream_client). The test outgrew the cap when the scenario's live event count rose past 100; a single oversized request was never the real wire behavior for 'a replay with a lost cursor'.

Fix: tests/e2e/test_tracking_v3.py — apply live_events in MAX_EVENTS_PER_REQUEST-sized batches via IngestService.apply, summing duplicates and concatenating conflicts across batches (IngestResult aggregates cleanly). Assertions unchanged.

Verified: tests/e2e/test_tracking_v3.py 16/16 pass; full suite 1364 passed, 6 skipped (remote); just lint + format-check clean.
close_reason: Completed: chunked the overlap test at MAX_EVENTS_PER_REQUEST (tests/e2e/test_tracking_v3.py). e2e file 16/16, full suite 1364 passed 6 skipped, lint+format clean.

title: Make retry host filesystem side effects explicit
description:
## Problem
StdoutHost is the retry-checker host that emits a script, but write_file/mkdir/remove_file are silent no-ops and file_exists is always false (backend/host.py:53-83). submit_sweep writes updated RetryContext through host.write_file (submission.py:186-190), so chained retries can keep the original context silently. Any future host-side prerequisite can also disappear without an error.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run a chained retry submission through StdoutHost.
2. Inspect the host retry context after depth 2.
3. Observe that submit_sweep called write_file but StdoutHost silently discarded it, leaving the prior context.

## Proposed Change
make StdoutHost emit safe filesystem commands into the composed script or fail explicitly for unsupported operations; do not silently discard side effects.

## Acceptance Criteria
after retry depth 2 the host retry context reflects depth 2 and current overrides/paths, or unsupported use fails loudly; unit coverage proves every Host protocol side effect has defined StdoutHost behavior.

The env-file no-op is deliberate and documented (submission.py:90-92). One real residue, accepted as minor: retry submissions leave no sweep/job rows on the tracking server (submission-events write no-ops through StdoutHost) — observability only, retries themselves run correctly. If that gap matters later, file a narrow issue then (vision.md: grow with real need, not ahead of it).

title: Unify Slurm cache template resolution

title: Autolog job resource metrics from sacct (wall/CPU/mem/allocation) into tracking
description:
# Autolog job resource metrics from sacct into tracking

## Decision (2026-08-30, user-approved)

Yes — autolog resource metrics as default harness behavior, **sacct-only, post-hoc**.
No in-job sampling of any kind. GPU **utilization** sampling (NVML thread) is
explicitly out of scope: non-goal until a concrete analysis needs utilization
*curves* rather than totals. GPU **allocation counts** (gres via AllocTRES) are
in scope — budgeting needs allocation x time, which sacct always provides.

Rationale: (1) budgeting questions ("40 GPU-hours or 400?") are answerable from
Elapsed + AllocCPUS + ReqMem + AllocTRES on any Slurm, including clusters that
emit no TRESUsage; (2) sacct is not an archive — clusters purge the accounting
DB after weeks-to-months, so capture-at-completion is the entire value of
"have it on hand"; (3) a post-hoc, timeout-bounded query cannot add a trial
failure mode — the hard isolation requirement holds by construction.

## Scope

### 1. sacct query (authoritative pattern)

```
sacct -n -P -j <job_id> --format=JobIDRaw,State,ExitCode,Elapsed,AllocCPUS,ReqMem,MaxRSS,AveRSS,%CPU,CPUTime,AllocTRES,NodeList
```

Strip step/aux rows: `grep -v -E "\.(batch|extern|[0-9]+)$"` on JobIDRaw.
Parse suffix-scaled values (K/M/G/T) explicitly. Missing/unknown field -> null.
Never raise.

### 2. Record shape (locked)

New append-only record type in `jernerics-schema` (e.g. `JobResourceRecord`),
referencing `job_id` (+ study/submission linkage). Do NOT bolt fields onto the
existing JobSnapshotEvent — ingest is append-only and the snapshot already
landed by the time resources are queryable.

Fields: `wall_time_s`, `cpu_time_s`, `cpu_pct`, `max_rss_mb`, `ave_rss_mb`,
`alloc_cpus`, `req_mem`, `alloc_tres` (raw string, carries gres/gpu counts),
`node_list`, `state`, `exit_code`. No GPU utilization fields exist in the
record at all — no dead null columns.

### 3. Emission path (two named variants; step 0 picks)

- **Step 0 — verify first:** from a compute node on the target cluster, run the
  query above for a known past job. Some clusters block compute-node slurmdbd
  access.
- If sacct works there: emit best-effort from the post-hook at completion.
  Timeout-bounded (10s). Failure -> one stderr line, rely on backfill.
- If blocked: emit from the deploy-side post-sweep hook instead.
  Record which variant was chosen in the implementation.

### 4. CLI: `jernerics job resources <job-id>`

Queries sacct, prints the parsed record, and when a tracking server is
configured (and `--ship` given, or non-interactive), appends it to the server.
Doubles as the on-demand query surface and the backfill tool for anything the
post-hook window missed. Must work for past jobs within the cluster's
retention window.

## Hard requirements

- Failure isolation: collection never raises into the trial/post-hook success
  path; timeouts bounded; missing fields degrade to null, never error.
- No new dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

1. One real HPC job: its resource record is in the tracker via post-hook or
   backfill, and `jernerics job resources <id>` prints the same numbers.
2. A job whose sacct row lacks fields (e.g. no AllocTRES) lands with nulls and
   no error.
3. With sacct unreachable/blocked: the sweep still completes, a warning is
   logged, backfill recovers the record later.
4. Unit tests: suffix parsing (K/M/G/T), step-row stripping, timeout path,
   null degradation.
close_reason: Implemented via herdr dispatch (e7t-agent), commit 4a03c6b, merged to main. sacct parser (backend/slurm/sacct.py) with full null-degradation, JobResourceEvent in schema (append-only, uuid5 id so re-captures reconcile), server ingest/query + unlinked job_resources table, post-hook best-effort capture (whole body exception-guarded, never fails the hook), jernerics job resources CLI with --ship. Verified: 1823 tests in worktree, live fake-sacct→uvicorn ship test, full suite 1828 passed post-merge. Remaining real-cluster items documented: array-row ordering assumption, compute-node slurmdbd reachability (backfill CLI is the recovery path), %CPU thousands-separator forms.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Triage verification (2026-08-30, at HEAD): the motivating gap is real in the harness. log_metric (trial_context.py:33-109) is user-facing only — nothing in the runner/tracker calls it with resource data; sacct is queried only for job state (slurm/adapter.py:474-485, 548-560), never usage; no CPU/GPU/memory sampling anywhere. Wall time is derivable only from execution lifecycle events. Question remains open for a design decision.

title: Investigations: cross-sweep organization for humans and agents (dashboard + CLI + API)
description:
# Investigations: cross-sweep organization for humans and agents

Status: DESIGN LOCKED. The information architecture and interaction model were validated in a real-data throwaway prototype (`/home/jerry/Projects/jernerics-proto`, pyrimel + symlab live tracking data, six build rounds + four user-driven correction rounds). This epic is the executable spec for production. Do not re-open settled questions here; "Deferred to real usage" items are decided with defaults and must not block implementation.

Research context: `agent://MLDashResearch`, `agent://OpsDashResearch`, `agent://UXResearch`, `agent://WebDesignResearch`. Canonical terms per CONTEXT.md: Sweep (never user-facing "study"), Trial, Selection.

## 1. Locked information architecture (validated)

- Project scope tabs: `Overview · Investigations · Exceptions`.
  - Catalog is merged into Overview's existing `Active / All` control; no separate global Catalog tab. Project pages show project-scoped counts only (the prototype's cross-project rollup table was a bug, not a feature).
  - Overview keeps: operational tiles (each tile filters, uniformly interactive — resolves jernerics-sdt6 and jernerics-1s6v), Active/All scope, paginated sortable sweep table with row selection.
  - Exceptions stays project-scoped failure triage; Investigations only surface member warnings, curation stays in Exceptions.
- Investigation views: `Compare · Series · Points · Search` plus actions `Open in Python` and `Edit members`. Python is never a global tab. Default tab is named **Compare** (decision; see deferred).
- Sweep hub views: `Overview · Series · Points · Search`, rendering only views the sweep's real data supports.
- Member scoping: opening an analysis view "from" one member carries that member scope across view switches; a visible `All members` control clears it; Compare never pretends a one-member scope is the full comparison (link visibly drops scope).
- Sweep opened from an Investigation: breadcrumb `pyrimel › Investigations › <name> › <sweep>` + explicit back link. Chart/table selection never mutates membership.

## 2. Investigation domain contract

- An Investigation is a saved analytical question over an explicit set of sweeps — not a folder, tag collection, journal, or lineage graph.
- Record fields: stable id, project, unique-per-project name, primary comparison factor, outcome key, optional replicate factor, archived flag, created/updated timestamps, explicit member sweep ids.
- Membership is many-to-many: a sweep may belong to several Investigations; membership implies no ancestry or inherited knowledge.
- Sweeps do NOT require an Investigation to run (no mandatory classification).
- Stored as server-owned organizational metadata — NOT immutable tracking events. Tracked facts (values, artifacts, scheduler state) stay immutable; Investigations + existing sweep curation are the only writes.
- Compatibility policy: hard-reject only cross-project / missing / malformed member references. Surface as visible warnings (never silent): missing outcome or factor values, differing git revisions or config sources, incomplete sweeps, sparse parameter overlap.
- Analysis semantics (validated on real data):
  - Invalid members: visible everywhere, excluded from numerical analysis by default, with an explicit include toggle and honest empty states stating how many data-bearing members are excluded.
  - Archived members: included (archiving is visibility, not invalidity). Incomplete members: included, reflect current coverage live.
  - Compare matches trials by exact sampled-parameter signature only. No nearest-neighbor matching, no imputation, no outlier suppression (known upstream data errors like rmse≈1.7e11 stay visible). No global overlap → say so; never manufacture a ranking.
- Investigation index shows: name, factor, outcome, member count, coverage summary (with outcome / incomplete / invalid), last activity, and a project-scope Unorganized count/list (sweeps in no Investigation).
- Create vs edit are distinct flows; a draft (unsaved or newly created) never overwrites an existing Investigation. Deterministic preview of candidate factors/outcomes with real coverage counts runs before save.
- Tables: sortable by every column, typed sort keys (numeric, ns timestamps, strings; empties last), sort survives re-renders and pagination (sorts the underlying row set, not the page).
- Artifacts: per-trial context only (trial expansion / inspector, linking to the existing dashboard artifact viewer). No Investigation-scope artifact surface in this epic (deferred).
- Series at Investigation scope: trajectory semantics unchanged (per-metric visibility, median+IQR band vs raw, shared focus). Focus is highlight-only and labeled as such.
- Points at Investigation scope: trials × final scalars + params→outcome parallel coordinates. On selection, table hides non-selected rows ("X of Y trials shown"); the parcoords keeps native brush semantics — all lines stay plotted as faded context, only line colors change, axes never rescale.

## 3. Storage (jernerics-server)

- `SCHEMA_VERSION` 8 → 9. New tables only; no backfill:
  - `investigations (investigation_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, project TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, factor TEXT NOT NULL, outcome TEXT NOT NULL, replicate_factor TEXT NULL, archived_ns INTEGER NULL, created_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, UNIQUE(project, name))` STRICT.
  - `investigation_sweeps (investigation_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES investigations(investigation_id), sweep_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sweeps(sweep_id), added_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(investigation_id, sweep_id))` STRICT.
- Store methods: list by project (excl/arch incl), get by id and by (project, name), create, replace-member-set / add / remove members, archive / restore, touch updated_ns on every mutation. All idempotent.
- Cross-project / unknown sweep_id member references are rejected at write time (the only hard failures).

## 4. HTTP API (authenticated, same bearer auth as /query)

- `GET /investigations?project=` list; `GET /investigations/{id}` one (with member coverage facts).
- `POST /investigations` create (idempotency: same (project,name) with matching body is a no-op returning the existing record; conflicting body is 409).
- `PUT /investigations/{id}/members` set membership (idempotent); `POST .../members/add`, `.../members/remove` for incremental.
- `POST /investigations/{id}/archive`, `POST .../restore` (idempotent).
- `POST /investigations/preview` — deterministic, side-effect-free: given project + candidate member ids, return candidate factors and outcomes each with real coverage counts (members with ≥1 completed trial carrying the outcome / a factor value), plus warnings (revision/config divergence, missing refs). Factor candidates derive from real data only: categorical manual params, config-source identity, sweep-name tokens — enumerated in the preview task, prototype is reference.
- Typed pydantic request/response models in jernerics-server; JSON only. Dashboard buttons call the same service layer as these routes (no private dashboard-only write path).

## 5. Client + CLI (human/agent parity)

- `TrackingClient` / `ProjectHandle`: investigations list/get/preview/create/members/archive/restore. Mutations idempotent (safe to retry).
- CLI: `jernerics investigation list|show|preview|create|members add|members remove|members set|archive|restore` with `--json` everywhere; `show` prints the materialized Selection. Agents use the same operations: stable ids, JSON, deterministic previews, no HTML scraping.
- `Open in Python` (dashboard action) exports the exact effective membership as an encoded Selection token for the existing Selection contract (`Selection(project=..., sweeps=(...))`).

## 6. Dashboard implementation notes

- Reuse the existing multi-sweep scope machinery: `analysis.py` `EMPTY_TRAY` / `default_scope_state()` / `tray_from_selection()` / URL hydration already model Selection scope — an Investigation materializes to a normal Selection; Series/Points components then operate unchanged over it.
- Navigation change lives in `workspace.py` (tab assembly); Investigations index + workspace are new surfaces; Compare is new; member editor is new; Search is member-filter minimal.
- Member scope across views = URL-carried state (existing pattern), not a second selection system. `Selection.sweeps` tuple is the only membership representation handed to analyses.

## 7. Explicit non-goals (do not build)

- Dynamic saved-query membership (queries silently change analyses; explicit sets only).
- Mandatory submission association (`jernerics run --investigation` convenience is a possible later addition, only after post-hoc workflow proves out).
- Continuation / Optuna journal reuse / seeding; sweep lineage, fork/ancestry graphs; any lineage-derived "journal".
- Research-journal metadata (hypothesis, role, lifecycle fields).
- Cross-project Investigations.
- Artifact surfaces at Investigation scope.
- Nearest-neighbor or fuzzy parameter matching.

## 8. Deferred to real usage — decided defaults (implement the default; revisit later)

- Investigation default tab name: **Compare** (not Overview — avoids collision with project/sweep Overview semantics).
- Draft factor summaries: derived from the actual member set via the preview contract (never baked constants — prototype's baked summary was a known rough edge).
- Series band pooling across problems: keep pooled median+IQR over analyzable trials with per-problem colored raw traces.
- Artifact placement at Investigation scope: none in v1; per-trial inspector remains the surface.

## 9. Verification bar

- Unit: schema records, store CRUD + migration, API routes (auth, idempotency, 409s, preview determinism), client, CLI.
- E2E (`tests/e2e/`): full journey — create → preview → add members → compare → scoped series/points → sweep return path → python export; plus an agent journey via the typed client only.
- Browser-driven verification of the real dashboard for every surface changed (per repo verification norms), including: scope survives repeated tab switches; brush keeps native parcoords semantics; table hides non-selected; invalid-excluded default with honest empty state; sortable tables across pagination.

title: log_metric as documented alias for log_value
description:
## Problem
Trial code naturally uses `tracker.log_metric()` while the public protocol exposes only log_value/log_param/log_artifact/finish. The mismatch currently surfaces late in container/HPC runs as AttributeError and test_trial_context.py pins the absence of the alias.

## Proposed Change
Add `log_metric` as the documented alias for `log_value` across TrackerProtocol, ConsoleTracker, and _JobTracker. Update the public-surface test and trial-authoring documentation in the same clean cutover.

## Acceptance Criteria
`log_metric(key, value, step=...)` produces the same console/event behavior as `log_value` in every tracker implementation; protocol typing exposes it; existing log_value behavior is unchanged; documentation uses one canonical explanation of the alias.
close_reason: Completed: log_metric alias added to TrackerProtocol, ConsoleTracker, and _JobTracker in trial_context.py, mirroring log_value's signature and delegating to it (preserves execution-ID stamping); internal tracking/tracker.py untouched; repo had zero log_metric callers (beads df6/e0e are the consumer records). Focused: 29 passed (3 new); full gate: 1362 passed, 6 skipped.

comments.author: jerry
comments.text: 2026-08-22 validity sweep: still actionable; one stale detail. test_trial_context.py does not currently pin log_metric absence. Keep the alias only on the trial-facing TrackerProtocol, ConsoleTracker, and _JobTracker in trial_context.py; delegate to self.log_value so JsonlTracker retains execution_id stamping from 09d89c6. Do not expand the backend tracker protocol.

title: Make large tracker results durable with a coherent artifact API
description:
REPRO (jernerics 1.1.2, slurm backend, pyrimel sweep):
  84/252 array tasks FAILED with exit 1 after 35-51 minutes each. Every restart had completed and every per-restart log_value had succeeded; the task died only at the final tracker.finish(results):

  pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ValueEvent
  observation
    Value error, observation encodes to 99717 bytes of JSON, exceeding the 65536-byte limit

  The payload was legitimate research output: 30 restarts x full pareto fronts (~3KB each). Nothing pathological - just a results blob over 64KiB.

WHY IT HURTS:
  - Worst-possible failure timing: all compute is done, then the trial is recorded as failed. No partial results event lands.
  - Retry system then re-runs the identical deterministic trial, burning another full compute cycle to die at the same line.

PROPOSED FIX:
  1. Raise the ValueEvent observation cap to something like 10MiB - still guards unbounded garbage, clears any realistic results blob.
  2. Consider validating the results size BEFORE the run starts (or at first log of a large json), not only at finish.
  3. Error message should suggest the remedy (artifact via log_artifact for bulky payloads).

CONTEXT: pyrimel worked around this in 296281e by slimming the event and using log_artifact for the full blob, so this is hardening, not blocking.
close_reason: Reworked per decision comments 45-48: data= union removed everywhere (tracker, protocol, NullTracker, trial_context); log_artifact(key, local_path) is path-only again; open_artifact(key, mode) context manager added — wt utf-8 text writer / wb binary writer, spool blobs/<id>.part, clean exit = close -> hash (1 MiB chunks) -> os.replace -> declaration -> manifest staged=True, exception = spool unlinked, no declaration; eager mode+manifest validation (blobs dir never created on bad input); filename defaults to key; oversize JSON error demonstrates the exact open_artifact call. Merged as 483e71a (agent commit 167219c independently re-verified: targeted suites 302 passed, full gates 1942 passed / 6 skipped), version bumped 1.2.1.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Triage: CONTEXT.md defines the 64 KiB JSON-observation bound as intentional and directs larger payloads to artifacts, so the proposed 10 MiB cap changes the canonical tracking contract. Before implementation, decide whether this bead is (a) a contract change, (b) an ergonomic fix that keeps the cap but gives an artifact remedy and prevents futile retry, or (c) automatic artifact promotion. The proposed pre-run validation cannot inspect results produced only at finish. The pyrimel artifact workaround means this is important hardening, not currently blocking.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Decision confirmed: retain the 64 KiB JSON-value contract and keep finish(results) for small objective payloads; large research output belongs in artifacts. Artifact ownership is snapshot semantics: when artifact logging returns, Jernerics owns immutable durable bytes independent of the caller. Path inputs are copied and hashed in one bounded-memory pass into cache_dir(), published atomically only after success, retained for replay, and deleted after upload acknowledgement. Do not switch silently to borrowed paths above a size threshold; a future zero-copy borrowed-path API must be explicit and earned by a concrete large-file workload. Remaining gate: select the call-site shape for supplying in-memory bytes/streams without inventing another semantic logging channel, and separate the post-hook's replacement of deterministic failed trials from this payload-contract issue.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Correction after review of 2dbe66d: snapshot storage is implemented correctly for existing path artifacts — 1 MiB streaming copy+hash into the tracking cache, atomic publish, replay from tracker-owned bytes, and post-ack cleanup. But the bead was closed without the agreed public-API decision. The implementation selected the unconfirmed tagged-union signature log_artifact(key, path=None, *, data: bytes=None), requiring exactly one source. This forces JSON callers to serialize fully to bytes, supplies no filename parameter for data (default is <key>.bin), and still makes one method secretly carry two source lifecycles. The 64 KiB error merely says 'via log_artifact' and cannot demonstrate the intended call. Reopened: preserve the snapshot implementation, but settle and implement the public artifact-input abstraction before closing. Do not revert the durable-copy behavior.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Terminology correction: both current inputs share snapshot ownership semantics. The unresolved problem is two distinct source forms hidden in one optional-argument signature, plus forced pre-serialization and missing data filename—not different durability lifecycles.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Decision confirmed: preserve one artifact semantic channel but expose its two honest source states explicitly.  captures an already-complete file as a tracker-owned immutable snapshot.  creates a tracker-owned writable artifact; it is a context manager for  or . Normal exit flushes/closes, hashes, atomically publishes, emits the declaration, and queues replay; exceptional exit removes the partial spool and emits no declaration. Both operations produce the same immutable, replayable artifact record. Remove the current  optional-union API; callers serialize JSON directly to the text writer or stream binary producers into the binary writer.  stays a small objective payload; large research output is explicitly written as an artifact.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
Supersedes malformed comment 47, caused by shell interpolation. Decision confirmed: preserve one artifact semantic channel but expose its two honest source states explicitly.

- `log_artifact(key, path)` captures an already-complete file as a tracker-owned immutable snapshot.
- `open_artifact(key, filename, *, mode, content_type=None)` creates a tracker-owned writable artifact; it is a context manager for `mode="w"` or `mode="wb"`.
- Normal exit flushes/closes, hashes, atomically publishes, emits the declaration, and queues replay. Exceptional exit removes the partial spool and emits no declaration.
- Both operations produce the same immutable, replayable artifact record.
- Remove the current `data: bytes | None` optional-union API. JSON serializes directly to the text writer; binary producers stream into the binary writer.
- `finish(results)` stays a small objective payload; large research output is explicitly written as an artifact.

title: slurm build jobs cannot exclude nodes; broken-but-idle nodes wedge container rebuilds
description:
## Problem

`SlurmAdapter.submit_job` — used for `container-build` jobs — hardcodes exactly
four sbatch directives (`partition`, `time`, `mem`, `cpus-per-task`). There is
no way to express node-selection constraints on build jobs, while the trial
sweep path supports the full `SBATCH_OVERRIDE_KEYS` whitelist (including
`exclude` and `nodes`) via per-config overrides.

Consequence: one broken-but-IDLE compute node wedges all container rebuilds
with no in-library remedy.

Incident (2026-08-27, symlab on hpc2): node `cn649` reports IDLE to SLURM but
has no `/home` mount. Two consecutive
`jernerics backend build -b hpc --force` attempts (jobs 27859285, 27859309)
were scheduled there and died in 0s:

```
error: couldn't chdir to `/home/jez21005': No such file or directory
slurm_script: line 13: cd: /home/jez21005/projects/symlab-overfit: No such file or directory
```

The scheduler re-picks the node (lowest-priority idle choice), so retrying
does not help. Hand-submitting an equivalent sbatch with `--exclude=cn649`
was rejected as a workaround: it forks the build-script generation logic out
of the library and bypasses job-meta bookkeeping.

## Reproduce

1. Have a node in the build partition that SLURM considers IDLE but which
   lacks the home mount (or block the home path).
2. `jernerics backend build -b <slurm-backend> --force` repeatedly until the
   scheduler picks it; the build fails before the script body runs and will
   keep failing on retries.
3. No config key or flag exists to avoid the node for builds.

## Proposed

Add `exclude` to `SlurmConfig` (`[tool.jernerics.backends.<name>.slurm]
exclude = "..."`), thread it through `SlurmAdapter.from_config` into
`submit_job`, and emit `#SBATCH --exclude=...` when set. Build jobs then get
the same node-avoidance capability the trial path already has.

Residual (out of library scope): the root cause on the cluster — `cn649`
IDLE with no `/home` — needs an admin report/drain; the config key is the
client-side defense.
close_reason: Fixed by c022172 (2026-08-27, same day as the incident): backend-config exclude is plumbed config.py:89/253 -> SlurmAdapter -> submit_job renders #SBATCH --exclude (slurm/adapter.py:417-421), with unit tests (test_exclude_emits_sbatch_directive, test_no_exclude_directive_by_default). Sweep-path whitelist claim also verified (adapter.py:15-28).

comments.author: jerry
comments.text:
Fix implemented in c022172 (local, main): `SlurmConfig.exclude` threaded from `[tool.jernerics.backends.<name>.slurm] exclude` through `SlurmAdapter.from_config` into `submit_job`, emitting `#SBATCH --exclude=...`. Per-token validation (shared validator charset rejects commas; each hostlist token validated individually, so injection surface unchanged). 2 new unit tests; full unit suite 926 passed.
