title: Iterate dashboard curation and series exploration
description:
## Goal

Remove two dogfooded dashboard blockers: historical/failed/invalid sweeps permanently clutter the project, and series analysis cannot inspect several tracked value keys together. Keep iteration fast and removal cheap while preserving tracking facts and explicit scientific semantics.

## Locked product decisions

### Sweep curation
- Add two distinct server-persisted states: archived (organizational visibility) and invalid (scientific interpretation with a required short reason).
- Marking a sweep invalid also archives it. Restoring validity clears invalid status/reason but leaves the sweep archived until separately restored. An invalid sweep cannot be restored to Current before validity is restored.
- Curation never deletes or rewrites sweep/trial/execution/value/artifact facts and never cancels scheduler work.
- Incomplete work remains visible in Current even when archived/invalid, so dashboard curation cannot hide running resources. Once terminal, archived/invalid work leaves Current.
- Current/Archived/All workspace filters are explicit. Project health and recent-sweep summaries default to Current semantics. Direct links always resolve and show curation banners.
- Analysis excludes archived/invalid sweeps from ordinary discovery by default, but explicit URL-restored selections remain intact and render warnings instead of silently dropping data.
- Persist curation in the tracking server SQLite database. The authenticated Dash callback surface may write only this narrow curation metadata; machine domain reads, tracking events, artifacts, and scheduler state remain unchanged. No browser-local-only source of truth.

### Series exploration
- A sweep detail page has a direct Analyze series entry that opens Analysis already scoped to that sweep.
- Analysis scope is visible/editable above every analysis view instead of living in a setup-only tab. The header tray becomes inspectable rather than a text-only count.
- Analysis URL state reproduces active view, selected metric keys, display mode, context choices, reductions, highlights, and per-metric axes in addition to the existing typed Selection token. No server-saved layouts.
- Series accepts multiple scalar value keys. Default rendering is vertically stacked metric panels with a shared step axis, independent y axes, stable trial/family identity across panels, and no interpolation or implicit latest-value choice.
- Overlay is explicit and uses one shared axis. It never normalizes automatically. Per-metric stacked-panel axis settings survive switching modes.
- Each stacked panel supports linear/log y scale and Auto/Custom finite bounds. Log is not applied when selected observations contain non-positive values; the panel explains why and remains linear. Invalid bounds leave the prior valid state. Manual clipping reports how many points lie outside the visible range.
- Large selections never silently sample or reduce. Raw, highlighted-only, and median-plus-IQR are explicit display modes. Execution reduction remains the existing explicit none/mean/min/max control and is distinct from cross-trial summary.
- Context filters, linked chart/family highlighting, manual refresh, and optional auto-refresh while selected work is incomplete complete the dense-sweep workflow. Refresh preserves zoom and controls.

## Iteration policy

Implement plain vertical slices. Dogfood each surface and delete controls that prove useless or harmful; do not preserve them behind compatibility aliases. Durable curation semantics remain explicit even if presentation changes.

## Non-goals

Permanent deletion, scheduler cancellation, arbitrary tags/folders, annotations, free-form or saved dashboard layouts, automatic metric-name semantics, automatic normalization, multi-user curation permissions, cross-project analysis, renderer/plugin frameworks, or backward-compatibility shims.

## Implementation tracks

1. Curation persistence and aggregate-query semantics.
2. Curation workspace/detail/analysis UI.
3. Analysis scope and URL view state with direct sweep entry.
4. Multi-metric stacked/overlay series with per-panel scales.
5. Dense-sweep summaries, context filtering, linked highlighting, and refresh.
6. End-to-end browser verification and documentation.

Tracks 1 and 3 are independent foundations. Track 2 depends on both 1 and 3. Track 4 depends on 3. Track 5 depends on 4. Final integration depends on tracks 2 and 5.

## Completion

Every child issue is complete; migrations preserve existing v6 tracking data; authenticated curation, Current/Archived/All semantics, invalid selection warnings, direct sweep-to-Series navigation, URL reload, multiple metrics, independent scale/range controls, explicit large-sweep modes, and refresh are browser-verified against a seeded mounted server. `just lint`, `just format-check`, `just typecheck`, and `just test` pass, relevant docs no longer describe the dashboard as wholly read-only, and all changes are staged.

Final state: just lint/format-check/typecheck/test all exit 0 (1634 passed), mounted-browser integration observed end-to-end, docs updated to the curation-only write boundary.

title: Persist sweep curation and current-view query semantics
description:
## Goal

Add the durable, narrowly writable curation model that lets dashboard reads distinguish current, archived, and scientifically invalid sweeps without changing canonical tracking facts.

## Files and symbols

Modify:
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/store.py`: `SCHEMA_VERSION`, migrations, `Store`, module-level curation exceptions.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/queries.py`: `QueryService.project_catalog`, `QueryService.sweep_overview`.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/service.py`: `ProjectSummary`, `SweepSummary`, aggregate mapping/properties.
- `packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_store.py`.
- `packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_views.py`.

Do not add public jernerics-schema records or new machine HTTP endpoints. Curation is dashboard-owned metadata, not part of the tracking event wire contract.

## Locked data model

Migrate schema v6 to v7 non-destructively. Add STRICT table `sweep_curation` keyed by `sweep_id` with a foreign key to `sweeps` and nullable `archived_ns`, nullable `invalid_ns`, nullable `invalid_reason`, and non-null `updated_ns`.

Constraints:
- Invalid status requires non-empty trimmed reason of at most 500 characters, `invalid_ns`, and `archived_ns`.
- A valid sweep has both `invalid_ns` and `invalid_reason` null.
- No curation row means valid and unarchived.
- No tracking table is rewritten by a curation operation.

Add explicit Store mutations under the existing writer lock/transaction discipline:
- archive a sweep;
- restore an archived sweep, rejected while it remains invalid;
- mark invalid with a required reason, also setting archived when absent;
- restore validity by clearing invalid fields while leaving archived unchanged.

Missing sweep ids and invalid transitions fail with descriptive module-level custom exceptions. Mutations are safe to retry; no duplicate rows. Do not add aliases or generic metadata APIs.

## Locked read semantics

Extend dashboard aggregate rows with archived/invalid facts and counts.

`SweepSummary.current` is true when the sweep is incomplete, regardless of curation, or when it is terminal and neither archived nor invalid. Thus curation cannot hide running/waiting/open-execution work; archived/invalid work leaves Current only after becoming terminal.

`project_catalog` health counts, recent sweep, and last activity use Current semantics. Projects remain listed even when every sweep is archived. Project rows also expose archived and invalid sweep counts so hidden history is discoverable.

`sweep_overview` still returns all matching sweeps and includes curation columns; presentation filters in the next issue. Explicit sweep-id reads always return archived/invalid sweeps.

## Acceptance

- Opening an existing schema-v6 database migrates to v7 without losing any tracking row.
- Archive/restore and invalid/restore-validity transitions obey the locked state machine and persist across Store reopen.
- Invalid reasons reject blank/whitespace-only and over-500-character values.
- Incomplete archived/invalid sweeps remain Current; terminal ones do not.
- Project health/recent activity exclude terminal archived/invalid sweeps and report archived/invalid counts.
- Explicit overview reads still return curated sweeps with their metadata.
- `pytest packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_store.py packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_views.py` passes.
- `just lint`, `just format-check`, and `just typecheck` pass for the changed files.

No file-level docstrings added, no multi-line mechanism comments, no backward compatibility shim beyond the required v6-to-v7 migration.

Verified: 118 target + 396 full server tests pass (orchestrator-run), ruff clean; format-check/typecheck failures confirmed pre-existing on pristine c022172 (packages/jernerics slurm adapter, untouched).

title: Add sweep archive and invalid dashboard workflows
description:
## Goal

Expose the curation model as a small authenticated dashboard write surface and make curated scope explicit in Analysis, while keeping tracking facts, machine APIs, artifacts, and scheduler operations read-only.

## Dependencies

Requires:
- `jernerics-cdf.1` for the v7 curation model and aggregate fields.
- `jernerics-cdf.3` for the persistent Analysis scope editor and v1 dashboard view state.

## Files and symbols

Modify:
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/app.py`: inject `Store` into the dashboard service.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/service.py`: curation mutation methods, display filtering, curated-selection facts; no SQL.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/layout.py`: project counts, workspace controls/actions, sweep-detail banners/actions.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/analysis.py`: Include archived/invalid scope controls and curated-scope warnings.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/callbacks.py`: workspace state, selection actions, curation mutations, analysis discovery/warnings, visible errors.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/assets/dashboard.css`.
- `packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_views.py`.
- `packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_analysis.py`.
- `packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard.py` only if callback/session coverage requires it.

Do not add a public curation endpoint. Dash callbacks are already protected by dashboard session middleware and call DashboardService in-process. DashboardService delegates mutations to explicit Store methods; it contains no SQL.

## Workspace UX

- Add Current / Archived / All controls with counts. Default is Current.
- Current shows every incomplete sweep plus terminal valid/unarchived sweeps. Archived shows terminal archived sweeps, including invalid sweeps. All shows all sweeps.
- Add a quick search and selected-row action bar: Analyze, Archive, Mark invalid, Restore validity, Restore.
- Mark invalid requires a trimmed reason before dispatch. Archive and invalid actions support multi-selection. Mixed selections expose only valid transitions; restoring validity never implicitly restores archive visibility.
- Running/incomplete curated rows remain visible in Current with a message that curation does not cancel or hide active work.
- Invalid rows and archived rows have distinct badges. Curation state never replaces tracked sweep state.
- Persist Current/Archived/All choice, quick filter, column filters, and sort order per project in session storage so detail-page navigation does not reset review work.

## Detail and project UX

- Sweep detail always resolves. Archived and invalid banners name the state; invalid includes reason and timestamp.
- Detail actions obey the same transition rules as workspace actions.
- Project rows show Current health plus separate archived and invalid sweep counts. Failed terminal curated work no longer keeps Current health red.
- Every mutation reports success/failure visibly and refreshes the affected grid/detail without a full browser reload.

## Analysis UX

- Ordinary sweep discovery in the persistent scope editor excludes terminal archived/invalid sweeps by default.
- Add explicit Include archived and Include invalid controls to v1 dashboard view state. They reveal curated sweeps for selection; they do not mutate the typed Selection token.
- A curated sweep already present through `sel`, workspace selection, or direct Analyze series is never silently removed even when include controls are off. The scope bar and all analysis views show archived/invalid badges; invalid includes reason and a clear warning that its data is marked scientifically invalid.
- The user may explicitly continue with or remove curated scope. Data queries honor the explicit Selection exactly.
- Direct Analyze series works for current, archived, and invalid sweeps and arrives with the right warning.

## Safety invariants

- No delete or scheduler cancel control.
- Archive never implies work cancellation.
- No trial/execution/value/artifact mutation.
- Missing sweep or invalid-transition errors render on page; callbacks do not swallow them.
- Direct links and selection URLs to curated objects continue to resolve.

## Acceptance

- Authenticated callbacks archive, mark invalid with reason, restore validity, and restore archive; unauthorized access remains blocked by existing middleware.
- Current/Archived/All and project health semantics match `jernerics-cdf.1`, including incomplete curated sweeps remaining visible.
- Invalid and archived states are distinct in workspace, detail, and Analysis.
- Analysis discovery defaults exclude curated terminal sweeps, explicit include controls reveal them, and explicitly selected curated scopes survive with warnings.
- View/filter/sort state survives workspace → detail → workspace navigation in the same session.
- Multi-row actions are deterministic and expose partial failures rather than claiming all succeeded.
- `pytest packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_views.py packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_analysis.py packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard.py` passes.
- Browser-drive every transition, curated selection URL restoration, default/include discovery, and direct Analyze series against the mounted seeded dashboard; record observed states in the close reason.

No new UI framework, generalized action system, compatibility alias, or file-level docstring.
close_reason: Implemented in 3d3ff04 (merged to main): DashboardService curation mutations delegating to Store (no SQL) + app.py store injection; Current/Archived/All workspace views with counts, quick search, mixed-selection action bar, session-persisted filter/sort/view per project; detail banners + same-transition actions; Analysis include_archived/include_invalid discovery controls, scope-bar badges/warnings, curated sel= survival. Verified by orchestrator: 495 server tests pass, lint clean, typecheck only the pre-existing slurm diagnostic. Agent browser-drove archive/restore/invalid/restore-validity, partial multi-failure messages, incomplete-curated Current note, include-controls discovery, curated URL restoration, Analyze-series-on-invalid on seeded 8792.

title: Make analysis scope direct, persistent, and URL-driven
description:
## Goal

Remove the setup-screen navigation tax: make scope visible/editable on every Analysis view, add direct sweep-to-Series entry, and make browser reload/back/share reproduce the actual analysis view rather than only its Selection.

## Files and symbols

Modify:
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/layout.py`: shell state and direct Analyze series link on sweep detail.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/analysis.py`: scope bar/editor, view-state codec/validation/defaults, URL synchronization helpers.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/callbacks.py`: hydrate/synchronize scope and view state without callback loops.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/assets/dashboard.css`.
- `packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_analysis.py`.
- `packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_views.py`.

Do not change the shared Selection token contract or duplicate its codec. `?sel=` remains the interoperable Python/dashboard scope token.

## Locked interaction

- Remove Selection as a setup-only tab. Render a persistent scope bar above Data catalog, Series, Points, Optuna views, and Continue in Python.
- The bar shows selected sweeps and family/execution counts. An Edit scope disclosure mounts the existing sweep/family grids and retry expansion control without navigating away from the active analysis view.
- The header selection tray becomes clickable and opens Analysis with the current scope instead of remaining count-only text.
- Sweep detail adds Analyze series, producing a Selection scoped to that sweep and opening Analysis with Series active. It must not require first selecting a workspace checkbox.
- Existing workspace selection and cross-sweep/family editing continue to feed one unified selection store.

## URL view state contract

Keep `sel=<existing-token>` and add one dashboard-only `view=<percent-encoded compact JSON>` query parameter. Version it as `v: 1`; do not add a second base64 token or server-saved layout.

The v1 shape carries:
- active analysis view;
- `series.keys` as an ordered list (the current single-key UI may use its first entry until the dependent series issue lands);
- series mode, execution reduction, trial display, context filters, color, facet, per-key axis map, highlighted families, and auto-refresh flag;
- Optuna contour selections.

Validate enums and JSON types. Unknown fields are ignored when reading and not re-emitted. A malformed/unsupported view shows a visible error, preserves a valid `sel`, and uses defaults. A malformed `sel` retains the existing visible selection error behavior. State edits use browser history coherently: back/forward restore scope and controls without callback loops.

Only URL-restorable user intent belongs in the view parameter; transient hover, open menus, and Plotly internal objects do not.

## Downstream contract

The multi-metric issue consumes `series.keys` and the per-key axis map directly; do not introduce a singular compatibility alias. The curation UI consumes the persistent scope editor to expose Include archived/invalid and warnings after its persistence dependency exists.

## Acceptance

- Sweep detail → Analyze series opens Series with exactly that sweep selected.
- Scope stays visible while switching analysis views and can be edited in place.
- Reload and browser back/forward restore active view, selection, and every existing analysis control represented in v1.
- Shared URLs continue to decode `sel` with the existing Python-compatible codec.
- Malformed view state fails visibly without discarding a valid selection.
- Header tray opens the current Analysis scope.
- `pytest packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_analysis.py packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_views.py` passes.
- Browser-drive direct entry, scope editing, reload, and back/forward against the mounted seeded dashboard.

No saved layouts, local-storage-only source of truth, compatibility alias, new public API, or file-level docstring.

title: Build multi-metric series panels with independent scales
description:
## Goal

Replace the one-key Series overlay with a multi-metric explorer that can inspect several scalar step series from the same or multiple sweeps without conflating their y scales.

## Dependency

Requires the v1 Analysis view/scope URL state from `jernerics-cdf.3`. Cleanly consume `series.keys` and per-key axes; do not keep or add a singular-key alias.

## Files and symbols

Modify:
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/queries.py`: add one framework-neutral aggregate query only if needed for family-aware key coverage; do not put SQL in dashboard modules.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/service.py`: `analysis_value_keys`, replace one-key `analysis_series` with ordered multi-key output using one paginated values read.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/analysis.py`: Series controls and panel construction.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/figures.py`: stacked-panel and explicit overlay figure builders.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/callbacks.py`: multi-key and pattern-matching per-panel axis callbacks.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/assets/dashboard.css`.
- `packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_analysis.py`.

## Metric selection and data contract

- Metric picker is ordered, searchable, and multi-select. Offer scalar keys with real step series; JSON/non-step values remain in their existing views.
- Options show key, kind, point count, selected-trial or retry-family coverage, and step extent. Do not guess semantics from key names.
- Fetch selected keys in one paginated values pass. Output retains key, trial id, execution id, step, numeric value, and flat context. Missing keys remain missing; never interpolate, forward-fill, select an implicit latest value, or invent zero.
- Existing explicit execution reduction none/mean/min/max applies independently per key and trial at each step.

## Stacked mode

- Default mode renders one vertically stacked Plotly panel per selected key, in picker order.
- Panels share the step x domain/zoom and aligned hover position but have independent y axes.
- A trial/family identity has a stable color across every panel; execution/retry distinctions remain visible through label and line style/opacity.
- Empty/missing metric panels explain coverage instead of disappearing.

## Per-panel y-axis controls

Each stacked panel has visible compact controls:
- scale: Linear or Log;
- range: Auto or Custom finite min/max;
- Reset.

Rules:
- Default is Linear + Auto.
- Custom min must be less than max. Log custom bounds must be positive.
- When any selected observation for a key is non-positive, choosing Log does not apply it: keep the last valid linear state and show the non-positive count/reason. Never silently drop those points.
- Manual clipping shows the count of observations outside the visible range in the panel header.
- Axis state is keyed by metric in the v1 view URL and survives reorder, mode switches, reload, and share.

## Overlay mode

- Overlay is explicit and uses one shared y axis/scale for all selected keys.
- Never normalize automatically and do not create automatic dual axes.
- Switching to Overlay does not destroy dormant per-key stacked settings; returning to Stacked restores them.

## Acceptance

- Selecting three heterogeneous scalar keys renders three ordered aligned panels from one data read with independent ranges/scales.
- Trial/family colors remain consistent across panels and missing coverage is visible.
- Linear/log validation, bounds validation, Reset, clipping count, and non-positive warning behave exactly as specified.
- URL reload reproduces selected keys, order, mode, and every per-key axis setting.
- Overlay is opt-in, shared-axis, and unnormalized.
- Existing one-key URLs are not supported through a deprecated alias; this is a clean pre-release cutover to `series.keys`.
- `pytest packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_analysis.py` passes.
- Browser-drive key add/remove/reorder, stacked/overlay switching, log rejection, custom range, reload, and linked zoom against seeded heterogeneous data.

No pandas/numpy dependency, unit schema, auto-normalization, dual-axis heuristics, saved layout, compatibility shim, or file-level docstring.

Verified by orchestrator: 542 combined server tests pass after rebase, lint clean, typecheck only pre-existing slurm diagnostic, codec round-trip re-verified by orchestrator script. title: Add explicit dense-sweep comparison and live refresh
description:
## Goal

Make the multi-metric explorer usable for real sweeps with many trial/execution lines, heterogeneous contexts, and live values without silently sampling or reducing data.

## Dependency

Requires the multi-metric panels from `jernerics-cdf.4`.

## Files and symbols

Modify:
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/service.py`: explicit cross-trial summary and context filtering inputs.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/analysis.py`: family table, display-mode controls, context filters, refresh status.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/figures.py`: highlighted and median/IQR marks with stable identities and `uirevision`.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/callbacks.py`: chart/table linking and refresh triggers.
- `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/assets/dashboard.css`.
- `packages/jernerics-server/tests/test_dashboard_analysis.py`.

Do not change tracking/event schemas or add a background service.

## Explicit trial display modes

- All raw: render every series after the selected execution reduction. Always show the raw series count. Above 100 series show a line-density/performance warning, but do not sample or switch modes automatically.
- Highlighted only: render only families/trials selected in the linked table; with no highlight, show an instruction rather than silently reverting to All.
- Median + IQR: at each observed step and explicit context/color group, aggregate the currently selected trial series after execution reduction. Plot median and a 25th–75th percentile band and show contributing series count. Missing steps remain missing; no interpolation. Implement deterministic percentile math with stdlib code and boundary tests, not numpy/pandas.

Execution reduction (none/mean/min/max within a trial) remains a separate control from cross-trial display mode. Labels state both choices.

## Context workflow

- Discover dimension values under the current scope.
- Add explicit multi-value filters per selected flat context dimension; filters apply before raw/highlight/summary rendering.
- Preserve global color and facet choices. A metric panel may contain context facets, but metric keys remain separate stacked panels.
- Context filters, color, facet, display mode, and highlights round-trip through the existing v1 view URL.

## Linked family interaction

- Add a compact family/trial table beside or immediately above the panels, showing number, short id, objective, state, and key sampled params available from existing data.
- Selecting rows highlights the same identity across all metric panels. Plot clicks/legend selection select or highlight the corresponding row when Plotly exposes the identity.
- Stable color assignment does not change when filtering or highlighting.

## Refresh

- Add Refresh and an `Updated … ago` fact.
- Add optional auto-refresh while the selected scope contains incomplete work, using the dashboard's existing five-second cadence. Auto-refresh stops when work is terminal.
- Refresh re-queries series/catalog/context data but preserves view controls, row highlights, linked x zoom, and valid manual y ranges through Plotly `uirevision` or equivalent stable state.
- Errors remain visible and do not clear the last successful controls.

## Acceptance

- Highlighted-only has no implicit fallback.

title: Workspace path dependencies break container builds
description:
## Problem

When a project uses local path dependencies (e.g., symlab depends on jernerics via `../jernerics/packages/jernerics`), container builds fail because the path dependency doesn't exist inside the container build context.

## Reproduction

```toml
# symlab/pyproject.toml
[tool.uv.sources]
jernerics = { path = "../jernerics/packages/jernerics", editable = true }
```

The container.def copies project files and runs `uv sync`, but `../jernerics/` doesn't exist in the container. The build fails.

## Current workaround

Create a separate pyproject.toml for the container that replaces path deps with git deps:
```toml
[tool.uv.sources]
jernerics = { git = "https://github.com/...", subdirectory = "packages/jernerics" }
```

## Proposed solution

Options:
1. jernerics automatically detects path deps and warns/instructs before container build
2. A `jernerics containerize` command that generates a container-appropriate pyproject.toml from the project's config
3. Document this as a known limitation in the deployment guide with the workaround pattern
4. Support a `.containerignore` or `.container-pyproject.toml` overlay that jernerics uses during build
close_reason: Detection + fail-fast implemented in commit 3fe1925. Overlay system deferred until push-to-test round-trip becomes a real pain point.

title: _JobTracker API mismatch between local and container jernerics versions
description:
## Problem
The local jernerics has `trial_tracker()` returning a tracker with `log_metric()` and `log_param()` methods. The container's jernerics (installed in /opt/venv) returns a `_JobTracker` that does NOT have these methods.

## Error
```
AttributeError: '_JobTracker' object has no attribute 'log_metric'
```

This causes every trial to fail with exit code 1, even when the actual cell execution succeeds and records are saved correctly.

## Impact
All HPC runs report as 'failed' even when they succeed. Records are saved before the tracker crash, but optuna marks trials as failed.

## Repro
Any `jernerics run` with a trial file that calls `tracker.log_metric()` or `tracker.log_param()`.

## Workaround
None — the tracker API needs to be consistent between local and container versions.
close_reason: Symlab-side bug: code called nonexistent log_metric; fixed by switching to log_value in commit pending symlab side. jernerics behaved correctly.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Root cause found — NOT a version mismatch. Local and container jernerics are identical (git-pinned, same lockfile). The real bug: symlab's trial scripts called tracker.log_metric(), a method that has never existed in jernerics' TrackerProtocol (the API is log_param/log_value/log_artifact/finish). Fixed symlab-side in trial.py, pysips_paper_trial.py, runner.py. No jernerics change needed. However, a DX improvement remains valid: _JobTracker could expose log_metric as an alias, or the protocol docs could make the API more discoverable.

title: Container build marker doesn't hash container.def — stale builds
description:
## Problem

The container build marker (`needs_rebuild` / `write_marker`) doesn't hash the `container.def` file content. If you modify the container definition, `jernerics run` doesn't detect the change and skips the rebuild. You have to manually pass `--force`.

## Reproduction

1. `jernerics run` — builds container, writes marker
2. Edit `container.def`
3. `jernerics run` again — says container is up to date, skips build

## Fix

Include a hash of `container.def` (and `pyproject.toml` / `pyproject.container.toml` if used) in the build marker. On subsequent runs, compare the hash to detect changes.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 8b436ab

title: Script-as-trial: replace trial function with plain Python script execution
description:
## Overview

Replace the `def trial(config, tracker)` function entry point with plain script execution. The same file runs standalone (prototyping) or via the runner (batch/SLURM) with zero modifications.

## API

```python
import jernerics

config = jernerics.trial_config(defaults={
    "lr": 3e-4, "n_steps": 100, "d_model": 128, ...
})

tracker = jernerics.trial_tracker()

model = build_model(config)
for step in range(config["n_steps"]):
    loss = train_step(model, config)
    tracker.log_value("loss", loss, step=step)

tracker.finish({"final_loss": loss})
```

Zero conditionals. Zero null checks. Works in both modes.

## Design

### trial_config(defaults: dict | None = None) -> dict
- **Job mode:** reads injected JSON from `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` env var
- **Standalone mode:** returns the `defaults` dict as-is
- Raises if job mode but env var not set
- Raises if standalone mode and no `defaults` provided

### trial_tracker() -> Tracker | ConsoleTracker
- **Job mode:** returns real `Tracker` (JSONL + server ship)
- **Standalone mode:** returns `ConsoleTracker` that prints to stdout
- Both implement same protocol: `log_param`, `log_value`, `finish`
- `ConsoleTracker.log_value` prints `[step N] key=value`
- `ConsoleTracker.finish` prints trial summary
- `ConsoleTracker.log_param` prints `param: key=value`

### is_job() -> bool
- Returns True if `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` env var is set (running as a scheduled job)
- Returns False when running standalone (python trial.py)
- Escape hatch for genuinely different behavior between modes

### tracker.finish(results: dict)
- **Tracker:** records results, picks up by runner as Optuna objective value
- **ConsoleTracker:** prints summary

## Runner changes

- `runner.py`: instead of `from trial import trial; trial(config, tracker)`, do:
  1. Write resolved config to temp JSON file
  2. Set `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` env var
  3. `subprocess.run(["python", trial_file])`
- Runner reads `tracker.finish()` results from the tracker output (or a known file)

## Breaking changes

- Drop `def trial(config, tracker)` entry point entirely (no backward compat)
- All symlab trial files need rewriting from function to script
- `load_config()` in config.py stays the same (still reads config.py files with base/grid/search_space)

## Trial protocol (type annotation)

```python
class TrackerProtocol(Protocol):
    def log_param(self, key: str, value: str) -> None: ...
    def log_value(self, key: str, value: float, step: int) -> None: ...
    def finish(self, results: dict[str, Any]) -> None: ...
```

## User Stories

1. **Prototype locally:** `python trial.py` runs with defaults config, prints metrics to console
2. **Submit to SLURM:** `jernerics run --backend hpc trial.py config.py` submits same file unchanged
3. **Grid sweep:** same file, runner materializes configs, each SLURM task gets its own env var
4. **Optuna search:** same file, runner asks study for suggestions, writes resolved config
5. **Marimo notebook as trial:** marimo .py files run via `python notebook.py` (marimo native script mode)
6. **Debug failed trial:** resolved configs written to cache for reproducibility
7. **Result feedback:** `tracker.finish()` → runner picks up → records in tracking / feeds Optuna objective

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `trial_config()`, `trial_tracker()`, `is_job()` implemented
- [ ] `ConsoleTracker` prints metrics to stdout
- [ ] Runner executes trial scripts via subprocess instead of function import
- [ ] All existing symlab trial files rewritten as scripts
- [ ] All jernerics tests pass
- [ ] `python trial.py` works standalone in symlab
- [ ] `jernerics run --backend hpc trial.py config.py` works end-to-end
close_reason: Split into three subtasks for incremental delivery

title: Keep tracking API keys out of generated commands
description:
## Problem
submission.py:202-206 reads JERNERICS_API_KEY, container.py:56-57/97-98 interpolates it into Apptainer/Docker argv, Slurm embeds that command in the job script, and backend.py:127-149 prints the full script for --dry-run. This leaks the bearer key to previews, scheduler/process inspection, and logs; unquoted values can also alter shell structure.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Export a distinctive JERNERICS_API_KEY value.
2. Render a Docker or Apptainer Slurm submission with `--dry-run`.
3. Observe the exact secret in the rendered container arguments and stdout.

## Proposed Change
provision the key through a mode-0600 remote env/secret file or scheduler-native channel, pass only a path/reference in argv, redact rendered previews, and preserve values byte-for-byte without shell interpolation.

## Acceptance Criteria
a sentinel key appears nowhere in rendered scripts, dry-run output, or container-engine argv, yet a submitted smoke job authenticates; keys containing spaces/metacharacters arrive unchanged.
close_reason: Completed: ContainerRuntime.wrap now takes env_file (Apptainer/Docker emit --env-file {path}); submit_sweep/Backend.sync provision JERNERICS_API_KEY via write_env_file() -> {cache}/tracking/env (write-tmp, chmod 600, atomic mv); dry-run renders the reference only. Shim e2e tests prove the sentinel (spaces/quotes/$/&) reaches the executed trial process byte-for-byte while absent from all rendered argv; independently reproduced leak-free render + shim e2e. Merged as 11cde6c; just check: 1289 passed, 6 skipped.

title: Restructure CLI and add safe interactive sync resolution
description:
Restructure the growing flat CLI into domain subcommands and add explicit, data-safe interactive sync inspection and conflict resolution.

Locked design:
- Keep root commands: init, local, run.
- Add groups: interactive start/stop/sync, job, backend, tracking.
- Clean cutover with no compatibility aliases.
- Split cli.py into a thin root plus jernerics.commands domain modules before changing behavior.
- Replace tracking sync + replay with tracking replay; no --backend uses local cache, --backend NAME replays from that backend.
- interactive sync status is report-only, supports JSON, and exits zero for successfully inspected missing/unhealthy states.
- Project-owned .jernericsignore uses Git-style patterns and applies with .gitignore plus shared defaults to deploy tar sync, interactive Mutagen, and one-shot fallback. Never silently restart sessions when ignore configuration changes.
- Resolver accepts explicit PATH... and --from local|cluster; no --all; regular files present on both endpoints only.
- Preview then confirm; --yes for noninteractive use and --dry-run for preview only.
- Back up every losing file locally under XDG_STATE_HOME (default ~/.local/state), with manifest and verified checksums, before any overwrite.
- Copy one path at a time via a checksum-verified destination temporary file and atomic replace. Stop on first failure, never auto-rollback, and report partial results.
- Recheck hashes for races, flush Mutagen, and require selected conflicts to disappear. Never restart or use one-shot deployment as resolution.
- Defer any TUI until observed operational pain requires persistent selection/live refresh; metric visualization remains dashboard territory.

All implementation follows repository Definition of Done and updates tests/docs for each changed public contract.

title: Split CLI into domain command modules
description:
Behavior-preserving source split.

Create packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/commands/{__init__,common,project,execution,interactive,backend,jobs,tracking}.py. Keep packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/cli.py as the thin Typer root, command registration, and main().

Ownership:

- project: init and scaffold helpers/constants.
- execution: local, run, relative-path validation, Git provenance.
- interactive: current interactive allocation and Mutagen orchestration.

title: Unify project source exclusion policy
description:
Create one project-source exclusion policy used by deployment tar sync, interactive Mutagen, and the one-shot interactive fallback.

Add optional project-root .jernericsignore with Git-style patterns for project-specific paths, including Git-tracked paths that must not synchronize. Do not hardcode .beads or other tool-specific exceptions. Combine pattern sources in this order: .gitignore, .jernericsignore, then a shared final built-in exclusion list so built-in safety/cache exclusions cannot be negated. Preserve Mutagen --ignore-vcs behavior. Reconcile the existing ProjectSync and INTERACTIVE_EXCLUDES lists into the shared defaults rather than maintaining two conventions.

ProjectSync and Mutagen creation must consume the same effective policy. .jernericsignore itself may synchronize. Mutagen locks ignores at session creation: changes apply only to the next intentionally created session. Never restart a live or conflicted session automatically to apply ignore changes.

Test files, directories, rooted patterns, negation behavior, tracked-path exclusions, missing ignore files, and equivalent application by tar collection and Mutagen argument construction. Document .jernericsignore and the next-session behavior.

title: Add interactive sync status command
description:
Add report-only `jernerics interactive sync status --backend NAME [--json]`.

Inspect the current project's named Mutagen session without creating, restarting, terminating, flushing, copying, or invoking one-shot fallback. Human output reports session name, raw Mutagen status, local/cluster endpoint connectivity, idle/converged state, conflict count, and conflicted relative paths. Use local/cluster vocabulary, not Mutagen alpha/beta, in the public output.

JSON contract includes project, backend, session, exists, status (nullable when missing), local_connected, cluster_connected, idle, converged, conflicts, and conflicted_paths. A successfully inspected missing, disconnected, syncing, or conflicted session exits zero; state is data. Exit nonzero only when configuration or Mutagen prevents inspection. Missing session returns exists=false, nullable endpoint/status fields, false idle/converged, zero conflicts, and an empty path list.

Reuse current SessionInfo/is_idle/is_converged/conflicted_paths logic and the existing warning policy. Do not alter normal interactive start conflict behavior.

Acceptance: human and JSON output cover healthy, conflicted, disconnected, syncing, and missing sessions; command is provably mutation-free; focused tests plus full Definition of Done pass; changed files staged.

title: Add safe interactive sync conflict resolver
description:
Add explicit conflict resolution:
`jernerics interactive sync resolve PATH... --backend NAME --from local|cluster [--dry-run] [--yes]`.

Scope and preflight:
- Require one or more explicit relative paths; no --all.
- One source applies to the invocation; mixed winners use separate invocations.
- Every selected path must be in the session's current Mutagen conflict list.
- Both endpoint entries must exist and be regular files. Refuse missing paths, directories, symlinks, type changes, unsafe traversal, or paths outside either project root.
- Never infer a winner from mtime or content.
- Preview every path, direction, size, endpoint checksum, and backup destination. Prompt once. --dry-run exits after validation/preview without backup or mutation. Noninteractive mutation requires --yes.

Backup and mutation:
- Store every losing copy locally under $XDG_STATE_HOME/jernerics/sync-backups/<project>/<UTC-unique-run>/, default ~/.local/state. Cluster losers download directly; create no persistent cluster backup.
- Write manifest.json with session, endpoints, source, selected paths, original and backup checksums, timestamps, and per-path results. Never auto-delete backups.
- Complete and checksum-verify all backups before the first overwrite. If local storage is insufficient or backup fails, mutate nothing.
- Re-hash source and destination immediately before each mutation; abort on changes.
- Process one path at a time. Transfer to a temporary sibling on the destination, verify checksum, atomically replace the loser, and remove temporary data. Peak destination temporary storage is one file; refuse before replacement if unavailable.
- On any copy/verification failure, stop immediately, never auto-rollback, and report completed, untouched, and unresolved paths plus the backup directory.
- Flush the existing Mutagen session, wait for idle, re-read conflicts, and require every selected path to disappear. Unselected conflicts may remain.
- Never restart/replace the Mutagen session and never invoke one-shot ProjectSync as resolution.

Verification must use isolated temporary Mutagen sessions/directories, not the live symlab session. Cover local winner, cluster winner, multiple explicit paths, mixed remaining conflicts, dry-run, refusal shapes, source/destination races, backup/download failure, temporary transfer failure, partial completion reporting, and conflict-clear verification.

Acceptance: focused unit and isolated end-to-end resolution scenarios pass, backup recovery evidence is verified, full Definition of Done passes, and changed files staged.
close_reason: Completed: jernerics interactive sync resolve PATH... --backend --from local|cluster [--dry-run] [--yes]; full safety contract implemented (explicit paths only, no --all, backups-first at XDG_STATE_HOME, checksum-verified atomic transfers, race re-hash, stop-without-rollback, flush+conflict-clear verification, no session restart/one-shot). Verified via 42 focused tests + orchestrator-run isolated Mutagen e2e (dry-run/refusal/local-wins/cluster-wins/mixed/no-yes/staging-cleanup); 761 full green. Fixed staging-residue deviation found during verification.

title: Define backend-neutral trial tracker primitives
description:
## Problem

Commit `af94fba` expanded `ConsoleTracker` to mirror `JsonlTracker` methods (`log_json`, `log_artifact`, `log_sweep_meta`) after standalone trial scripts crashed. Mirroring the backend surface is the wrong boundary: job mode exposes backend-only methods that standalone mode cannot reliably match.

## Locked design

The trial-facing protocol has four backend-neutral operations:

- `log_param(key, value)` for scalar experiment configuration.
- `log_value(key, value, *, step: int | None = None)` for any small JSON-compatible observation. `step` is special event metadata: an optional caller-supplied ordinal in a repeated measurement series, not specifically a deep-learning optimizer step.
- `log_artifact(key, path)` for externally materialized files requiring retention/transfer.
- `finish(results)` for terminal JSON-compatible results and lifecycle completion.

`log_text` and `log_json` are not separate trial primitives; strings and structured values use `log_value`. `log_sweep_meta`, `context`, `close`, context-manager methods, and writer details remain backend/runner internals.

Job and standalone modes must expose the same runtime surface. Implement the job tracker as a small adapter around `JsonlTracker`, not by inheriting and leaking its full method set. The adapter dispatches numeric observations to `JsonlTracker.log_value` and other JSON-compatible observations to `JsonlTracker.log_json`, preserving optional `step`.

## Changes

Jernerics:

- Revert commit `af94fba` with `git revert af94fba`.
- Update `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/trial_context.py` with the four-method protocol, JSON-compatible value typing, bounded `ConsoleTracker`, and composed job adapter.
- Update `packages/jernerics/tests/unit/test_trial_context.py` for standalone/job numeric and structured values, optional step, artifact events/manifests, finish behavior, and absence of backend-only methods.
- Leave the low-level `JsonlTracker` API intact unless a minimal annotation-only change is required.

Symlab:

- Change `experiments/overfit/trial.py` from `tracker.log_json("pred_expr", pred_expr, step=step)` to `tracker.log_value("pred_expr", pred_expr, step=step)`.
- Existing `log_artifact` calls remain valid.

## Acceptance

- `ConsoleTracker` and the job adapter support the same four public operations.
- Numeric and structured observations preserve their values and optional `step` in JSONL output.
- Artifact logging writes the event and job-mode manifest; standalone mode prints the key/path.
- Trial code cannot rely on `log_text`, `log_json`, or `log_sweep_meta` through the trial-facing object.
- Standalone and temporary job-mode smoke scenarios succeed.
- From `/home/jerry/Projects/jernerics`, `nix develop --command just check` passes without creating a `.venv`.
- The symlab migration receives a focused Nix-based syntax/lint check without creating a `.venv`.
- Commit history contains the explicit revert and a clear design-decision commit; the separate symlab repository receives its own migration commit.
close_reason: Completed in jernerics commits 00b031b and 5bb3153 plus symlab commit 22100ee. Verified nix develop --command just check (656 passed, 6 skipped), standalone/job smoke scenario, artifact manifest, and symlab Nix py_compile.

title: Investigations: cross-sweep organization for humans and agents (dashboard + CLI + API)
description:
# Investigations: cross-sweep organization for humans and agents

Status: DESIGN LOCKED. The information architecture and interaction model were validated in a real-data throwaway prototype (`/home/jerry/Projects/jernerics-proto`, pyrimel + symlab live tracking data, six build rounds + four user-driven correction rounds). This epic is the executable spec for production. Do not re-open settled questions here; "Deferred to real usage" items are decided with defaults and must not block implementation.

Research context: `agent://MLDashResearch`, `agent://OpsDashResearch`, `agent://UXResearch`, `agent://WebDesignResearch`. Canonical terms per CONTEXT.md: Sweep (never user-facing "study"), Trial, Selection.

## 1. Locked information architecture (validated)

- Project scope tabs: `Overview · Investigations · Exceptions`.
  - Catalog is merged into Overview's existing `Active / All` control; no separate global Catalog tab. Project pages show project-scoped counts only (the prototype's cross-project rollup table was a bug, not a feature).
  - Overview keeps: operational tiles (each tile filters, uniformly interactive — resolves jernerics-sdt6 and jernerics-1s6v), Active/All scope, paginated sortable sweep table with row selection.
  - Exceptions stays project-scoped failure triage; Investigations only surface member warnings, curation stays in Exceptions.
- Investigation views: `Compare · Series · Points · Search` plus actions `Open in Python` and `Edit members`. Python is never a global tab. Default tab is named **Compare** (decision; see deferred).
- Sweep hub views: `Overview · Series · Points · Search`, rendering only views the sweep's real data supports.
- Member scoping: opening an analysis view "from" one member carries that member scope across view switches; a visible `All members` control clears it; Compare never pretends a one-member scope is the full comparison (link visibly drops scope).
- Sweep opened from an Investigation: breadcrumb `pyrimel › Investigations › <name> › <sweep>` + explicit back link. Chart/table selection never mutates membership.

## 2. Investigation domain contract

- An Investigation is a saved analytical question over an explicit set of sweeps — not a folder, tag collection, journal, or lineage graph.
- Record fields: stable id, project, unique-per-project name, primary comparison factor, outcome key, optional replicate factor, archived flag, created/updated timestamps, explicit member sweep ids.
- Membership is many-to-many: a sweep may belong to several Investigations; membership implies no ancestry or inherited knowledge.
- Sweeps do NOT require an Investigation to run (no mandatory classification).
- Stored as server-owned organizational metadata — NOT immutable tracking events. Tracked facts (values, artifacts, scheduler state) stay immutable; Investigations + existing sweep curation are the only writes.
- Compatibility policy: hard-reject only cross-project / missing / malformed member references. Surface as visible warnings (never silent): missing outcome or factor values, differing git revisions or config sources, incomplete sweeps, sparse parameter overlap.
- Analysis semantics (validated on real data):
  - Invalid members: visible everywhere, excluded from numerical analysis by default, with an explicit include toggle and honest empty states stating how many data-bearing members are excluded.
  - Archived members: included (archiving is visibility, not invalidity). Incomplete members: included, reflect current coverage live.
  - Compare matches trials by exact sampled-parameter signature only. No nearest-neighbor matching, no imputation, no outlier suppression (known upstream data errors like rmse≈1.7e11 stay visible). No global overlap → say so; never manufacture a ranking.
- Investigation index shows: name, factor, outcome, member count, coverage summary (with outcome / incomplete / invalid), last activity, and a project-scope Unorganized count/list (sweeps in no Investigation).
- Create vs edit are distinct flows; a draft (unsaved or newly created) never overwrites an existing Investigation. Deterministic preview of candidate factors/outcomes with real coverage counts runs before save.
- Tables: sortable by every column, typed sort keys (numeric, ns timestamps, strings; empties last), sort survives re-renders and pagination (sorts the underlying row set, not the page).
- Artifacts: per-trial context only (trial expansion / inspector, linking to the existing dashboard artifact viewer). No Investigation-scope artifact surface in this epic (deferred).
- Series at Investigation scope: trajectory semantics unchanged (per-metric visibility, median+IQR band vs raw, shared focus). Focus is highlight-only and labeled as such.
- Points at Investigation scope: trials × final scalars + params→outcome parallel coordinates. On selection, table hides non-selected rows ("X of Y trials shown"); the parcoords keeps native brush semantics — all lines stay plotted as faded context, only line colors change, axes never rescale.

## 3. Storage (jernerics-server)

- `SCHEMA_VERSION` 8 → 9. New tables only; no backfill:
  - `investigations (investigation_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, project TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, factor TEXT NOT NULL, outcome TEXT NOT NULL, replicate_factor TEXT NULL, archived_ns INTEGER NULL, created_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, UNIQUE(project, name))` STRICT.
  - `investigation_sweeps (investigation_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES investigations(investigation_id), sweep_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sweeps(sweep_id), added_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(investigation_id, sweep_id))` STRICT.
- Store methods: list by project (excl/arch incl), get by id and by (project, name), create, replace-member-set / add / remove members, archive / restore, touch updated_ns on every mutation. All idempotent.
- Cross-project / unknown sweep_id member references are rejected at write time (the only hard failures).

## 4. HTTP API (authenticated, same bearer auth as /query)

- `GET /investigations?project=` list; `GET /investigations/{id}` one (with member coverage facts).
- `POST /investigations` create (idempotency: same (project,name) with matching body is a no-op returning the existing record; conflicting body is 409).
- `PUT /investigations/{id}/members` set membership (idempotent); `POST .../members/add`, `.../members/remove` for incremental.
- `POST /investigations/{id}/archive`, `POST .../restore` (idempotent).
- `POST /investigations/preview` — deterministic, side-effect-free: given project + candidate member ids, return candidate factors and outcomes each with real coverage counts (members with ≥1 completed trial carrying the outcome / a factor value), plus warnings (revision/config divergence, missing refs). Factor candidates derive from real data only: categorical manual params, config-source identity, sweep-name tokens — enumerated in the preview task, prototype is reference.
- Typed pydantic request/response models in jernerics-server; JSON only. Dashboard buttons call the same service layer as these routes (no private dashboard-only write path).

## 5. Client + CLI (human/agent parity)

- `TrackingClient` / `ProjectHandle`: investigations list/get/preview/create/members/archive/restore. Mutations idempotent (safe to retry).
- CLI: `jernerics investigation list|show|preview|create|members add|members remove|members set|archive|restore` with `--json` everywhere; `show` prints the materialized Selection. Agents use the same operations: stable ids, JSON, deterministic previews, no HTML scraping.
- `Open in Python` (dashboard action) exports the exact effective membership as an encoded Selection token for the existing Selection contract (`Selection(project=..., sweeps=(...))`).

## 6. Dashboard implementation notes

- Reuse the existing multi-sweep scope machinery: `analysis.py` `EMPTY_TRAY` / `default_scope_state()` / `tray_from_selection()` / URL hydration already model Selection scope — an Investigation materializes to a normal Selection; Series/Points components then operate unchanged over it.
- Navigation change lives in `workspace.py` (tab assembly); Investigations index + workspace are new surfaces; Compare is new; member editor is new; Search is member-filter minimal.
- Member scope across views = URL-carried state (existing pattern), not a second selection system. `Selection.sweeps` tuple is the only membership representation handed to analyses.

## 7. Explicit non-goals (do not build)

- Dynamic saved-query membership (queries silently change analyses; explicit sets only).
- Mandatory submission association (`jernerics run --investigation` convenience is a possible later addition, only after post-hoc workflow proves out).
- Continuation / Optuna journal reuse / seeding; sweep lineage, fork/ancestry graphs; any lineage-derived "journal".
- Research-journal metadata (hypothesis, role, lifecycle fields).
- Cross-project Investigations.
- Artifact surfaces at Investigation scope.
- Nearest-neighbor or fuzzy parameter matching.

## 8. Deferred to real usage — decided defaults (implement the default; revisit later)

- Investigation default tab name: **Compare** (not Overview — avoids collision with project/sweep Overview semantics).
- Draft factor summaries: derived from the actual member set via the preview contract (never baked constants — prototype's baked summary was a known rough edge).
- Series band pooling across problems: keep pooled median+IQR over analyzable trials with per-problem colored raw traces.
- Artifact placement at Investigation scope: none in v1; per-trial inspector remains the surface.

## 9. Verification bar

- Unit: schema records, store CRUD + migration, API routes (auth, idempotency, 409s, preview determinism), client, CLI.
- E2E (`tests/e2e/`): full journey — create → preview → add members → compare → scoped series/points → sweep return path → python export; plus an agent journey via the typed client only.
- Browser-driven verification of the real dashboard for every surface changed (per repo verification norms), including: scope survives repeated tab switches; brush keeps native parcoords semantics; table hides non-selected; invalid-excluded default with honest empty state; sortable tables across pagination.
close_reason: Epic complete: all 11 tasks closed with independently verified evidence (each: targeted pytest + lint/format/typecheck + live browser verification where UI-facing; final full just check 2159 passed/6 skipped at fc57ee9). Delivered: schema records + store v9 + authed idempotent HTTP + preview, typed client, jernerics investigation CLI, Overview/Investigations/Exceptions nav with filter tiles + sortable tables, investigation workspace (Compare + member editor), scoped Series/Points/Search with member scoping + via return + Open in Python token, e2e journeys, docs.

title: Sweep inspector does O(sweep) work every poll tick: re-query, rebuild, re-digest, re-ship the whole page
description:
User report: opening a large sweep on the live dashboard (pyrimel, focus kind=sweep) causes severe slowdown.

Mechanism, measured on a synthetic store with the real query/render path (1000 vs 3000 single-execution trials):

| trials | sweep_detail() | inspector tick: inspector_content build + _content_digest | serialized inspector tree |
|--------|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| 1000   | 33 ms          | 156 ms                                                    | 0.71 MB (8062 nodes)      |
| 3000   | 121 ms         | 472 ms                                                    | 2.13 MB (~24k nodes)      |

Costs compound per 5s poll tick while the page is open and the sweep is incomplete:
1. _render_inspector (callbacks.py:817) rebuilds inspector_content and _content_digest on EVERY tick even when nothing changed — the digest can only be computed by json.dumps-ing the whole 8k-24k node tree (45-200+ ms alone).
2. inspector_content -> sweep_detail (service.py:374) runs 8 queries fetching EVERY execution, family, param set, job, and lineage row under the sweep, then _sweep_sections (workspace.py:489) materializes all of them: a plain html DataTable row per execution (no virtualization), an AgGrid row per family, and the full lineage list baked into a dcc.Store.
3. _render_page tick branch (callbacks.py:329) calls workspace.focus_incomplete (workspace.py:1307), which for a sweep runs the FULL sweep_detail again just to compute a boolean.
4. When the digest changes (relative-time strings tick — same volatile-digest defect as jernerics-l4k, at least once per minute while anything is active) the entire multi-MB tree is serialized, shipped over the tailnet funnel, and React remounts every node. The browser visibly janks; the server burns CPU continuously; neither cost is bounded as the sweep grows.

Fix directions:
- focus_incomplete for sweeps must use a cheap liveness read (sweep_overview row or monitoring counts), never sweep_detail.
- Digest canonical facts (ids, counts, terminal flags, latest updated_ns) instead of rendered children; compute facts before building the tree so unchanged ticks do zero tree work.
- Bound the inspector: render executions/families in the virtualized AgGrid or paginate; cap or trim the lineage store payload.
- Never remount the region when only volatile strings changed (shares its fix with jernerics-l4k).

Acceptance: at 3000 trials the steady-state poll tick performs bounded server work (tens of ms) and ships no inspector payload when no user-visible fact changed; opening a large sweep stays interactive.
close_reason: Completed: digests computed over canonical facts (no relative-time churn); unchanged ticks build zero trees and ship nothing; focus_incomplete uses cheap liveness read, never sweep_detail; executions/families virtualized in AgGrid, lineage store capped; scroll restored after genuine overview re-renders. Proofs: 8dc85f8, 6e00223, 3b8e37f, 26be22a, 935dd39; full suite 1896 passed.

title: Slurm checker chain uses misspelled kill-on-dep-invalid sbatch flag
description:
## Problem
backend/slurm/adapter.py:143 emits #SBATCH --kill-on-dep-invalid=yes in the checker script. The real Slurm option is --kill-on-invalid-dep=<yes|no>; the misspelling is rejected by current Slurm (reproduced on hpc2: sbatch --test-only returns 'unrecognized option'), so the checker/post-hook job fails to submit and remote sweeps never replay tracking data (no retry chain, empty server until manual sync).

## Reproduction
printf '#!/bin/bash\n#SBATCH --kill-on-dep-invalid=yes\n' | sbatch --test-only on hpc2 -> unrecognized option; with --kill-on-invalid-dep=yes -> accepted.

## Fix
One-line rename in the checker script directive.

## Acceptance
sbatch --test-only accepts the generated checker script on hpc2; remote e2e HPC module passes (post-hook replays tracking data).
close_reason: Completed: slurm/adapter.py checker directive renamed to the real option --kill-on-invalid-dep=yes (was --kill-on-dep-invalid, rejected by Slurm 25.05: sbatch 'unrecognized option', orchestrator-reproduced via sbatch --test-only on hpc2; correct spelling accepted). The silent failure killed the whole Slurm post-hook pipeline (checker sbatch swallowed by command substitution). With the fix, live HPC runs land sweeps on the v3 server via checker+post-hook replay; unit test pins the full directive. Merged as 18add7f; just check: 1345 passed, 6 skipped.

title: Tracking v3, analysis client, and dashboard
description:
## Goal
Redesign tracking around a versioned event protocol, normalized SQLite operational store, typed Python client, and persistent read-only dashboard. Support live operational monitoring and post-hoc cross-sweep analysis without coupling the canonical model to Optuna or a dashboard framework.

## Locked architecture
- SQLite remains the operational source of truth: WAL, one writer, bounded transactional ingest batches, controlled reads, online backups, non-destructive future migrations.
- v2 is archived read-only and v3 starts fresh; no v2 server compatibility or semantic data migration.
- Add lightweight `jernerics-schema` package containing Pydantic wire/record contracts only.
- Canonical hierarchy: project -> sweep -> submission/trial -> execution. Optuna retries create linked replacement trials with immediate parent, root, and retry index.
- Optuna remains the current optimizer behind ask/tell. Its journal is authoritative for optimizer state; SQLite holds a reconciled generic mirror. Conflicting terminal states fail visibly.
- Runner automatically records sampled params, resolved config, provenance, objective, lifecycle, and exit facts. `log_param` remains trial-scoped for manual params.
- Execution monitoring records start, heartbeat, latest observation, optional explicit progress, terminal outcome, exit code, and bounded failure summary. Stale is derived, not persisted as failure.
- Tagged UUID events ship from local JSONL in batches of up to 100 or 500 ms. Immutable event IDs provide replay idempotence.
- Flat scalar contexts are canonical JSON text. JSON observations are limited to 64 KiB; larger documents are artifacts.
- Artifacts use immutable UUID identity and two-phase declaration/blob storage. Stored stdout/stderr are system artifacts; live log tail is deferred.
- Typed domain API backs `TrackingClient`; raw `/query` remains an expert escape hatch. `Selection` is project-scoped and can span sweeps, trials, retry families, and executions.
- Dashboard is Dash + Plotly + Dash AG Grid Community mounted on FastAPI. It is read-only, supports unified monitoring-to-analysis drill-down and cross-sweep comparison, and authenticates through API-key exchange for a signed session cookie.
- Dashboard dependencies are standard `jernerics-server` dependencies. No pandas, DuckDB, SQLAlchemy/Alembic, Perspective, marimo, or OpenTelemetry dependency in the initial implementation.

## Non-goals
Multi-user auth, write controls, live scheduler polling, live log tail, saved layouts, annotations, renderer plugins, cross-project comparison, remote code execution, additional optimizer engines, database backends, and supported v2 migration.

## Completion
Every child issue is complete, applicable tests and docs are updated, project checks pass, and an end-to-end smoke test exercises submit correlation, live execution state, values, immutable artifacts/logs, typed client queries, and dashboard drill-down/comparison.
close_reason: Epic complete: all 15 children closed; DoD green (ruff/format/ty/1185 tests); live end-to-end verified

title: Add shared jernerics-schema package
description:
## Scope
Create a third lightweight workspace package, `jernerics-schema`, that is the single runtime definition of tracking wire contracts and typed API records.

## Requirements
- Python 3.12+, with Pydantic as its only runtime dependency.
- Own protocol version, UUID identity aliases/models, flat scalar context type, lifecycle/outcome enums, retry lineage fields, and optimizer-neutral trial records.
- Define a discriminated union for tagged v3 events: sweep/submission/trial snapshot, execution start/heartbeat/progress/end, manual param, value, and artifact declaration.
- Define bounded batch ingest request/response models.
- Define project-scoped multi-sweep Selection, typed domain query/filter/page models, and API response records.
- JSON observation validation enforces 64 KiB encoded payload and flat scalar context.
- Models are immutable where appropriate and generate JSON Schema.
- Package contains no HTTP, SQLite, Optuna, tracker buffering, dashboard, plotting, or business query behavior.
- Wire the package into the workspace and make both `jernerics` and `jernerics-server` depend on it.

## Acceptance
Contract tests cover every event variant, invalid nested context, invalid payload size, serialization round-trip, selection round-trip, and schema-version rejection. Existing packages import the shared models without creating a dependency between client and server packages.
close_reason: Completed: packages/jernerics-schema with tagged v3 event union, ingest/selection/record models, 54 contract tests; full suite 815 passed; commit 6f020dc

description:
