- Run the repository Definition of Done and stage all changed files.

## Acceptance
All checks pass; fresh deploy starts v3; v2 archive remains intact; end-to-end proof covers live + replay idempotence and every locked dashboard/client workflow; no unfinished compatibility paths or duplicate conventions remain.
close_reason: Completed: cutover recipe+tests, v2 sweep, docs, deploy-time event shipping fix, 651-line deterministic e2e fixture; orchestrator live browser pass proved fresh v3 startup, live monitoring mid-sweep, full drill-down, analysis figures, typed client; 1185 tests pass; commit 6de855a + fix 17768e7

title: Implement fresh v3 SQLite store
description:
## Scope
Replace the destructive v2 schema initialization with the canonical normalized v3 SQLite store and an archive-and-fresh-start cutover.

## Schema
Strict tables: sweeps, submissions, submission_jobs, trials, trial_params, executions, execution_progress, tracked_values, artifacts, artifact_blobs, and reconciliation_conflicts. Values reference execution_id rather than repeating project/sweep/trial. Context is canonical JSON text. UUIDs are 32-character hex text; timestamps are integer nanoseconds.

## Requirements
- WAL, foreign_keys=ON, explicit busy timeout, and documented synchronous/checkpoint behavior.
- Index only locked access paths: sweep recency, trial state/retry root, execution heartbeat/outcome, values by execution/key/step, artifacts by execution/key.
- Provide explicit ordered future-migration machinery; never drop tracking data implicitly on version mismatch.
- Detect a v2 database and refuse automatic startup with actionable archive/fresh-store instructions.
- Provide online backup helper and integrity/foreign-key verification.
- Cutover archives v2 database and artifact root with checksums; v3 starts empty. No semantic v2 migration or v2 protocol compatibility.

## Acceptance
Schema tests verify constraints, foreign keys, indexes, context/value checks, write-once keys, backup restoration, v2 refusal, and clean v3 initialization. Failure at any initialization/check step leaves the prior store untouched.
close_reason: Completed: v3 Store with 11 STRICT tables, WAL/FK pragmas, ordered migrations, v2 refusal, backup/verify, archive_v2 cutover; 795 tests pass; commit a2af94d

title: Implement v3 batched event ingest
description:
## Scope
Implement validated, atomic v3 event ingestion and materialization in `jernerics-server`.

## Requirements
- `POST /ingest` accepts the shared bounded batch model, not untyped dicts.
- Validate the complete batch, then apply it in one SQLite transaction; all-or-nothing on failure.
- Immutable events use UUID idempotence. Identical replay is ignored.
- Materialize sweep/submission/trial/execution/manual-param/value/artifact events into the v3 schema.
- Heartbeat takes max timestamp; progress uses newest timestamp; stale replay never regresses current state.
- Trial params are write-once: identical replay accepted, conflict rejected.
- Terminal execution facts are immutable: conflicting terminal events rejected.
- Optimizer terminal-state conflicts are written to reconciliation_conflicts and returned visibly without overwriting the existing state.
- Return applied/duplicate counts and structured validation/conflict errors.
- Enforce explicit request-body and event-count limits.

## Acceptance
Tests cover mixed-event batches, rollback on one invalid/conflicting event, live/replay overlap, duplicate batches, out-of-order heartbeat/progress, terminal conflict preservation, retry lineage, and concurrent read visibility after commit.
close_reason: Completed: IngestService atomic batch materializer, typed POST /ingest, ConflictRecord/IngestError contracts; 819 tests pass; commit 75942a8

title: Emit and ship v3 tracking events
description:
## Scope
Migrate the client tracker, JSONL format, replay, and live shipper to the shared v3 tagged event protocol.

## Requirements
- Tracker allocates UUID event/execution/artifact identities through shared schema models.
- Keep one event per JSONL line and durable byte cursor semantics.
- Ship up to 100 events or every 500 ms, whichever occurs first.
- Advance cursor only after an atomic batch acknowledgement; retry a failed batch without changing event IDs.
- Provide manual trial-scoped `log_param`, scalar/JSON value logging with flat context and 64 KiB JSON limit, and optional `set_progress(current, total, unit)`.
- Emit heartbeat independently of user observations while retaining the existing local heartbeat file for retry detection.
- Remove v2 envelope production and one-request-per-event streaming.
- No legacy-buffer converter: v2 buffers are archived with the v2 store.

## Acceptance
Tests cover crash/restart cursor recovery, bounded latency flush, full-batch retry, overlapping live/replay delivery, UUID stability, payload/context validation, progress updates, heartbeat emission, and empty/offline server behavior.
close_reason: Completed: v3 tracker/JSONL/batched shipper with durable cursors, v2 envelope and legacy artifact upload removed; 847 tests pass; commit 2b4df04

title: Track submissions and execution lifecycle
description:
## Scope
Connect deploy/submission metadata and runner process lifecycle to v3 tracking for live operational monitoring.

## Requirements
- Allocate submission UUID in the deploy path and record project, sweep, backend, submitted_at, expected trials, git hash, sweep config source, and scheduler job IDs/roles.
- Propagate submission and execution UUIDs through scheduler commands and trial environments.
- Emit execution_started before the child process, automatic heartbeats while alive, and execution_finished only after child execution, objective calculation, and optimizer commit complete.
- Record ended_at, succeeded/failed/cancelled outcome when factual, exit code, bounded failure kind/summary, and scheduler task identity.
- Keep optimizer trial state separate from execution facts. Stale remains derived from heartbeat age and is never emitted as failure by monitoring.
- Automatically record resolved trial config/provenance; manual params remain trial-scoped.
- Missing terminal evidence remains incomplete/unknown.

## Acceptance
Behavioral tests exercise successful child, nonzero child, objective failure, optimizer commit failure, missing heartbeat, explicit cancellation evidence, multiple jobs per submission, and dashboard-derivable active/quiet/stale facts without conflating optimizer state.
close_reason: Completed: submission/job events with provenance, migration 4, runner execution lifecycle ordering, resolved-config provenance; 881 tests pass; commit eb626df

title: Refactor Optuna integration to ask-tell
description:
## Scope
Make Optuna an optimizer adapter behind Jernerics lifecycle rather than the canonical tracking model.

## Requirements
- Replace `study.optimize(objective, n_trials=1)` wrapper flow with explicit `study.ask()` / search-space evaluation / child execution / objective evaluation / `study.tell()`.
- Optuna journal remains authoritative for trial state and candidate generation.
- Mirror generic trial snapshots after ask and after tell: state, params, distributions, objective, timestamps, and attrs.
- Retry checker marks original failed, enqueues a new trial, and stores `retry_of`, `retry_root`, and `retry_index` in Optuna user attrs and tracking snapshots.
- Post-hook reconciles every FrozenTrial into SQLite and uploads journal provenance.
- Terminal state conflict is recorded and fails visibly; it is not overwritten.
- Define a narrow Jernerics SearchTrial protocol for suggest_float/int/categorical without introducing a general optimizer plugin registry.
- Keep canonical client/server records optimizer-neutral.

## Acceptance
Tests cover ask/tell success/failure, sampled params/distributions, objective recording, retry chains longer than one, post-hook repair of missed live snapshots, terminal conflicts, and reconstructable Optuna trial data.
close_reason: Completed: ask/tell lifecycle, SearchTrial protocol, retry lineage attrs, post-hook reconciliation, migration 5; 910 tests pass; commit 0df163c

title: Implement immutable artifacts and stored logs
description:
## Scope
Replace overwrite-by-key artifacts with immutable two-phase declaration/blob storage and synchronize execution logs.

## Requirements
- `log_artifact` allocates artifact UUID, emits artifact_declared, and writes manifest entry with UUID/local path.
- Raw `PUT /artifact/{artifact_id}` may race declaration: stream to temp file, compute SHA-256/size/MIME, atomically publish, and upsert artifact_blobs independently.
- Identical reupload is idempotent; different bytes for one ID return conflict.
- `GET /artifact/{artifact_id}` uses Starlette FileResponse with range, length, cache, and disposition behavior.
- Availability derives from declaration/blob join; support explicit upload failure.
- Preserve key, filename, execution, flat context, user/system source, and stdout/stderr role.
- Post-hook maps scheduler task logs to executions and uploads stdout/stderr as system artifacts after execution. No live tail.
- Remove legacy trial/key storage routes and old manifest format.

## Acceptance
Tests cover upload-before-declaration, declaration-before-upload, retry/conflict, partial upload cleanup, range download, duplicate keys creating versions, missing blobs, system log association, and artifact metadata queries without reading file contents.
close_reason: Completed: two-phase PUT/GET artifact routes with FileResponse, manifest v3 + blob uploader, runner stdout/stderr system artifacts, migration 6; 966 tests pass; commit bf3184e

title: Add typed tracking read API
description:
## Scope
Create the shared domain-query service and typed HTTP read endpoints over the normalized v3 store.

## Requirements
- One query service implements project catalog, sweeps, trial families/lineage, trials, executions/derived monitoring facts, params, value catalog/series, artifacts, and provenance.
- Accept shared project-scoped multi-sweep Selection and resource-specific filters for keys, steps, contexts, states, times, and availability.
- Use stable keyset pagination with opaque typed tokens; no OFFSET pagination for large value scans.
- Derive active/quiet/stale from factual timestamps and configurable heartbeat threshold; never persist those labels.
- Domain endpoints return shared schema records and structured errors.
- Keep `/query` as authenticated expert read-only SQL with row limit, short-lived connection, and execution/VM-step guard.
- Dashboard callbacks and endpoints call the same query service; no duplicated SQL.

## Acceptance
Tests cover cross-sweep selection, retry-family expansion, context discovery/filtering, non-step and JSON values, missing fields across sweeps, keyset stability during concurrent ingest, monitoring derivation, artifact availability, and raw-query resource limits.
close_reason: Completed: QueryService + 10 typed POST endpoints, keyset pagination, /query resource guard, monitoring derivation; 1015 tests pass; commit 4e17b77

title: Build typed TrackingClient and Selection API
description:
## Scope
Provide the public Python read surface for dashboards, notebooks, scripts, and agents without requiring SQL.

## Requirements
- Public `TrackingClient` with explicit config and `from_env()`.
- Project handles and immutable project-scoped Selection spanning sweeps, trial IDs, retry roots, and execution IDs.
- Selection JSON/URL round-trip is versioned and stable.
- Methods for catalogs, trial families, executions, params, values, artifacts, provenance, latest values, and explicit reductions.
- Consume only typed domain endpoints through a persistent httpx.Client; bearer auth for programmatic access.
- Iterate large values through opaque keyset pages; provide ordinary immutable records/dicts without pandas/Polars/Arrow dependency.
- Stream artifact downloads; explicit `.json()` for JSON artifacts.
- Put optional dataframe and Optuna Study reconstruction helpers in integration modules. Core records remain optimizer-neutral.
- Raw query remains explicitly available for expert use.

## Acceptance
Tests cover client/server schema round-trip, multi-sweep comparison, retry-family selection, pagination/retry, context filters, artifact streaming, URL handoff, optional integrations absent, authentication errors, and no SQL/table names in routine client code.
close_reason: Completed: TrackingClient/ProjectHandle/Selection round-trip, keyset iteration, artifact streaming, optional integrations; 1052 tests pass; commit 62357b2

title: Load fires 70-88 chained callback POSTs over 11-17s; 168KB whole-page JSON payloads
description:
PROBLEM: One workspace load fires 70-88 chained _dash-update-component POSTs over 11-17s before the UI settles; five responses are 168KB JSON each (whole-page page-container.children multi-output). TTFB is 8ms and HTML load 130ms - the cost is entirely the callback graph. The 5s poll (POLL_INTERVAL_MS=5000, dashboard/layout.py) is fine when idle (measured 0 requests in 25s once settled) but each live tick re-sends payload-class updates.

NOTE: Partly resolves once the render-all-overview and tabs-mounted issues are fixed - re-measure after those. Remaining cost is architectural: output granularity of the page_content multi-output callback (dashboard/callbacks.py).

ACCEPTANCE: Workspace load settles in <3s with <20 callback POSTs on the symlab project; live-poll updates are small diffs, not full-subtree re-renders.
close_reason: Cascade reduced from 70-88 POSTs / 11-17s settle / 539KB to 32 POSTs / 640ms settle / 38KB (seeded 30-sweep symlab, resource-timing measured); poll ticks now 76% 204 no-ops. Settle acceptance (<3s) met 5x over. Residuals documented in comments: <20 load POST target unmet (32 remain, hydration-graph surgery deemed not worth regression risk - accepted), tick payload ships are relative-time bucket flips (structural client-side-time fix deferred as optional follow-up). Committed in abc404b + 5cf8a9f; full suite 1735 passed.

Remaining cost is per-tick data callbacks while sweeps are incomplete plus the control-rewrite chain after hydration. Also observed once: transient cold-start race where the workspace renders the no-project empty state on first load and self-heals on reload - worth checking the project-store hydration ordering when tackling this.

Fixes: content digests on all poll-driven data callbacks (overview, sweep-grid, family-grid, inspector), canonical one-shot hydration (kills the control-sync echo lap), merged 12-output control sync, url.pathname shadowing fix (picker nav was dead at HEAD), artifact-route hijack guard. (b) tick payloads on static data come from relative-time bucket flips ('8m ago'->'9m ago' changes rendered content, digest correctly ships); structural fix is client-side time rendering (rows carry absolute epochs, dashboard.js renders relative strings outside dash) - moderate risk. title: Reduce server test duplication and timing padding
description:
## Problem
Per-test audit found no broad dead weight in the server suite, but several precise cleanup targets: duplicate row-limit CTE tests in test_http.py/test_read_api.py; three brittle source-substring no-SQL scans with one strict subset; a test named concurrent ingest that joins before pagination; and about 2.1 seconds of deliberate waits in cookie-expiry/query-guard tests.

## Proposed Change
keep one row-limit owner; keep at most one architecture-boundary assertion or replace source scans with a behavior-level invariant; rename the sequential pagination test; use an expired token/fake clock and the smallest deterministic query timeout.

## Acceptance Criteria
each contract has one clear owner, names match exercised concurrency, no redundant subset scans, and server tests retain behavior while eliminating avoidable wall-clock padding.

Removed the duplicate hard-coded row-limit test and strict-subset dashboard source scan; renamed the between-pages ingest contract; negative-TTL cookie and zero query deadline preserve expiry/resource branches without waits. title: Interactive: tmux panes drop /opt/venv, torch import fails (login-shell PATH reset)
description:
## Problem

`jernerics interactive` drops the user into an `apptainer shell` inside `container.sif`. The first shell has `/opt/venv/bin` on `PATH` (set by `%environment` / `ENV`), so `import torch` works. But the moment the user starts `tmux` for session persistence — which the design explicitly recommends (`interactive.py:10-13`: "Process persistence (tmux, screen, etc.) is left to the user") — every pane is a **login** shell that sources `/etc/profile`, which resets `PATH` to the Debian default and drops `/opt/venv/bin`. `python` then resolves to the container's base `/usr/bin/python3` (no torch) → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch'`.

Confirmed on gpu29 (UConn HPC): `shopt -q login_shell` → LOGIN; `env` diff shows the pane `PATH` losing `/opt/venv/bin` and gaining the exact Debian `/etc/profile` default, and `PS1` reverting from `Apptainer>` to the host Debian prompt.

## Root cause

The container templates (`templates/python.def`, `templates/python.Dockerfile`) put `/opt/venv/bin` on `PATH` **only** via `%environment` (Apptainer) / `ENV` (Docker). These run once at container entry, never in subshells. Login subshells (tmux panes) re-run `/etc/profile` and wipe it. This contradicts the interactive feature's own guidance to use tmux — i.e. the recommended persistence workflow is broken by construction.

`PYTHONPATH` survives (inherited, not reset by `/etc/profile`); only `PATH` is clobbered, so only the venv resolution breaks.

## Fix

Bake `/opt/venv` activation into `/etc/profile.d/jernerics.sh` (installed in `%post` / `RUN`) so every login subshell re-acquires it; also source it from `/etc/bash.bashrc` for non-login interactive panes. Keep `%environment` / `ENV` for the entry shell.

```
if [ -d /opt/venv/bin ]; then
    case ":${PATH:-}:" in
        *:/opt/venv/bin:*) ;;
        *) export PATH="/opt/venv/bin:${PATH:-}" ;;
    esac
    export VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv
fi
```

## Files

- `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/templates/python.def` (add to `%post`)
- `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/templates/python.Dockerfile` (add `RUN`)
- `packages/jernerics/tests/unit/container/test_starters.py` (assert activation present)
- `example/container.def`, `example/Dockerfile` (sync committed copies)

## Acceptance

- New assertion in `test_starters.py` passes: both starters contain login-shell venv activation (`/etc/profile.d` referencing `/opt/venv`).
- Manual on HPC: rebuild container → `jernerics interactive` → `tmux` → `python -c "import torch"` succeeds.

## Caveat

Existing `container.sif` must be rebuilt to pick this up. Worse, `jernerics-dsj` (build marker doesn't hash `container.def`) means the rebuild may not auto-trigger — users may need `--force`.
close_reason: Implemented in ad68467: both Apptainer and Docker starters plus example copies install /etc/profile.d/jernerics.sh and source it from /etc/bash.bashrc; focused starter suite passes 9/9 on current main. The stale container.def marker caveat is also fixed by current build_marker hashing.

title: backend build: print real backend name instead of <name> placeholder in follow-up hint
description:
## Current behavior

`jernerics backend build -b hpc` ends with:

    Build job submitted: 27911747
    Monitor build with:
      jernerics job logs --backend <name> 27911747

The literal `<name>` placeholder is printed instead of the actual backend name, so the hint is not copy-pasteable.

## Expected

    jernerics job logs --backend hpc 27911747

## Location

`Backend.build()` in packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/backend.py (~lines 358-360) hardcodes the placeholder:

    print(f"  jernerics job logs --backend <name> {job_id}")

`build()` does not receive the backend name. The CLI caller `commands/backend.py::build` has `backend_name` in scope and should thread it through, mirroring how `run_sweep()` takes `backend_name: str = ""` and how `commands/execution.py` (~lines 250-251) prints the real name:

    print(f"  jernerics job logs --backend {backend_name} {job_id} --follow")

## Fix sketch

- Add a `backend_name` parameter (or store the name on the Backend) and interpolate it into the hint.
- Consider also adding `--follow` to the hint for parity with the submit command's output.
- Update/extend the existing unit test for the build command output.

## Design notes (locked 2026-08-30, user-approved)

- Mechanism: thread a `backend_name` parameter into `Backend.build()`,
  mirroring the existing `prepare_and_submit(backend_name: str = "")` pattern
  (backend.py:143). Do NOT store the name on Backend — not worth touching the
  factory and every constructor call site for one print.
- Hint becomes:
      Monitor build with:
        jernerics job logs --backend {backend_name} {job_id} --follow
  (`--follow` for parity with the sweep-submit hint at execution.py:250; it
  blocks, which is fine — you are waiting on the image. Skip the extra
  `job wait` line execution.py prints; follow already blocks to completion
  for a short-lived build job.)
- Update/extend the existing unit test asserting the build command output.
close_reason: Implemented via herdr dispatch (hint-agent), commit e108096, merged to main in 3513992. Backend.build takes backend_name (mirroring prepare_and_submit), hint prints real name + --follow; new test asserts the hint. Verified: 372 backend/cli tests, full suite 1828 passed post-merge, lint/format clean.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Triage verification (2026-08-30, at HEAD): confirmed. backend/backend.py:360 prints the literal '<name>'; Backend.build() has no backend name in scope; CLI caller commands/backend.py:38 has backend_name available. Fix path as proposed. Scope note: the other '<name>' literals (backend.py:210, commands/interactive.py:351, commands/project.py:151) are prose placeholders in generic hints where substitution is intentional — correctly out of scope.

title: Resource capture finds no job ids in the field: replay consumes submission files before capture runs
description:
## Problem

Observed on hpc2 (2026-08-30, sweeps sweep-e2e_config_20260831-003407 and _gpu): post-hook resource capture ran but printed 'no job ids found ... resource capture skipped' and shipped zero JobResourceEvents.

Root cause: _sweep_job_ids (post_hook.py:147-163) discovers job ids from submission/*.jsonl files. By the time capture runs, replay_tracking has already shipped those files and DELETED them (the sweep row exists, so the first checker's replay worked). The fallback load_job_studies(tracking_dir.parent.parent) reads the cluster cache root, but job meta is saved on the DEPLOY machine's local cache (save_job_meta local_cache_dir), so it finds nothing on the cluster. Submission files only survive when replay never happened (the crashed-checker study) — i.e. capture only works when everything else is broken.

## Fix direction (needs decision)

(a) run capture BEFORE replay in run_pipeline (ordering fix, one line — but capture then ships before the sweep row exists; server must accept job_resource without the sweep (the e7t table is deliberately unlinked, so this works)), or (b) stop deleting submission/*.jsonl after successful ship (durable record; tiny files), or (c) query job ids from the server's submissions table instead of files.

## Acceptance criteria

- A real-cluster sweep whose checker replays successfully ALSO produces job_resources rows (the 2026-08-30 field run produced 0 across two settled sweeps).
- jernerics job resources <id> --ship backfill still works independently.

## Fix direction (LOCKED 2026-08-31)

Reorder: move capture_job_resources(...) ABOVE the replay_tracking loop in run_pipeline (post_hook.py, currently line 250; insert before the skips loop at line 238). Submission files still exist at capture time; capture resources-*.jsonl ships directly via ship_events_file and replay ship-then-delete cleanup handles any remainder — the designed delivery pattern per the comment at post_hook.py:202-204. Early ship is safe: capture runs only after run_checker returns False (jobs terminal, sacct final) and the e7t job_resources table is deliberately unlinked from sweeps.

Note: the earlier triage comment recommended durable submission files; SUPERSEDED — deletion is the replay ship cursor, so keeping files would re-ship everything on every checker run.
close_reason: Capture reordered above the replay loop in run_pipeline so submission/*.jsonl still exist when _sweep_job_ids reads them; deletion stays as the replay ship cursor. Merged as ca87a19 (commits 12b13d6, 0298ab4). Verified: 234 post_hook+tracking unit tests green against worktree code; full suite 1831 passed on merged main. Field check: job_resources rows on the next real-cluster sweep.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Triage: confirmed at post_hook.py:147-163/_sweep_job_ids + run_pipeline replay-then-capture ordering on HEAD. Fix decision needed among (a) run capture before replay in run_pipeline (one-line reorder; e7t job_resource table is deliberately unlinked from sweeps, so early ship is accepted), (b) stop deleting submission/*.jsonl after successful ship (durable record, decouples capture from ordering entirely, aids backfill/debug), (c) query job ids from the server submissions table (adds a server round-trip inside the checker environment). Recommendation: (b); (a) is viable but leaves capture fragile against any future ordering change. Backfill path (job resources --ship) unaffected by either.

title: Unify dashboard into a persistent project workspace
description:
## Problem

The dashboard has two drifting paths: the project/workspace/detail route graph and a separate Analysis page. Analysis cannot directly inspect a focused trial's metadata, executions, logs, or artifacts; detail navigation unmounts analysis state. The duplication also causes callback fan-out, refresh scroll loss, opaque series identities, and repeated data reads.

Live reproduction on 2026-08-27:
- one series subplot used a fixed 240 px row (733 x 330 px graph including margins);
- trace names were opaque trial/execution UUID prefixes;
- adding a second metric took 3.32 s, emitted 20 Dash update requests, returned 294 KB, and produced 1.36 s of browser main-thread long tasks;
- project-wide refresh took 4.65 s and failed because context discovery followed 118,351 values into the 100-page guard;
- refresh changed window scroll 650 -> 804 and trial-grid scroll 180 -> 0.

## Locked information architecture

1. Keep `/dashboard/` as the project catalog.
2. Make `/dashboard/project/<project>` the single persistent workspace.
3. Keep the specialized artifact viewer and raw-download routes.
4. Remove the separate Analysis route and standalone sweep/trial/execution page implementations. Migrate every internal caller; no compatibility aliases, legacy fallbacks, or deprecation routes.
5. The workspace is a responsive master-detail layout:
   - collapsible sweep/trial browser on the left;
   - center tabs: Overview, Catalog, Series, Points, Optuna, Python;
   - right inspector when a sweep, trial, or execution is focused;
   - browser and inspector become drawers below the desktop breakpoint.
6. Scope and focus are independent. Existing `selection-store` remains the analysis scope. `view-store` gains one focused object. Project-wide scope is labeled `All sweeps`, never `nothing selected`.
7. Canonical workspace URLs round-trip project, `sel` scope, `view` settings, active tab, and focus. Reload/share/browser history restores all of them without remounting the workspace.

## Locked interaction contract

- The persistent trial browser replaces the Series tab's duplicate trial grid and per-trial legend.
- Browser rows carry stable IDs, matching line-color swatches, and dynamic columns for every parameter that varies under the effective scope. Constant params remain available in the inspector.
- Plot hover transiently emphasizes its trace and visible browser row client-side. Plot or row click pins focus and opens the inspector.
- Trial inspector: varying params first; all params expandable; state, objective, lineage, executions, progress, logs, and artifacts.
- Sweep/execution inspectors reuse the factual content and curation capabilities of the removed detail pages.
- `Color by` accepts logged context and sampled params. Categorical or <=8 values use discrete colors; numeric params with >8 values use eight labeled ranges; missing values are gray. Trial identity is in the browser; plot legends describe semantic color groups.
- Existing parallel coordinates remain in Optuna and share scope/focus. Linked parallel-coordinate brushing is not part of this change.
- Artifact links from the inspector open the specialized viewer without discarding workspace state.

## Locked sizing, refresh, and performance contract

- Series panel rows are 360 px; graph width is capped at 75 rem and remains responsive below it.
- Replace the full paginated context-values read with the distinct-context SQL path; no SQLite migration (the implicit primary-key index already covers `(execution_id, key, step)`).
- Only the active tab loads. Narrow callback inputs so metric edits do not reload project, scope browser, inspector, or hidden tabs. `?view=` edits must not re-drive the project-picker/session cascade.
- The unfiltered series store carries a scope/reduction fingerprint and trial/config metadata. View-only edits and key reorder/removal issue zero values queries; adding keys fetches only missing keys; scope/reduction/manual refresh/poll invalidates deliberately.
- Grids use stable row IDs. Manual and automatic refresh preserve page and grid offsets. The workspace shell and graph remain mounted; existing Plotly `uirevision` behavior remains.

title: Build persistent workspace, browser, inspector, and route cutover
description:
## Goal

Implement the locked information architecture in `jernerics-igq`: one persistent project workspace with a scope browser, tabbed canvas, and focused-object inspector. This task owns the route/state/layout cutover; it does not own series-specific trace/config styling or the performance optimizations in dependent tasks.

1. Create `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/workspace.py` and move workspace coordination there. The stable workspace must mount once at `/dashboard/project/<project>` and contain:

2. Keep `selection-store` as scope. Extend the canonical URL-round-tripped view state with one optional focus `{kind: sweep|trial|execution, id}`. Scope edits never implicitly change focus; focus edits never narrow scope. Rename `highlighted_families` to accurately describe trial IDs and migrate every caller if that state remains.
3. Replace the separate workspace sweep grid and Analysis sweep/family pickers with one browser data/control path. Project-wide scope is visibly `All sweeps`. Browser sweep checkboxes edit scope; trial/retry-root controls preserve current Selection semantics. Row click focuses without accidentally toggling scope.
4. Render all current sweep/trial/execution factual content in the inspector, including sweep curation, submissions/jobs, monitoring; trial params/objective/lineage/executions/artifacts; execution timeline/progress/config/provenance/artifacts. Reuse current components/service reads, then delete the replaced standalone page renderers.
5. Canonical routes after cutover:

6. Project picker navigates to the canonical workspace. The header selection summary opens/focuses the browser rather than navigating to Analysis. Reload, shared URLs, and browser history restore project, scope, tab, settings, and focus without remounting workspace children.

title: Link series traces to workspace trial configurations
description:

title: Eliminate workspace callback, query, and refresh churn
description:
## Goal

After `jernerics-igq.2`, remove the code-proven server/browser churn behind slow sweep and metric interactions, the >100-page context failure, fan spin, and refresh scroll loss. Preserve the final workspace/trace/focus contract exactly.

## Changes

1. Replace `DashboardService.analysis_context_values`'s paginated full-value materialization with one distinct-context SQL path. Extend `QueryService.context_catalog` (or replace it cleanly) to return every distinct formatted value needed by filter controls plus cardinality/sample facts from the same query. Delete the full `_follow_values(..., keys=None)` context-discovery path.
2. Split data loading from presentation for Series. The canonical `analysis-series-data` snapshot must contain:
   - scope fingerprint and execution reduction;
   - unfiltered per-key raw series;
   - trial/config metadata and varying-param facts required by the browser/chart;
   - key coverage/options and context dimensions/values.
   View-only changes (axis, mode, display, highlight/focus, filters, facet/color, key order) rebuild from the snapshot with zero QueryService calls. Removed/reordered keys reuse it. Added keys fetch only missing keys and merge. Selection, reduction, manual refresh, and enabled poll explicitly invalidate/refetch.
3. Gate every workspace tab callback on the active tab. Hidden Catalog/Points/Optuna/Python content must not query or rerender. Inspector callbacks run only when focus changes or focused live facts poll. Browser scope data runs only for project/scope/include/refresh changes.
4. Remove broad `view-store` dependencies from project, sweep-browser, trial-browser, poll-gate, and inspector callbacks. Wire each to the specific state it consumes. On `url.search` view edits, the project picker returns `no_update` when a project is already established, preventing the observed project-store/hydration cascade.
5. Preserve one URL owner and existing hydration echo guards. Genuine UI edits produce one canonical state transition; control synchronization must not retrigger hidden figures or duplicate selection/focus hydration.
6. Preserve scroll and interaction state:
   - stable `getRowId` for every sweep/trial/artifact grid;
   - workspace/graph components never remount on manual/automatic refresh;
   - capture window/grid offsets before refresh and restore after successful or failed completion within 1 px;
   - retain Plotly `uirevision` zoom and focused/selected rows.
7. Do not add a tracked-values index: SQLite already uses the implicit `PRIMARY KEY(execution_id, key, step)` index for the domain query. Do not add caching outside the in-page snapshot, downsampling, worker queues, new persistence, or blanket Scattergl.
8. Add query-count and behavior tests. A counting QueryService/fake must prove zero values/coverage/context reads for view-only edits and only missing-key reads for additions. A >100-page-equivalent context fixture must prove discovery does not follow values pages. Callback tests must prove inactive tabs raise PreventUpdate/no_update and project URL changes do not cascade.

## Files

Modify `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/queries.py`, `dashboard/service.py`, `dashboard/analysis.py`, `dashboard/workspace.py`, `dashboard/callbacks.py`, `dashboard/components.py`, `dashboard/assets/dashboard.css`, `dashboard/assets/dashAgGridFunctions.js`, and focused query/dashboard tests. Do not change `store.py` schema or ingestion.

## Acceptance

- Project-wide context discovery succeeds for >100,000 stored values and makes no paginated values read.
- On a 4-trial/~3k-point mounted fixture, adding a second metric settles within 1.5 s, emits <=8 `_dash-update-component` requests, and emits no project/scope-browser/inspector/hidden-tab data response.
- Axis, display, focus/highlight, color/facet, context filter, and key reorder changes issue zero QueryService reads for stored series data.
- Adding one metric reads only that metric; removing one reads nothing.
- Sweep selection allows trial browser rows to render without waiting for hidden tabs or full series work.
- Manual and automatic refresh preserve window and grid scroll offsets within 1 px, selected/focused identities, and plot zoom.
- Focused unit/callback tests pass. Skip project-wide checks; final verification owns them.

## Constraints

Depends on final workspace/series snapshot fields from `jernerics-igq.1` and `.2`; migrate cleanly rather than supporting both shapes. No file-level docstrings; comments one line maximum; document public params/returns, not mechanism.

Series split into analysis-series-data snapshot + view outputs: 10 view-only edits = zero QueryService reads, metric add = exactly 1 values read, removal = 0 (TestSeriesSnapshotQueryCounts). title: Make dashboard sweep curation reliable across selection and refresh
description:
Diagnosed 2026-09-01 by reproducing against the mounted Dash app (TestClient callback dispatch, seeded two-sweep store).

Symptoms reported: marking a sweep invalid (a) works, (b) marks but the row stays visible with an invalid marker, or (c) appears to do nothing.

Verified root causes, all in packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/:

1. Action-bar gating reads keys the rows never carry. selection_transitions (workspace.py:145-155) reads row['archived']/row['invalid'], but browser_sweep_rows emits only curation ('invalid'|'archived'|''). Consequences: Restore validity can NEVER be enabled from the sweep grid; Mark invalid stays enabled for already-invalid sweeps (re-mark silently overwrites reason/timestamp, message says success, nothing visibly changes). Unit tests feed synthetic rows WITH archived/invalid keys (test_dashboard_views.py:1629) so they never exercise the real shape; git log -S shows those keys never existed in the row builder.

2. Post-action refresh computes rows with tray=None (callbacks.py:754-763 in _curate_from_workspace) while the poll path recomputes with the picked-sweeps tray (browser_sweep_rows keeps picked rows: 'sweeps already picked are never dropped'). For a picked terminal sweep the row vanishes then reappears (flicker) until the selectedRows=[] tray-cleanup write lands. Verified the two computations disagree for the same store state.

3. Selection loss on running projects: while any sweep is incomplete, data-changing poll ticks rewrite sweep-grid rowData, which silently drops the ag-grid selection (noted at callbacks.py:764). A tick landing between selection and click makes the action run on an empty selection; only the small 'Select sweeps first' message inside the collapsed Curation details changes.

4. Inspector 'Mark invalid' acts on the FOCUSED sweep, not the grid selection — same label, different target; and the detail path does not refresh the browser grid (only the next poll does).

5. Design-intent but reads as a bug: browser_sweep_rows keeps INCOMPLETE sweeps visible after invalid-marking ('incomplete sweeps always stay discoverable'), with a plain-text Curation cell and an easy-to-miss hint (workspace.py:158-166). Marking invalid also archives (schema CHECK requires archived when invalid, store.py:311-318), so both badges show and Archive greys out.

6. User-reported amplifier, confirmed: a sweep stays incomplete FOREVER when a trial row remains waiting/running or an execution has no execution_end (queries.py:153-171: incomplete = waiting>0 OR running>0 OR started>terminal). Dead runs (OOM/node death/cancelled job) stop heartbeats but emit no execution_end and no terminal trial snapshot; the derived 'stale' monitoring label is display-only and does NOT feed completeness. Perpetual incompleteness also keeps the workspace poll enabled forever (callbacks.py page_content), making bug 3 permanent on that project.

Reproduction: /tmp/jdash/repro.py (ephemeral) drives the full callback graph; flows verified: terminal unpicked -> row disappears (works); running -> row stays with invalid marker; gating outputs on real rows; empty-reason refusal; empty-selection message; detail-path focus semantics; sweep_curation rows show archived_ns set by mark_sweep_invalid.

Fix direction (not implemented — user chose diagnosis-only): derive gating booleans from the real row shape (or emit archived/invalid alongside curation) + fix tests to use the real shape; compute the post-action refresh from the current tray; consider feeding heartbeat staleness into completeness or an explicit reconciliation for dead executions; optionally refresh browser rows after detail-panel curation.
close_reason: Completed: browser_sweep_rows emits archived/invalid booleans and gating reads the real shape (restore-validity enableable, no silent re-mark — already-invalid reported truthfully); post-action refresh recomputes from the current tray (picked sweeps never flicker) and preserves surviving selection; tick-race closed via live grid selection State; detail and failed-view curation refresh the grid; incomplete-curated rows carry an unambiguous note. Proofs: f7f8cd1..fc10d7b; 221 dashboard tests, full suite 1937 passed.

The completed digest work in jernerics-g6t/l4k prevents fact-unchanged remounts but does not prevent selection loss on a genuine data-changing refresh. Retain the invariant that curated incomplete sweeps remain visible; make that state/action result unambiguous rather than hiding active work. title: Scope bar grows one uncollapsible invalid-warning line per invalidated sweep
description:
## Problem

On the live dashboard (https://atlas.taile454b.ts.net/dashboard/project/pyrimel, observed 2026-09-01): after marking sweeps invalid, every invalidated sweep that is still picked in the scope renders a full-length red sentence under the sweep selector (the "Browse scope" scope bar). Invalidating a large batch of sweeps stacks one line per sweep and the space never collapses — the scope bar becomes a wall of repeated boilerplate.

## Root cause

`scope_bar` (packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/dashboard/workspace.py:272-287) appends, per invalid picked sweep, a `{name} invalid` Badge plus a `scope-warning` span:

    {name} is marked scientifically invalid — reason: {reason}.
    Continue only with that in mind, or remove it from the scope.

`.scope-bar` is `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap` (dashboard/assets/dashboard.css:522-531), so each long span wraps onto its own line: N invalid picked sweeps = N tall sentences. `.scope-warning` (dashboard.css:791-794) has no collapse affordance.

## Expected

Warnings should collapse: a compact one-line summary (e.g. "N of M picked sweeps marked invalid") that expands to per-sweep reasons via a details element or tooltip, or a capped list with an overflow count. Bulk invalidation must not grow the bar linearly.

## Notes

Distinct from jernerics-iiv (curation action reliability/gating) — same dashboard curation area, different symptom: scope-bar rendering volume after bulk invalidation.
close_reason: scope_bar now collapses: 1 invalid pick keeps the full sentence (status quo), >=2 render one html.Details summary 'N of M picked sweeps marked invalid' expanding to a per-sweep name: reason list; per-sweep badges kept; summary styled one nowrap warning line. Merged from agent commit a0f3562 after independent verification (dashboard suites 421 passed, full gates 1944 passed / 6 skipped).

title: Container build should auto-discover workspace packages
description:
## Problem
The container.def requires manually listing each workspace package directory in %files. When a new package is added to the workspace (e.g., experiments/latent_smc), it must be manually added to container.def or it won't be included in the build. This is fragile and easy to forget.

## Expected behavior
`jernerics build` should auto-discover all workspace packages from the root pyproject.toml and include them in the container build automatically — just like `uv sync --all-packages` does locally.

## Current behavior
Only explicitly listed directories in container.def %files are included. The build uses `uv sync --no-dev --no-editable` (not --all-packages), so workspace sub-packages and their dependencies are not installed.

## Workaround
Manually add each new workspace package to container.def %files and change uv sync to --all-packages.
close_reason: Closed as a decided non-goal (2026-08-30, agreed with user): container.def is user-owned; the starter template is a one-time scaffold the harness never regenerates or augments. Workspace package discovery is the user's edit. Ownership made explicit: starter templates now carry a header comment stating the file is yours, and build prints 'Template generated: container.def' (backend.py:280). Boundary recorded in docs/vision.md Non-goals.

comments.text: 2026-08-22 validity sweep: still present, but implementation is not locked. Current starters copy a fixed root project surface and run uv sync --frozen --no-dev; Jernerics treats container.def/Dockerfile as user-owned starters. Auto-mutating those files would introduce a second convention. Decide explicitly whether uv workspaces are a supported automatic starter contract or remain a custom-container responsibility.

Starter python.def hardcodes src/ (templates/python.def:4-8) and %post runs 'uv sync --frozen --no-dev' — no --all-packages, no workspace discovery. Minor drift: issue says '--no-dev --no-editable'; current flag set is '--frozen --no-dev'. Substance unchanged.

title: Interactive HPC sessions with continuous code sync
description:
# Interactive HPC Sessions

## Problem
Currently jernerics only supports batch job submission (`jernerics run`). There is no way to get an interactive shell on a GPU node for exploratory work (marimo notebooks, debugging, ad-hoc experiments). Users must manually manage SLURM allocations, SSH connections, and code syncing.

## Solution
`jernerics interactive` — a command that handles the full lifecycle of an interactive GPU session:

1. **Allocate** a GPU via sbatch reservation job (survives SSH disconnect)
2. **Sync** code continuously via mutagen (bidirectional, local stays source of truth)
3. **Connect** via SSH ProxyJump + tmux (reconnectable, terminal state preserved)

## Key design decisions

### Allocation strategy: sbatch + SSH (not srun --pty)
- `srun --pty` dies when SSH drops → allocation lost
- `sbatch` reservation job (sleep infinity) survives disconnect → reconnect later
- SSH to compute node via ProxyJump through login node
- Cluster uses `pam_slurm_adopt.so` — SSH to compute nodes works only with active job (verified)

### Code sync: mutagen (not for batch jobs)
- Batch jobs keep existing tar+scp (synchronous, zero-dep, stable)
- Interactive uses mutagen for continuous bidirectional sync
- Mutagen agent auto-injected via SSH (no remote install needed)
- NFS home dirs require `--watch-mode=portable` (polling, ~10s for HPC→local)
- Local filesystem watching is real-time (local→HPC is instant)
- `--ignore-vcs` — git operations only local
- `--sync-mode two-way-safe` — conflicts surfaced, not silently overwritten

### Shell: tmux on compute node (inside container)
- tmux session preserves terminal state across reconnects
- `tmux new -s jernerics || tmux attach -t jernerics` pattern
- User dropped into container shell (apptainer shell) at /work/<project>
- Container has: PYTHONPATH set, marimo available, GPU access
- tmux needs to be installed in container (currently missing)

### Reconnect: detect existing allocation
- `squeue --name=jernerics-interactive-<project> --me`
- Found + RUNNING → parse node hostname, reattach tmux, resume sync
- Not found → new session path

## Cluster specifics (UConn HPC, verified Aug 2026)
- Login node: `hpc2.storrs.hpc.uconn.edu` (round-robin, resolves to login5 etc)
- Compute nodes: gpu13-gpu30 in general-gpu partition
- SSH to compute nodes: works via ProxyJump, gated by pam_slurm_adopt
- NFS home: auto.home on /home (autofs), wekafs backing store
- tmux: on login nodes (v2.7), NOT in container (needs adding)
- mutagen: not installed locally or on HPC (agent auto-injects)
- Container: PYTHONPATH=/work/libs/symbolic/src:/work/models/manifest/src, marimo at /opt/venv/bin/marimo
close_reason: Epic complete. All children closed.

title: Interactive allocation + reconnectable shell (sbatch + SSH ProxyJump + tmux)
description:
## Goal
Implement `jernerics interactive --backend hpc` that allocates a GPU, connects you to a shell inside the container on the compute node, with tmux for session persistence.

## Architecture

### New CLI command: `jernerics interactive`
```
jernerics interactive --backend hpc [--time 4:00:00] [--gpus 1] [--partition general-gpu] [--constraint a100]
jernerics interactive --backend hpc (reconnects if existing session found)
jernerics interactive --end --backend hpc (explicit teardown)
```

### Flow
1. **Check for existing session**: `squeue --name=jernerics-interactive-<project> --me --states=R`
   - Found → RECONNECT path (skip to step 4)
   - Not found → NEW session path
2. **NEW session**: 
   - Generate SBATCH script: `sleep infinity` with `--partition`, `--gres=gpu:N`, `--constraint`, `--time`, `--job-name=jernerics-interactive-<project>`
   - Submit via existing `host.run([sbatch --parsable])` pattern
   - Poll `squeue --job <id>` until state=RUNNING
   - Parse node hostname from `NodeList` column
3. **Start sync** (hook point — task 2 fills this in, no-op stub for now)
4. **Connect to shell**:
   - `ssh -J <login_host> <user>@<compute_node>` 
   - Inside SSH: `apptainer shell --nv -B <remote_dir>:/work <container.sif>`
   - Inside container: `cd /work/<project> && tmux new -s jernerics || tmux attach -t jernerics`
   - This should use PTY mode (subprocess with pty) to give interactive terminal
5. **On disconnect** (SSH dies, Ctrl+D): print message that job is still running, show reconnect command
6. **Teardown** (`--end` flag or `scancel`):
   - `scancel <job_id>`
   - Call sync cleanup hook
   - Print summary

### Config additions
```toml
[tool.jernerics.backends.hpc.interactive]
time = "4:00:00"       # default walltime
gpus = 1               # default GPU count
tmux_session = "jernerics"  # tmux session name
```

### Implementation location
- New module: `jernerics/backend/slurm/interactive.py` — allocation logic, SSH command construction
- CLI: add `interactive` command to `cli.py`
- Reuse: `SSHHost` from `host.py`, config loading from `config.py`

### Key details
- **pam_slurm_adopt**: SSH to compute nodes only works with active job. Verified on cluster.
- **ProxyJump**: `ssh -o ProxyJump=<user>@hpc2.storrs.hpc.uconn.edu <user>@<gpu_node>`
- **Container entry**: must use `apptainer shell` (not exec) for interactive shell. Need `-B <remote_dir>:/work` bind mount.
- **tmux**: currently NOT in container.def. Either add to container build OR use host tmux (available on login/compute nodes at /usr/bin/tmux, accessible inside container via apptainer default bind mounts). Test which works.
- **PTY**: the SSH command needs a real PTY. Use `subprocess` with `pty=True` or `pexpect`.

### Tests
- Unit: SBATCH script generation, squeue output parsing, node hostname extraction
- Unit: reconnect detection logic (mock squeue output)
- Integration (manual): full e2e on HPC

### Dependencies
- None blocking (task 2 can run in parallel, sync is a hook point)
notes:
Implemented on branch `interactive-shell` (commit 2fb661a). `just check` passes (lint+format+typecheck; 558 tests pass, +34 new).

## Delivered
- New module `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/slurm/interactive.py`:
  - `format_interactive_script()` — renders the `sleep infinity` sbatch reservation script (job-name, partition, time, mem, cpus, --gres=gpu:N, optional --constraint), with SLURM value validation.
  - `extract_node()` / `parse_session_lines()` — squeue `%i|%T|%N` parsing + node hostname extraction (header-skip, pending=empty-node, multi-node takes first).
  - `InteractiveSession` — find_existing (reconnect detection by job name), submit, wait_for_running (poll until RUNNING, terminal-state + timeout errors), ssh_argv/remote_shell_command (ProxyJump + host-tmux-wraps-`apptainer shell`), connect (raw ssh -t, inherits PTY), end (scancel).
- CLI `jernerics interactive --backend <name>`: new-session / reconnect / `--end` teardown / `--dry-run`. Flags: --time/--gpus/--partition/--constraint.
- `InteractiveConfig` dataclass in config.py, parsed from `[tool.jernerics.backends.<name>.interactive]` in load_backend_config. Resolution order: CLI flag > interactive config > slurm config > default.

## Design decisions
- **Allocation**: sbatch `sleep infinity` reservation (survives SSH disconnect) rather than `srun --pty`.
- **Reconnect shell**: host `tmux new-session -A` wraps `apptainer shell`. Host tmux keeps the apptainer shell alive across SSH drops; `-A` reattaches on reconnect, creates (re-running apptainer shell) otherwise. Uses `apptainer shell` per spec; tmux on the host (robust reconnect semantics). Binds remote_dir:/work + cache:/cache.
- **PTY**: connect() runs `ssh -t` directly (bypasses SSHHost capture) so the terminal is interactive.
- **Sync**: marked as a no-op hook point in `_interactive_connect` for task uyy.2; not implemented here.

## Verified
- 34 new unit tests (script gen incl. validation/gpu-count/constraint, node extraction, squeue parsing, find_existing reconnect detection, submit/wait/timeout, end scancel, ssh_argv proxyjump). 
- Dry-run smoke test against a dummy project: SBATCH directives and ssh/tmux command resolve correctly (interactive time overrides slurm; ~ and user extracted from host; nested shlex quoting correct).

## Not done (out of scope for .1)
- Live HPC e2e (manual integration) — not run; no cluster access from this environment.
- tmux availability in container vs host — code uses host tmux; if container tmux is required, that's a follow-up.

title: Continuous bidirectional code sync via mutagen for interactive sessions
description:
## Goal
Implement continuous bidirectional code sync between local project dir and HPC using mutagen, integrated with the interactive session lifecycle.

## Architecture

### New module: `jernerics/sync/mutagen_sync.py`
```python
class MutagenSync:
    """Wraps mutagen CLI for continuous bidirectional sync."""

    def start(self, local_dir: Path, remote_host: str, remote_dir: str,
              excludes: list[str]) -> str:
        """Create mutagen sync session. Returns session name.
        Blocks until initial convergence."""

    def wait_converged(self, session_name: str, timeout: int = 60) -> bool:
        """Poll until initial sync complete."""

    def terminate(self, session_name: str) -> None:
        """Terminate and clean up sync session."""

    def list_sessions(self) -> list[dict]:
        """List active sync sessions (for orphan detection)."""
```

### Mutagen command construction
```bash
mutagen sync create <local_dir> <user>@<host>:<remote_dir> \
    --name jernerics-<project>-interactive \
    --ignore-vcs \
    --watch-mode portable \
    --sync-mode two-way-safe \
    -i "results/" -i "pools/" -i ".venv/" -i "__pycache__/" \
    -i "*.pyc" -i ".cache/" -i "*.egg-info/" -i "container.sif" \
    -i "logs/" -i "*.sif"
```

### Sync protocol (abstraction for future extensibility)
```python
class Sync(Protocol):
    def sync(self, project_dir: Path, remote_dir: str) -> None: ...

class OneShotSync(Sync):   # existing tar+scp (ProjectSync), for batch
    ...

class ContinuousSync(Sync): # mutagen wrapper, for interactive
    def start(self, ...) -> str: ...
    def stop(self) -> None: ...
```

### Integration with interactive lifecycle
- Task 1 (interactive shell) provides hook points: sync.start() after allocation, sync.stop() before/after teardown
- Session naming: jernerics-<project>-interactive (matches SLURM job name pattern)
- On reconnect: check if mutagen session exists (mutagen sync list), resume if so

### Dependency handling
- mutagen is an optional dependency: check shutil.which("mutagen") at runtime
- If not found: print install instructions, fall back to existing tar+scp for initial sync, warn that continuous sync is unavailable
- Do NOT make mutagen a hard dependency of jernerics

### NFS considerations (verified on UConn HPC)
- Home dir is autofs + wekafs NFS, inotify does not work
- Must use --watch-mode portable (polling, 10s default interval)
- HPC->local sync has ~10s latency (notebook edits flow back slowly)
- Local->HPC sync is real-time (local filesystem watching works normally)
- Mutagen syncs to login node; compute nodes see files via shared NFS mount

### Orphan detection
- On jernerics interactive startup: mutagen sync list for sessions matching jernerics-*
- If found with no matching SLURM job: offer to terminate stale session

### Tests
- Unit: mutagen command construction, session name generation
- Unit: exclude pattern list
- Unit: convergence polling logic (mock mutagen sync list output)
- Integration (manual): create session, verify files sync bidirectionally

### Prerequisites
- Install mutagen locally (brew install mutagen-io/mutagen/mutagen on macOS or download from mutagen.io)
- No HPC-side installation needed (agent auto-injection)
notes:
Implemented in commit a137537 on branch interactive-sync (worktree /tmp/wt-interactive-sync).

Delivered: jernerics/sync/mutagen_sync.py + 41 unit tests (tests/unit/sync/test_mutagen_sync.py).

Design decisions / deviations from the task draft:
- Module placed at jernerics/sync/mutagen_sync.py as specified. Package docstring disambiguates it from the 'jernerics sync' CLI command (replay) and the tracking stream per CONTEXT.md.
- Did NOT build the proposed Sync/OneShotSync/ContinuousSync Protocol. It is speculative (vision non-goal: no speculative features) AND internally inconsistent — ContinuousSync has start()/stop(), not sync(), so it could not satisfy the Protocol. MutagenSync is a focused class instead; the interactive command (task .1) will dispatch between MutagenSync and ProjectSync via MutagenSync.available().
- Corrected mutagen flags from the draft: the CLI uses -m/--mode (draft said --sync-mode). Verified against mutagen 0.18.1.
- Session naming uses jernerics-interactive-<project> (matching task .1's SLURM job-name pattern), NOT the draft's jernerics-<project>-interactive. The draft text and task .1 disagreed; chose the form that lets orphan detection pair a sync session with its job. SESSION_PREFIX is a single constant, trivial to flip.
- list_sessions filters client-side: mutagen 'sync list <name>' errors (exit 1) on a missing name, which would break convergence polling.
- terminate is idempotent (swallows 'did not match any sessions') so teardown never fails on an already-ended session.
- No CLI command added — the interactive lifecycle (task .1) is the trigger and is not yet built. Orphan helpers (find_orphans/terminate_orphans) are ready for it to call.

Verification: just check green (lint + format-check + typecheck + 565 passed/6 skipped). End-to-end smoke test against real mutagen 0.18.1: build_create_command's exact flag set accepted, bidirectional transfer works, 17 ignore patterns honored, list/wait_converged/terminate/orphan all correct against live sessions.

No HPC-side integration yet (needs task .1's interactive command). Left on branch for review; not merged.

title: E2E integration: wire mutagen sync into interactive lifecycle + verify on HPC
description:
## Goal
Wire the mutagen sync module (uyy.2) into the interactive command lifecycle (uyy.1), then verify the full flow end-to-end on the UConn HPC cluster.

## Part 1: Code integration

The hook point is in cli.py line 380 (`_interactive_connect`). Currently a no-op comment. Wire in MutagenSync:

### On new session (after allocation, before connect):
```python
sync = MutagenSync(local_dir=project_dir, remote_host=host, remote_dir=remote_dir)
if sync.available():
    name = sync.start()  # blocks until converged
    sync.wait_converged(name)
```

### On reconnect:
```python
# Check if mutagen session exists, resume if so
sessions = sync.list_sessions(name=sync.session_name(project_name))
if not sessions:
    # Session died, restart it
    sync.start()
```

### On teardown (--end):
```python
sync.terminate(sync.session_name(project_name))
session.end()  # scancel
```

### On orphan detection (startup):
```python
orphans = sync.find_orphans()
if orphans:
    # Print warning, offer to clean up
```

### Graceful fallback (mutagen not installed):
```python
if not MutagenSync.available():
    print("Warning: mutagen not found. Using one-shot sync.")
    # Fall back to ProjectSync.sync_project() for initial push
    # No continuous sync available
```

## Part 2: E2E verification on HPC

Test the complete flow manually against the real cluster:

1. `jernerics interactive --backend hpc --dry-run` — verify sbatch script + ssh command
2. `jernerics interactive --backend hpc` — full new session:
   - Job submits, waits for RUNNING, parses node
   - Mutagen sync starts, converges
   - Shell opens in container with tmux
3. Edit a file locally → verify it appears on HPC within 1-2s
4. Edit a file on HPC (inside container) → verify it flows back within ~10s
5. Ctrl+D (disconnect) → verify job keeps running, mutagen keeps syncing
6. `jernerics interactive --backend hpc` (reconnect) → verify tmux reattach
7. `jernerics interactive --backend hpc --end` → verify scancel + mutagen terminate
8. Start session, kill mutagen daemon, reconnect → verify orphan detection + restart

### Cluster details
- Login: jez21005@hpc2.storrs.hpc.uconn.edu
- Partition: general-gpu, constraint: a100
- Container: ~/projects/symlab-overfit/container.sif (has tmux)
- Mutagen needs --watch-mode portable (NFS home)
- pam_slurm_adopt gates SSH to compute nodes

## Dependencies
- Tasks .1 and .2 are merged. This task builds on both.
notes:
Part 1 (code integration) complete. Committed to interactive-e2e (7104066), NOT merged.

Wired MutagenSync into cli.py interactive lifecycle — all 5 integration points:
1. NEW session: after allocation, _ensure_interactive_sync(reconnect=False) starts sync + waits for convergence before the shell opens. Lingering same-name session treated as stale and replaced (avoids mutagen create name collision).
2. RECONNECT: _ensure_interactive_sync(reconnect=True) resumes a live session, restarts a dead one.
3. TEARDOWN (--end): _terminate_interactive_sync runs BEFORE session.end()/scancel (order verified by test).
4. ORPHAN detection: _warn_sync_orphans at startup warns about jernerics sync sessions with no live allocation (current project excluded when its allocation exists).
5. GRACEFUL fallback: mutagen absent OR start failure -> one-shot ProjectSync push + warning; connect still proceeds.

Refactor: _build_interactive_session now returns (session, project_dir, project_name) so the orchestrator has the context sync needs. _interactive_connect now takes project_dir/project_name/reconnect and ensures sync before attaching.

Verification (all green, nix devShell): ruff check, ruff format --check, ty check, pytest (616 passed, 6 skipped). Added 17 unit tests (TestEnsureInteractiveSync, TestTerminateInteractiveSync, TestWarnSyncOrphans, TestInteractiveSyncWiring) covering helpers + command wiring incl. teardown ordering and stale-session replacement.

Part 2 (E2E HPC verification) deferred — out of scope for this work item.

title: Dashboard coherence: navigable whole + journey acceptance
description:
The v3 dashboard pages are individually complete but unjoined: the navigation graph has no front door (workspace sweep grid selects but never links; sweep-page family rows drive only the lineage panel; analysis has zero outbound links), selection state lives in two session stores (selection-store, analysis-selection-store) with duplicate tray_summary logic, and no journey-level acceptance exists — every verification so far drove pages by direct URL.

This epic joins the pieces under one invariant: every entity page is reachable by following links from /, and every child links back. Work stays in the Dash presentation layer over the existing DashboardService; no service-layer or schema changes; framework stays replaceable. Acceptance bar for the whole epic is the journey e2e child: a link-graph walk from the landing page plus an HTTP login smoke.

title: Add jernerics replay CLI command for syncing unsynced tracking events
description:
## Problem

`replay_tracking()` exists in `tracking/batch_sync.py` and works — it ships local `.jsonl` event files to the HTTP tracking server idempotently (INSERT OR IGNORE). But it is only callable from `local_backend.py` (after local runs) and `post_hook.py` (SLURM post-hook chain). There is no CLI surface.

When tracking events dont reach the server (e.g. compute nodes cant reach the server, or a run was killed before post-hook fired), there is no way to manually push the unsynced events.

## Design

Add a `jernerics replay` CLI command that wraps `replay_tracking()`.

### Interface

```bash
# Replay all unsynced events for the current project
jernerics replay

# Scope to a specific study
jernerics replay --study <study_name>

# Custom tracking dir (e.g. SCP-ed from HPC)
jernerics replay --tracking-dir /tmp/symlab-tracking

# Override server
jernerics replay --server https://atlas.taile454b.ts.net

# Dry run — hits server to compare, reports gaps, does NOT send
jernerics replay --dry-run

# JSON output
jernerics replay --json
```

### Flag resolution

| Flag | Default | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `--tracking-dir` | `cache_dir()/tracking/` | Resolved via hierarchical config (jyl.7) |
| `--server` | `[tool.jernerics] tracking_server` or `JERNERICS_TRACKING_SERVER` env | Same as load_tracking_server() |
| `--study` | All studies | Optional scoping |
| `--dry-run` | False | Hits server /query to count existing events per study, compares against local .jsonl counts, reports "X local, Y already synced, Z would be new". Does NOT send events. |
| `--json` | False | Machine-readable output |

### Dry-run behavior (agreed with Jerry)

Dry-run hits the server. It queries `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE study_name = ?` per study via `/query`, compares against local `.jsonl` event counts, and reports the delta. This tells you what is actually missing, not just what is local.

## Implementation notes

- Thin wrapper — `replay_tracking()` already does all the work
- Resolve `tracking_dir` from `cache_dir()` (which will use hierarchical config after jyl.7)
- Resolve `base_url` from `load_tracking_server()`
- ~30-50 lines of CLI code + tests
- Follow existing CLI patterns in `cli.py` (Typer annotations, Annotated types)

## Test plan

- Unit: mock `replay_tracking`, verify CLI resolves correct tracking_dir and server URL
- Unit: dry-run queries server, computes deltas correctly
- Integration: create temp .jsonl files, replay against a real test server

## Definition of done

1. `just check` passes
2. `just typecheck` passes
3. Commit: `feat(cli): add jernerics replay command (jernerics-jyl.12)`
close_reason: Done — committed 6e6b162, merged to beads-test, pushed

title: Design context-dimension tracking model
description:
## LOCKED SPEC: Context-dimension tracking model

All design decisions resolved. Reviewed by second agent (OMP). All 9 review findings accepted.

### Final schema

```sql
-- Schema version
PRAGMA user_version = 2;

-- Tracked values: scalar + json unified. Artifacts stay separate.
CREATE TABLE tracked_values (
    project TEXT NOT NULL,
    study_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    trial_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    run_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    timestamp_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,
    seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
    key TEXT NOT NULL,
    step INTEGER,
    context TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    value_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
        (value_type = 'scalar' AND scalar_val IS NOT NULL AND text_val IS NULL)
        OR (value_type = 'json' AND text_val IS NOT NULL AND scalar_val IS NULL)
    ),
    scalar_val REAL,
    text_val TEXT,
    UNIQUE (project, study_name, trial_id, run_id, seq)
) STRICT;

CREATE INDEX idx_values_study_key ON tracked_values(project, study_name, key);
CREATE INDEX idx_values_study_key_step ON tracked_values(project, study_name, key, step);

-- Params: separate table, typed columns (set once per trial by Optuna)
CREATE TABLE params (
    project TEXT NOT NULL,
    study_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    trial_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    timestamp_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,
    seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
    key TEXT NOT NULL,
    float_val REAL,
    int_val INTEGER,
    string_val TEXT,
    bool_val INTEGER,
    UNIQUE (project, study_name, trial_id, key)
) STRICT;

-- Artifacts: separate table (different access pattern, file references)
CREATE TABLE artifacts (
    project TEXT NOT NULL,
    study_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    trial_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    run_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    timestamp_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,
    seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
    key TEXT NOT NULL,
    context TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    filename TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    UNIQUE (project, study_name, trial_id, run_id, seq)
) STRICT;

-- Sweep provenance (unchanged)
CREATE TABLE sweep_meta (
    project TEXT NOT NULL,
    study_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    trial_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    timestamp_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,
    seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
    git_hash TEXT,
    config TEXT,
    UNIQUE (project, study_name, trial_id, seq)
) STRICT;

-- Trial lifecycle marker (unchanged)
CREATE TABLE trial_end (
    project TEXT NOT NULL,
    study_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    trial_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    timestamp_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,
    seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (project, study_name, trial_id, seq)
) STRICT;
```

### Key design decisions (locked)

1. **Context storage**: JSON TEXT column. Always serialize with `json.dumps(context, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))` in the tracker — single chokepoint.
2. **Unified values table**: scalar + json only. Artifacts separate. value_type CHECK constraint enforces column consistency.
3. **Params separate table**: UNIQUE on (project, study_name, trial_id, key) with INSERT OR REPLACE for upsert. Params JOINed as pseudo-dimensions at query time.
4. **step as reserved INTEGER column**: nullable, indexable. Not privileged (context still carries seed/fold/etc), but first-class for the 80% "loss vs step" query. step IS NULL = non-time-series value.
5. **run_id column**: assigned per tracker instantiation. Included in UNIQUE. Fixes multi-seed/re-run/concurrent-writer collisions.
6. **Fresh start migration**: drop old tables, create new schema, bump PRAGMA user_version to 2.
7. **Secondary indexes**: (project, study_name, key) and (project, study_name, key, step) on tracked_values.

### Tracker API

```python
tracker.log_value("loss", 0.32, step=100, context={"seed": 3})
tracker.log_value("test_accuracy", 0.91)  # step IS NULL = non-time-series
tracker.log_value("confusion_matrix", {...})  # dict → json storage
tracker.log_artifact("plot.png", "/path/to/plot.png", context={"seed": 3})
tracker.log_param("lr", 0.01)  # unchanged, upserts
```

Type inference rules (in order):
1. Check bool BEFORE int (isinstance(True, int) is True)
2. Coerce numpy types: np.float64 → float, np.int32 → int via numbers.Real/numbers.Integral or explicit float()/int()
3. Handle NaN/Inf: coerce to NULL with a warning, or sanitize at serialization
4. int/float → value_type='scalar', scalar_val
5. dict/list → value_type='json', text_val (json.dumps)
6. str → not supported in log_value (use log_result or wrap in dict)

### Envelope changes

The JSONL envelope must carry the unified payload. New shape:

```python
class ValueEvent(TypedDict, total=False):
    key: str
    value: float | str  # scalar value or JSON string
    step: int | None
    context: dict  # arbitrary dimensions

class Envelope(TypedDict, total=False):
    project: str
    study_name: str
    trial_id: int
    run_id: int  # NEW
    timestamp_ns: int
    seq: int
    value: ValueEvent       # replaces metric + result
    param: ParamEvent       # unchanged
    artifact: ArtifactEvent # now carries context
    sweep_meta: SweepMetaEvent
    trial_end: TrialEndEvent
```

### Files to modify

1. `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/store.py` — new schema, new insert dispatch
2. `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/http.py` — no endpoint changes, but MAX_ROWS may need increasing
3. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/envelope.py` — new envelope shapes
4. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/tracker.py` — new API (log_value, log_artifact with context, log_param unchanged)
5. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/jsonl_io.py` — may need updates for new envelope
6. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/stream_client.py` — no changes (ships envelopes generically)
7. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/batch_sync.py` — artifact sync path cleanup (issue .2 overlaps)
8. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/runner.py` — run_id assignment
9. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/trial_environment.py` — run_id propagation
10. All test files under `tests/unit/tracking/` — update for new API
11. `example/trial.py` — update to new API
close_reason: Implemented context-dimension tracking model: unified tracked_values table, run_id, context JSON, fresh-start migration (user_version=2), params upsert. One documented deviation to the CHECK scalar branch to resolve the NaN-vs-NULL contradiction.

title: Design analysis/exploration layer
description:
Design how analysis and monitoring work on top of the context-dimension model. Two distinct use cases:

1. MONITORING — 'is my job alive, is training diverging, show me that artifact' — real-time, glanceable, high-frequency. Open → scan → close.

2. ANALYSIS — 'which trials should I care about, how does this compare to last week' — post-hoc, comparative, exploratory. Explore → drill → compare → decide.

Key constraint: must not become a maintenance burden. The old React SPA (jernerics-dashboard) was a full frontend stack — too heavy.

Direction from research:
- Grafana Metrics Drilldown pattern: queryless exploration where the data's own structure IS the navigation (discover dimensions from data, show breakdowns per label value, click to filter)
- No pre-declaration needed — dimension-type heuristics infer role (numeric monotonic → x-axis candidate, low cardinality → grouping, etc.)
- Grafana itself is a poor fit (Prometheus cardinality, time-as-x-axis assumption, wrong query patterns)
- Start with /query (SQL endpoint) before building any UI

Options to evaluate:
A. Start with no dashboard — analysis via notebook/CLI against /query
B. Build minimal exploration tool later (lightweight, not full SPA)
C. Use Grafana for live monitoring only (thin exporter for active runs)
close_reason: Design completed. Decisions: (1) Analysis functions query Store directly, no decoupling layer. (2) Generic computational primitives (first→last, change, early/recent slope), not ML-specific assertions like 'plateaued'. (3) Three CLI commands: jernerics runs, summary, diff. watch deferred. (4) All params shown, no filtering. (5) rich for formatting. (6) Every metric treated identically — no semantic grouping. (7) Slope windows: first 10% vs last 10%, min 5 points, step ranges in header. (8) diff uses final values only, not trajectory shape. (9) --json flag for agent consumption, same data, raw values (not human-formatted). (10) Agent guidance to dig deeper lives in skill, not tool logic.

title: Implement observability CLI (runs, summary, diff)
description:
## Context

Design completed (jernerics-jyl.4, now closed). This task implements the three CLI commands.

## Deliverables

### 1. `jernerics/observability/` module

```
src/jernerics/observability/
    __init__.py
    analysis.py    # query Store, compute primitives
    render.py      # rich tables for runs/summary/diff
```

**analysis.py** — functions that query the Store directly:

- `get_all_runs(store)` → list of run summaries (study_name, trial_id, status, step range, duration, all params, final value of priority metrics)
- `get_run_summary(store, study_name, trial_id)` → full run detail (params dict, per-metric analysis, artifacts)
- `get_run_diff(store, run_a, run_b)` → param diff + metric final-value comparison
- `compute_slope(steps, values, window_start, window_end)` → mean slope over a step range
- `compute_metric_analysis(store, study_name, trial_id, key)` → {first, last, change, early_slope, recent_slope, early_range, recent_range, n_points}

**Slope computation:** first 10% of logged steps vs last 10%. Min 5 points required — if fewer, skip slopes. Step ranges shown in headers (e.g., "Slope [0-500]").

**Metric selection:** all metrics treated identically. No semantic grouping. Sorted alphabetically. No special-casing of lr, val_, etc.

**Priority metric for runs table:** try ["loss", "error", "accuracy", "r2"] in order, use first match. If none match, omit the column.

**Param formatting:** show all params. No filtering. Format large numbers human-readably in text mode (35770381 → 35.8M), raw in JSON mode.

### 2. CLI commands (in `src/jernerics/cli.py`)

Three new typer commands:

```python
@app.command("runs")
def runs(...): ...

@app.command("summary")
def summary(run_id: str, json_output: bool = False): ...

@app.command("diff")
def diff(run_a: str, run_b: str, json_output: bool = False): ...
```

- All support `--json` flag (same data, raw values, no human formatting)
- All use `load_tracking_server(project_dir)` for server connection (same pattern as existing commands)
- All use `rich` for text rendering (Table, Console)
- run_id is "study_name" or "study_name:trial_id" (default trial_id=0)

**Output layouts:**

`jernerics runs`:
```
RUN           STATUS      STEPS   LOSS     DURATION  CREATED   PARAMS
symlab-131    completed   5000    0.854    4m        2h ago    batch_size=64 d_ff=2048 d_model=512 ...
                                                    lambda_=0.01 lr=3e-4 max_inputs=2 max_ops=3 ...
```

`jernerics summary <run>`:
```
Run symlab-131
  status: completed    steps: 0-4999    duration: 234.8s

  Params (17):
    batch_size=64  d_model=512  lambda_=0.01  ...

  Metrics:
  Metric          First     Last      Change      Slope [0-500]      Slope [4500-4999]
  ce_loss          2.656    0.707    -1.95       -0.004/step         +0.0001/step
  loss             2.914    0.854    -2.06       -0.004/step         -0.0001/step
  ...

  Artifacts:
    model.pt
```

`jernerics diff <a> <b>`:
```

Run B: symlab-127  (completed, 5000 steps)

Params that differ:
  lambda_           0.01          ->    0.0

Params that match (16):
  batch_size=64  d_model=512  ...

Metric              A (Last)    B (Last)    Change
ce_loss              0.707       0.707       0.000
loss                 0.854       0.854       0.000
```

### 3. Skill update

Update `skills/jernerics/SKILL.md`:
- Add observability commands to CLI surface table
- Add "observability", "summary", "diff" to trigger words

Create `skills/jernerics/references/observability.md`:
- Document the three commands and their --json flag
- Agent guidance: after getting summary, check slope ratios. If early/recent ratio > 10x, the metric behavior changed significantly during training — consider pulling raw series via /query before drawing conclusions
- When to use summary vs raw SQL: summary for quick lookups and comparisons, raw SQL for custom analysis the summary doesn't cover

### 4. Tests

`tests/unit/observability/test_analysis.py`:
- Synthetic Store with known metrics
- Verify slope computation on linear and flat data
- Verify first/last/change extraction
- Verify min-points guard (skip slopes when fewer than 5 points)
