title: Hierarchical jernerics config resolution across nested pyproject.toml
description:
## Problem

`find_pyproject_dir()` walks up from cwd and stops at the FIRST pyproject.toml. In uv workspaces with experiment subpackages (e.g. symlab/experiments/probe/pyproject.toml), this shadows the project root and breaks:

- Project name resolution (gets "probe" instead of "symlab")
- `cache_dir()` paths (~/.cache/jernerics/probe/ instead of symlab/)
- Tracking server URL (not found → empty → "Request URL missing protocol")
- `[tool.jernerics]` backend config lookup

## Root cause

`config.py::find_pyproject_dir()` returns the nearest pyproject.toml, not the one that owns jernerics config.

## Design: hierarchical config

Implement a merge-based config system:

1. **Root detection** — the topmost pyproject.toml containing `[tool.jernerics]` is the root. Project name always comes from root.
2. **Deep merge** — nested pyproject.toml files with `[tool.jernerics]` override root settings. E.g. experiments/probe/pyproject.toml can override `backends.hpc.remote_dir` without redefining the full config.
3. **Backward compatible** — if no nested `[tool.jernerics]` exists, behavior is unchanged.

## Touchpoints

- `config.py` — `find_pyproject_dir()`, `get_project_name()`, config loading
- `paths.py` — `cache_dir()` uses project name
- All callers of `find_pyproject_dir()`

## Symlab-side (separate, no beads task)

After the jernerics fix lands, remove unnecessary pyproject.toml from experiment subpackages OR add `[tool.jernerics]` overrides where experiment-specific config makes sense.

## Test plan

- Unit: nested pyproject with/without [tool.jernerics], deep merge correctness, root detection
- Integration: run `jernerics logs`, `jernerics runs` from a nested experiment dir — resolves root config correctly

title: Design analysis/exploration layer based on dogfooding findings
Live ship stalls on prefix batch when trial snapshot lands after execution start
description:
## Problem

`TrialEnvironment.start()` writes `execution_start` as the FIRST event of a trial's JSONL (trial_environment.py:81); the trial snapshot is emitted later (runner.py:116, after search-space suggestion and config write). `StreamClient` closes its batch window between those two writes under CPU load, ships the prefix batch `[execution_start(+resolved_config)]`, and the server rejects it permanently:

`HTTP 409: execution <id> references unknown trial <id>`

`_ship_batch` (stream_client.py:156-211) retries the SAME frozen request body with backoff — it never rescans the file to extend the batch with the events that would satisfy validation — until `flush_timeout` (60s) leaves everything for replay. Live materialization never happens; the post-hook replay is the only thing that lands the data.

## Reproduction

`python3 -m pytest tests/e2e/test_tracking_v3.py::TestSubmissionEvents::test_first_trial_materializes_live_without_replay -q`

Under CPU load (concurrent agent sessions/builds) this fails deterministically: 409 retry storm, ~122s runtime (two 60s flush timeouts), then `assert rows["trials"] == 1` sees 0. On a quiet machine it passes in ~3s (single whole-file batch; the server accepts execution-before-snapshot WITHIN a batch — passing runs prove batch-scoped validation).

Verified pre-existing: fails 3/3 at clean HEAD (9f1b0f0) with the working tree fully stashed, under load. Also fails with an unrelated Slurm-rendering change applied and with it reverted — tree state is irrelevant; machine load decides.

## Fix directions (design decision required)

- (a) In `_ship_batch`'s retry loop, on validation 409 rescan the file and rebuild/extend the batch body instead of retrying the frozen one. The window-phase rescan (stream_client.py:131-147) only covers writes during the window, not during retries.
- (b) Emit the trial snapshot before `execution_start` in the runner lifecycle (needs tracker available before environment start / snapshot with pre-ask state).
- (c) Server-side deferred reference validation.

## Impact

`just test` (Definition of Done gate) fails under load. Live tracking v3's core promise — facts queryable live without replay — silently degrades to replay-only when the race hits.
close_reason: Fixed by 4c912a8: shipper rescans before closing the batch window (stream_client.py:143-157) and regrows the batch when the server names an unmet ordering precondition (_regrow_for_validation, stream_client.py:198-201, 227-246). Unit suite tests/unit/tracking/test_stream_client.py green (24 passed, 2026-08-30).

description:
User report: in the Overview sweeps-in-scope grid, clicking a row scrolls the page back to the top.

Root cause chain:
1. _render_overview (callbacks.py:924) replaces all workspace-overview children whenever the content digest changes; it fires on every view-store change and every 5s poll tick.
2. The digest (overview_content -> _content_digest(children)) includes relative_time() strings, which tick at second granularity under a minute ("37s ago") and minute granularity under an hour. With any sweep activity newer than an hour the digest churns and the whole region, including overview-sweep-grid, is remounted.
3. Remounting destroys the focused ag-grid cell; Chromium then resets window scroll to top. The scroll-restore-store clientside pair (callbacks.py:1566-1622) saves scroll on every poll but only restores when analysis-refresh-store changes (manual refresh button), so this path is uncovered.

Fix directions (any or all): compute the digest over canonical facts excluding volatile relative-time strings; restore saved scroll after overview re-renders; patch volatile cells in place instead of replacing the region.

Acceptance: with a sweep active in the last minute, clicking a row far down the grid keeps scroll position and opens the inspector; poll refreshes never reset scroll.
close_reason: Completed: overview digest excludes volatile strings so fact-unchanged ticks never remount the region; scroll-restore clientside now also fires on workspace-overview children re-renders (double-rAF). Proofs: 6e00223, 26be22a, 935dd39; full suite 1896 passed.

title: sbatch rejection is swallowed: failed submission exits 0 with empty job ids
description:
## Problem
`_compose_chain` (packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/slurm/adapter.py:178-192) submits via `ARRAY_JOB_ID=$(sbatch --parsable <<'EOF' ...) ; CHECKER_JOB_ID=$(sbatch --parsable --dependency=... <<'EOF' ...)` and finally `echo "$ARRAY_JOB_ID $CHECKER_JOB_ID"`. When sbatch rejects the script (unknown directive, bad partition/account, scheduler policy), stderr carries the error but the composed script still exits 0 with both variables empty. The CLI then prints monitor hints with blank ids and returns success.

Observed live: a submission whose generated script contained `#SBATCH --target=3200` (see companion issue jernerics-ykh) synced, printed `jernerics job logs --backend hpc --follow` with no id, exit 0, nothing in squeue. Any sbatch-level rejection is currently indistinguishable from success until the user notices the missing job.

Same bug class exists in `submit_job` (adapter.py:362-380, build-job path): `BUILD_JOB_ID=$(sbatch ...)` + `echo $BUILD_JOB_ID` — failure also exits 0 with an empty id. The non-chain path in `submit_sweep` (adapter.py:303-318) already checks returncode correctly; only the chain and build paths swallow.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Submit any sweep whose directives include an invalid sbatch flag (easiest via the --set leak from jernerics-ykh).
2. Observe exit 0, empty job ids in the monitor output, no queue entry.

## Locked Design (confirmed with user 2026-08-27)

All changes in `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/slurm/adapter.py` plus one except-branch in `commands/execution.py`.

1. **Fail the composed script on submission failure.** In `_compose_chain`, the exit status of a plain `VAR=$(cmd)` assignment is the command substitution's exit status, so:
   - `ARRAY_JOB_ID=$(sbatch --parsable <<'EOF' ... EOF)` gets `|| { echo "array job submission failed" >&2; exit 1; }`
   - additionally guard emptiness: `[ -n "$ARRAY_JOB_ID" ] || { echo "array job submission failed (empty job id)" >&2; exit 1; }`
   - same two guards for `CHECKER_JOB_ID`; its failure message must include the already-queued array id so the user can scancel: `checker submission failed; array job $ARRAY_JOB_ID already queued`
   - inner sbatch stderr already propagates to the outer bash's stderr, which `host.run(..., capture_output=True)` captures — no temp files needed; verify this in tests.
2. **Same guards in `submit_job`** for `BUILD_JOB_ID`.
3. **New exception**: `class SlurmSubmitError(RuntimeError)` at module level in adapter.py (project convention: descriptive module-level exceptions).
4. **Python-side validation in `submit_sweep`** (chain path, adapter.py:320-336) and `submit_job`: parse the printed id(s); each must match `^(\d+)(;\S+)?$` (parsable output is `<id>` or `<id>;cluster`); strip nothing — validate, keep the full string as job_id. Empty/non-numeric → raise `SlurmSubmitError` including `result.stderr.strip()`. Existing `returncode != 0` checks now raise `SlurmSubmitError` instead of `RuntimeError` (same message text).
5. **Exit-code mapping** in `commands/execution.py` `run_remote` (~line 205): add `except SlurmSubmitError as e:` BEFORE the existing `(RuntimeError, ValueError)` catch → `print(f"Error: {e}")` + `raise SystemExit(ExitCode.SLURM_ERROR) from None`. Verify no intermediate layer (`backend.prepare_and_submit` → `submission.submit_sweep`) re-wraps exceptions as plain RuntimeError; if one does, preserve the type there.

Note: jernerics-ykh's render-time allowlist (validated in `_render_overrides`, which dry-run also exercises) separately catches unknown directive keys before submission. This issue is the safety net for rejections an allowlist cannot predict (bad account, scheduler policy, partition limits).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Regression tests in `packages/jernerics/tests/unit/backend/test_slurm_adapter.py` (follow existing fake-host conventions):
  - chain submit where the fake host returns rc 0, empty stdout, stderr containing an sbatch error → `SlurmSubmitError` raised, message contains the stderr text
  - checker-fails-after-array-succeeds → `SlurmSubmitError`, message names the queued array job id
  - happy path unchanged: numeric ids parsed, SubmitResult carries array + checker submissions
  - `submit_job` with failing sbatch → `SlurmSubmitError`; non-numeric stdout → `SlurmSubmitError`
- CLI mapping test (tests/unit/commands/): `run_remote` with a failing backend exits with code 4 (`ExitCode.SLURM_ERROR`)
- `just lint`, `just format-check`, `just typecheck`, `just test` all pass

## Scheduling
Land before jernerics-ykh (both edit adapter.py). No formal dependency — the fixes are logically independent.
close_reason: Implemented: SlurmSubmitError(RuntimeError) + _validate_job_id in slurm/adapter.py; || { ...; exit 1; } and [ -n "$VAR" ] guards on ARRAY/CHECKER/BUILD_JOB_ID (checker msg names queued array id); all three returncode raises converted; execution.py maps to ExitCode.SLURM_ERROR(4) before the RuntimeError branch. Verified: 7 new adapter tests + CLI exit-4 test (54 targeted pass), composed chain executed under real bash with stubbed sbatch (array-fail rc1+stderr propagate, checker-fail names id 10001, happy '10001 10002', empty-id rc1), just lint/format-check/typecheck pass.

title: Dashboard-wide: long values overflow or clip with no consistent truncation strategy
description:
User report: the dashboard is hard to read because many values are horizontally long and overflow frequently.

Partial mitigations already exist: .surface horizontal scroll (dashboard.css, jernerics-jum), .fact-row flex-wrap, grid wrappers min-width 0. Still clipped with no signal: monitoring summary strings in overview grid cells (workspace.py _monitoring_summary, "active 2 . quiet 1 . stale 3 ..."), failure summaries in the inspector (workspace.py:684), long value keys in Points/Params column headers (analysis.py:1598), and JSON payloads.

AG Grid default cells clip without ellipsis or wrap, so readers cannot tell content is truncated and cannot retrieve it.

Fix direction: one shared policy — clamp with ellipsis plus title tooltip as baseline; wrap or expand where full content matters (see the point-values issue); cap column widths; keep enableCellTextSelection so identifiers stay copyable.

Acceptance: no dashboard surface blows out the horizontal layout; every clipped cell signals truncation and offers the full value via tooltip or expansion.
close_reason: Completed: one shared policy (clamp_text/clamp_tooltip/clamped_column in components.py) + CSS baseline (ellipsis + hover title on clipped ag-cells/fact rows, overflow-wrap anywhere, capped column widths) applied to grid cells, headers, monitoring summaries. Proofs: 497dcce; full suite 1896 passed.

title: Retried trials lose server_addr — tracking streams fail on retry
description:
## Problem

When a trial is retried (via the checker/heartbeat mechanism), the retry context (`ctx.json`) does not persist `server_addr`. The resubmitted trial runs with a schemeless tracking URL, causing `httpx.UnsupportedProtocol: Request URL is missing an 'http://' or 'https://' protocol`.

The fresh-submission path is unaffected — only retried trials lose the tracking server address.

## Reproduction

1. Submit a job to HPC with `JERNERICS_TRACKING_SERVER` set
2. Kill the trial mid-run (or let the heartbeat go stale) to trigger a retry
3. The retried trial's tracking events fail to stream — `Failed to send event, retry 1/2/3...`

## Root cause

The retry context serialization (`ctx.json`) doesn't include `server_addr`, so when the checker resubmits the trial, the env var is missing.

## Fix

Persist `server_addr` in the retry context alongside other fields, and restore it when resubmitting.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 8b436ab

title: Migrate remote E2E tests to tracking v3
description:
## Problem
all six tests in tests/e2e_remote delegate to _helpers.py, which queries retired v2 metrics/trial_end/results tables and calls GET /artifact/{project}/{study}/{trial}/{key} (notably _helpers.py:113-174). The v3 server exposes typed reads and artifact-id PUT/GET only. The skip-gated suite therefore provides zero current signal and would fail when JERNERICS_RUN_REMOTE=1.

## Proposed Change
migrate helpers and assertions to v3 sweep/trial/value/artifact records and current CLI terminology, or delete the suite if real remote acceptance coverage is no longer worth its operational cost. Do not retain a permanently skipped misleading suite.

## Acceptance Criteria
on configured Slurm and Pueue hosts, all six remote tests pass against the co-located v3 server and assert only current schema/routes; otherwise the retired suite and just recipe are removed deliberately.
close_reason: Completed: tests/e2e_remote helpers + all six tests migrated to v3 only (sweeps/trials/tracked_values per-execution join, artifact-id GET /artifact/{id}, sweeps_since timestamp-scoped discovery immune to straggler/replay races; retry ledger verified still current in source and kept). Live evidence: pueue-remote 3/3 pass on scimlab (370s/623s/104s); hpc basic+gpu pass on hpc2 after jernerics-gvs flag fix; hpc test_retry blocked structurally by the container image pinning pre-fix jernerics via example/uv.lock (depth-1 checker renders old flag inside the image) — pin bump + rebuild follow-up recorded; identical helper code passes retry on pueue (no slurm directives). Skip gate intact locally (6 skipped). Merged as 3bbf042 + 3bbde91; just check: 1345 passed.

title: Preserve value attribution across retry replay
description:
## Problem
ValueEvent lacks execution_id. IngestService._resolve_execution attaches it to the currently active execution; replaying an older execution after a retry starts can therefore attach old values to the new execution. Reused key/step tuples then conflict in _apply_value, /ingest returns 409, and batch replay leaves the cursor before the failing batch, blocking later events. This violates CONTEXT.md's live/replay overlap and idempotence guarantee.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. End one execution after it logged a value key/step.
2. Start a retry execution for the same trial and log the same key/step.
3. Replay the older execution's ValueEvent after the retry is active.
4. Observe active-execution attribution, an immutable-value conflict, HTTP 409, and no cursor advance past the failing batch.

## Proposed Change
Design must be locked before implementation: prefer explicit execution identity in the schema; a recorded_at window heuristic is weaker around overlap.

## Acceptance Criteria
replay old-execution values after a retry execution has logged the same key/steps; values remain attributed to the correct execution and later events continue, with any conflict surfaced without permanently poisoning replay progress.
close_reason: Completed: ValueEvent gains optional execution_id (legacy JSON still validates); tracker stamps it on log_value/log_json; ingest honors it after exists+same-trial validation (legacy unstamped -> active-execution fallback unchanged); batch_sync drops conflict-coded 409 events (records ConflictRecord, ratchets cursor, resends remainder) so genuine conflicts never wedge replay — validation-coded 409s keep retry (asktell race regression test). Orchestrator verified the exact bead scenario on a live server: E1 ended, E2 retry active logging same key/steps, E1 replay -> 3 rows attributed to E1 (1.0/2.0/3.0), E2 4 rows, later events continue, no 409. Merged as 09d89c6; just check: 1345 passed, 6 skipped.

title: Blob sweep prunes cache before confirmed server receipt (pyrimel f01 trial 11 full_results lost)
description:
Evidence (pyrimel study pyrimel_roberts2024_f01_20260902-153117, sweep commit e286600, jernerics 1.2.1, apptainer/HPC backend):

- artifacts row for trial 11's full_results exists: artifact_id a095a6e2-5718-46bb-ac27-4d47ac52c1e1, size_bytes 108102, declared via open_artifact spool.
- artifact_blobs has NO row for that id; GET /artifact/a095a6e2... returns 404 while the other 11 trials' blobs fetch fine.
- The HPC cache copy was pruned after the sweep reported success (artifacts/blobs/ empty, events/ pruned), so the blob is unrecoverable; the trial's fronts survive only as tracked_values pareto_front_* JSON.

Suspect: the post-job blob sweep counts an upload as done (and prunes) without the server confirming receipt, or dedupes on a hash it never persisted. Repro window: 12 artifacts, 1 lost (~8%).

title: Fail fast on scheme-less tracking server URL
description:
Validated defect from the atlas cutover: JERNERICS_TRACKING_SERVER=atlas.taile454b.ts.net:443 (v2-era host:port) passes silently through load_tracking_server (config.py:195, env beats pyproject) and every ship then fails late with the cryptic httpx "Request URL is missing an 'http://' or 'https://' protocol." — observed as 66 failures across deploy-time ship, 11 StreamClient retries, blob upload, and post-hook replay for a single-trial sweep.

TARGET: packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/infra.py (resolve_tracking_ship); possibly config.py.

CHANGE: resolve_tracking_ship raises a new module-level exception with a descriptive name (AGENTS convention) when the server value lacks an http:// or https:// prefix; the message names both the JERNERICS_TRACKING_SERVER env var and the [tool.jernerics] tracking_server pyproject key and shows the offending value. load_tracking_server stays permissive (it feeds display/hints); enforcement lives at ship resolution, the chokepoint every shipper passes through. Audit the ship entrypoints — LocalBackend._ship_submission_events, the trial-side tracker/StreamClient resolution, post_hook __main__ --server-addr, tracking replay --server — each must surface the error immediately and cleanly, with no retry loop.

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests per entrypoint with a scheme-less URL: immediate failure naming the env var and key, zero retries; existing tests green; ruff check/format and ty clean.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 7f9659e: TrackingServerSchemeError at resolve_tracking_ship chokepoint; all entrypoints surface immediately; 16 new unit tests; gates green (lint/format/ty, 1199 passed); live repro of scheme-less atlas host:port raises with env var + pyproject key named.

title: Overview roll-up and scope grid include archived and invalid sweeps
description:
User report: the scoped roll-up does not respect the archived status of experiments.

Evidence: queries.sweep_overview (packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/queries.py:1000) selects every sweep in scope — its sel CTE applies no curation filter, unlike _CURRENT_SWEEPS_CTES (queries.py:162) which treats a terminal sweep as current only when neither archived nor invalid. workspace.overview_tab (workspace.py:989) filters summaries only by picked sweeps, so archived/invalid sweeps remain counted in the Scope roll-up and listed in Sweeps in scope.

The Browse tab already implements the intended semantics: browser_sweep_rows (workspace.py:60) hides terminal archived/invalid sweeps unless the include_archived / include_invalid toggles are set, while picked and incomplete sweeps always stay discoverable. The overview region has no such filtering and the include toggles only feed browser rows (callbacks.py:754).

Fix direction: apply the same curation semantics to the overview region — reuse the hidden_curation rule or push the filter into sweep_overview; decide whether the Browse include toggles should govern the overview too (they already round-trip through the scope document).

Acceptance: archiving a terminal sweep removes it from roll-up counts and the scope grid unless include-archived is set; incomplete sweeps remain visible regardless of curation; picked sweeps never disappear.
close_reason: Completed: overview region now honors Browse curation semantics (filter pushed into queries, _CURRENT_SWEEPS_CTES reuse): archived/invalid terminal sweeps excluded from roll-up and scope grid unless include toggles set; incomplete always visible; picked never disappear. Proofs: ef2b0ce; curation tests green, full suite 1896 passed.

title: cache_dir() is not container-aware: resolves to $HOME inside container jobs instead of the /cache bind
description:
OBSERVED FAILURE (pyrimel, 2026-09-01):
Pilot slurm array task 28198623 failed in 9s with ENOSPC: shutil.copytree("/opt/venv/julia_env", ...) wrote ~2GB toward /home/jez21005/.cache/jernerics/pyrimel/julia_env. Home is quota-limited; the intended persistent cache (gpfs scratch, backend cache_dir, 923G free) sat unused, mounted and empty at /cache in the same container.

MECHANISM:
- jernerics/paths.py cache_dir() unconditionally returns Path.home()/.cache/jernerics/<project_name>. It has no is_hpc() branch.
- Its sibling work() IS container-aware: `if is_hpc(): return Path("/work")` (paths.py lines 19-20). cache_dir() lacks the mirrored branch.
- The backend provisions the real cache and hardcodes the mount: backend/path_resolver.py line 59 returns "/cache"; line 94 binds `<backend cache_dir>:/cache` (already project-scoped via the {project_name} template). Project container.def %environment blocks contract against it (e.g. JULIA_DEPOT_PATH=/cache/julia_depot:/opt/julia_depot, PYTHON_JULIAPKG_PROJECT=/cache/julia_env).
- JERNERICS_HPC=1 is exported in exactly one place: the generated sbatch script (backend/slurm/adapter.py line 171). So every internal cache_dir() consumer (backend.py line 510, local_backend.py lines 31+37, commands/*) runs on the orchestrating host where the env is unset and is unaffected - only trial scripts inside container jobs get the wrong path.

HISTORY:
Worked previously - old pyrimal/primel runs left their julia_env/julia_depot seeds on scratch via the /cache contract. A downstream refactor of trial seeding code to cache_dir() drifted the destination to home silently; nothing failed loudly until a fresh project without existing seeds ran.

PROPOSED FIX:
1. paths.cache_dir(): add first branch `if is_hpc(): return Path("/cache")` - NO project-name suffix: the bind is already per-project, and the flat layout matches backend writes (/cache/tracking, /cache/optuna) and container.def contracts.
2. Root-cause hardening: hoist a single CACHE_MOUNT constant imported by both paths.py and backend/path_resolver.py. The bug exists because "/cache" is two independent literals (API-side resolution and backend bind target) that drifted; one constant makes drift impossible.
3. Docstring: document both resolutions (host: ~/.cache/jernerics/<project>; in-container: /cache bind). The existing layout description (optuna/, tracking/, jobs/) describes /cache and becomes accurate in-container after the fix.

TESTS:
- Unit: monkeypatch JERNERICS_HPC=1 -> cache_dir() == Path("/cache"); env unset -> home path. Env is read at call time, so no fixture gymnastics needed.
- Contract: assert PathResolver.cache_prefix() == str(cache_dir()) under is_hpc() - the drift-proof assertion.

BLAST RADIUS:
Zero for jernerics-internal consumers (JERNERICS_HPC is only set inside container jobs). Only in-container trial scripts change behavior - which is the intent. Downstream trial code that already calls cache_dir() becomes correct as written.

DEPLOYMENT NOTE:
jernerics is installed into project container images from git, so reaching jobs requires an image rebuild (jernerics backend build), roughly 15 min on pyrimel.

ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED:
Env var (e.g. JERNERICS_CACHE_DIR=/cache) exported via the tracking env-file alongside JERNERICS_API_KEY - more general (pueue/docker backends, arbitrary mounts) but adds config surface; nothing today mounts cache anywhere but /cache. Revisit if a backend ever binds the cache elsewhere. The work()-style mirror is the established pattern.
close_reason: Implemented per issue recipe: paths.cache_dir() gains first branch is_hpc() -> Path(CACHE_MOUNT) (no project suffix; bind is already project-scoped); single CACHE_MOUNT constant in paths.py now feeds cache_dir(), PathResolver.cache_prefix/bind_args, and the slurm interactive shell bind (third /cache literal found and unified). Docstring documents both host and in-container resolutions. Tests: new tests/unit/test_paths.py (hpc -> /cache, unset -> ~/.cache/jernerics) and contract test in test_path_resolver.py asserting cache_prefix == str(cache_dir()) under JERNERICS_HPC. Verification: 81 affected-file tests pass, full just check green (1847 passed, 6 remote-skipped), smoke test confirms /cache == cache_prefix == bind target under JERNERICS_HPC=1 and unchanged host resolution. Deploy note: needs jernerics backend build (image rebuild) on pyrimel to reach jobs.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
Triage 2026-09-01: verified against code, classification actionable (confirmed live bug).

CONFIRMED: paths.py:25-41 cache_dir() has no is_hpc() branch while sibling work() does (paths.py:19-20). PathResolver.cache_prefix returns "/cache" for containerized runs (path_resolver.py:56-59) and bind_args binds {cache_host}:/cache (path_resolver.py:91-95). JERNERICS_HPC=1 exported in exactly one place, the generated sbatch script (slurm/adapter.py:212; issue cited 171 — line drift only, substance correct). Fix per proposal is safe against existing coverage: test_config.py:580 asserts the host-side path and runs with the env unset, stays green.

Priority raised P2 -> P1: observed production failure (ENOSPC after 9s, ~2GB into quota-limited home), silent drift, affects every fresh slurm container project.

SCOPE NOTE for implementer: pueue adapter renders its own scripts and never exports JERNERICS_HPC (checked backend/pueue/adapter.py _render_script). The work()-style mirror heals slurm container jobs only; pueue+container trial scripts calling cache_dir() would still resolve to home. Matches the tradeoff already documented under ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED — no clarification needed, but if pueue+container is an active usage mode the env-var route closes both at once.

title: job logs --follow exits immediately even while the job is running
description:
Repro (pyrimel consumer, job RUNNING on hpc2):
  $ jernerics job list --backend hpc   -> 28148821 RUNNING
  $ timeout 20 jernerics job logs --backend hpc 28148821 --follow
  prints a snapshot, exits 0 after ~4s. No streaming.

Root cause (primary) — backend/slurm/adapter.py get_logs follow branch (~line 683):
  n_trials == 1 forces effective_array_index = 1 (line ~635), so
  status_job_id = f'{base_job_id}_1' — an ARRAY id. Build jobs are plain
  sbatch jobs, not arrays: squeue -j 28148821_1 and sacct -j 28148821_1
  both fail, get_status returns None, and wait_for_completion treats None
  as 'job unknown -> return True' (line ~593). It returns instantly, the
  finally block terminates the tail process, follow ends after one SSH
  round trip. Affects every non-array job (builds at minimum).

Secondary defects in the same branch (fix together):
1. sp.Popen(['ssh', ..., 'tail', '-f', log]) — plain tail -f shows only
   the LAST 10 lines; follow should stream from the start (tail -n +1 -f).
2. After wait_for_completion returns, tail_proc.terminate() fires with no
   drain grace — final buffered output can be lost; also no indication the
   job ended.
3. If the job is ALREADY terminal when --follow starts, wait returns
   instantly and the same terminate() races the dump — should cat the
   full log and exit deterministically.
4. Wildcard log_file branch (~line 651): --follow silently degrades to a
   single cat unless the pattern contains %a — any wildcard + follow
   should error and ask for --array-index.

Acceptance criteria:
- follow on a RUNNING non-array job streams output from the beginning and
  keeps streaming until the job reaches a terminal state, then drains,
  prints an end marker, and exits.
- follow on an already-terminal job prints the complete log and exits.
- follow with an unresolvable wildcard pattern errors with guidance.
- status polling must resolve the correct id: plain jobs by base id,
  array jobs as base_index (squeue/sacct behavior differs; probe base id
  first, fall back to base_index).
- unit tests in packages/jernerics/tests/unit/backend/ covering: running
  non-array job (mock host + mock subprocess.Popen; assert tail -n +1 -f
  argv, wait_for_completion called with base id), terminal job (full cat,
  no tail), wildcard + follow error. wait_for_completion's terminal-state
  set should be shared with get_logs (module-level constant).

Related: jernerics-342 (same consumer session; remote_dir template bug).
close_reason: get_logs --follow: SLURM_TERMINAL_STATES shared constant; _resolve_status_job probes base id first then base_index (plain jobs no longer polled as arrays); tail -n +1 -f with pump thread streams from start; terminate-then-drain keeps the end marker last with no output loss; terminal/purged jobs cat the full log; wildcard+follow errors with --array-index guidance. Merged as 33b5613 (commits e0f6bca..03f13bf). Verified: 368 backend unit tests green in worktree, full suite 1844 passed on merged main. Field check: follow on a RUNNING non-array job on hpc2.

title: job logs --array-index/-i is accepted then silently discarded; --follow error tells user to pass the flag they just passed
description:
REPRO (jernerics 1.1.2, slurm backend):
  jernerics job logs -b hpc -f -i 1 <job-id>
  -> Error: --follow requires --array-index to select a single log file

The user DID pass --array-index/-i. Reproduced twice: with an array job id and with the checker/post-hook id (array_id+1, the id job list surfaces).

ROOT CAUSE:
- commands/jobs.py logs() declares array_index (typer.Option "--array-index", "-i", lines 122-125) but the call at lines 135-140 passes only job_id, follow, stderr, local_cache_dir. The flag is parsed then silently discarded.
- backend/slurm/adapter.py get_logs() (line 632) has no array_index parameter. The array index is derived solely from an "_N" suffix embedded in the job id string (lines 660-661). No suffix + n_trials != 1 -> effective index None -> pattern expands with a wildcard -> the misleading error at lines 680-685.

SECONDARY: following the checker job id resolves against the array log pattern (%A_%a) and can never locate checker_%j.out - the post-hook sbatch uses a different output pattern.

WORKAROUND (works, verified): pass the task-suffixed job id:
  jernerics job logs -b hpc -f 28201616_1

PROPOSED FIX:
1. Pass array_index through the get_logs call chain; when provided, prefer it over id-suffix parsing (and keep the suffix path working).
2. Keep the wildcard error only for the genuinely ambiguous case (no index from any source); message should not instruct the user to pass a flag that is already passed.
3. Optional: resolve checker/post-hook jobs to checker_%j.out instead of the array pattern.

EVIDENCE: reproduced against a live slurm backend (UConn HPC2, apptainer container); workaround command streamed trial-0 stderr correctly.
close_reason: Completed: --array-index threads through jobs.py -> Backend -> SchedulerAdapter -> SlurmAdapter (explicit index beats _N suffix); wildcard error fires only when truly ambiguous; checker jobs resolve checker_%j.out. Proofs: 8d4b064; test_slurm_adapter/test_backend/test_pueue_adapter/test_adapter/test_cli green (221), full suite 1896 passed.

title: logs --follow blocks indefinitely, agents resort to sleep loops
description:
## Problem

`jernerics logs --backend hpc <job_id> --follow` blocks the terminal until the job reaches a terminal state. For Slurm, it spawns `tail -f` via SSH and calls `wait_for_completion(poll_interval=10)` internally — it does return when the job finishes, but:

1. It blocks for the entire job duration (could be hours)
2. Agent sessions with timeouts get killed mid-follow
3. The SSH tail connection can drop, leaving the process hanging
4. Agents can't do other work while blocked

As a result, agents (OMP, Hermes) skip `--follow` entirely and resort to `sleep N && jernerics jobs --backend hpc` polling loops. This is wasteful and fragile.

## Current behavior

```
# After jernerics run, the CLI prints:
#   jernerics logs --backend hpc <job_id> --follow

# But agents do this instead:
sleep 30 && jernerics jobs --backend hpc
sleep 60 && jernerics jobs --backend hpc
# ... repeat until COMPLETED
```

## Proposed solution

Add a `--wait` / `--timeout` option to `jernerics logs` (or a new `jernerics wait` command) that:

- Polls job status at a configurable interval (default 10s)
- Returns immediately if the job is already in a terminal state
- Returns with exit code 0 if COMPLETED, non-zero if FAILED or TIMEOUT
- Accepts `--timeout <seconds>` — returns after N seconds if job hasn't finished yet, printing partial logs
- Does NOT spawn `tail -f` — instead polls log content incrementally and prints new lines since last poll

This would let agents do:
```
jernerics wait --backend hpc <job_id> --timeout 60  # poll for 60s
# ... do other work ...
jernerics wait --backend hpc <job_id> --timeout 60  # poll again
```

Or just:
```
jernerics wait --backend hpc <job_id>  # blocks until done, no timeout
```

The difference from `--follow` is that `--wait` uses polling internally (resilient to SSH drops) and supports `--timeout` for bounded waits.
close_reason: Implemented in commit bf10602

title: Artifact row-click navigates to artifact-view/undefined (getRowId never evaluated)
description:
Browser walkthrough on atlas (2026-08-21) + local mounted-harness repro on main 38e079a: clicking a row in the artifact listing (trial and execution pages, artifact-grid) fires cellClicked with rowId="undefined" and callbacks._open_artifact navigates to /dashboard/artifact-view/undefined, which renders the missing-object dead end ("No artifact matches undefined"). The only interactive path into the artifact viewer is broken; direct viewer URLs still work.

Root cause (two layers):
1. artifacts.py artifact_grid passes getRowId="params => params.data.artifact_id" as a top-level prop, but dash-ag-grid 35.3.0 only evaluates inline JS-string props when dangerously_allow_code=True (dashboard sets it nowhere). Without evaluation, AG Grid assigns no row ids and the wrapper serializes cellClicked.rowId as the string "undefined". Fix: either set dangerously_allow_code=True on the artifact grid or use the documented safer form getRowId={"function": ...} backed by a registered function in assets (see dash.plotly.com/dash-ag-grid/row-ids and /javascript-and-the-grid).
2. callbacks._open_artifact trusts click["rowId"] verbatim. Add a UUID-parse guard (raise PreventUpdate on non-UUID) so garbage can never navigate.

Test gap: tests/e2e/test_dashboard_journeys.py asserts getRowId statically on the rendered layout (_ARTIFACT_ROW_ID) and adds viewer_href to the expected link set, but never executes a browser click, so it cannot catch this. Extend the journey suite (or the mounted smoke) with a real cellClicked round-trip asserting the payload rowId is the artifact UUID.

Verified on: https://atlas.taile454b.ts.net (dash-ag-grid 35.3.0, dash 4.4.1 — same pins as repo) and locally on main via /tmp/jhe1-check harness pattern.
close_reason: Fixed in 8a16c0b (merged to main): registered-function getRowId (assets/dashAgGridFunctions.js, expression form jernericsArtifactRowId(params) verified against the dash-ag-grid 35.3.0 bundle) + UUID guard in _open_artifact + 3 new e2e round-trip tests (TestArtifactRowClickNavigation, shown failing pre-fix). Independently verified by orchestrator: full gates green (1218 passed on re-run), real browser clicks on worktree-mounted harness — trial AND execution pages both sent cellClicked rowId=<real UUID> and navigated to /dashboard/artifact-view/<hex-no-dashes> with content rendering.

title: After jernerics run, print tracking server query example
description:
## Problem

After `jernerics run` submits a job, it prints:
```
Monitor progress:
  jernerics logs --backend hpc <job_id> --follow
```

But this only helps with logs. There's no hint about how to check tracking data (metrics, params, artifacts). New users don't know they can query the tracking server.

## Proposed solution

After submission, also print:
```
Track metrics:
  curl -X POST <server>/query -d '{"sql": "SELECT * FROM tracked_values ORDER BY timestamp_ns DESC LIMIT 5"}'
```

Or better, add a `jernerics metrics <job_id>` command that wraps the curl.

title: Script-as-trial: new trial context API (trial_config, trial_tracker, is_job, ConsoleTracker)
description:
## Scope

Create a NEW module that provides the script-as-trial API. This is purely additive — do NOT modify the runner or existing trial execution path. Nothing existing should break.

## CRITICAL: No backward compatibility

This task is part of a breaking change. Do NOT add any backward compatibility shims, legacy function import fallbacks, or deprecation warnings. The old `def trial(config, tracker)` pattern will be removed in a subsequent task. This task only adds the new API.

## API

New module: `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/trial_context.py`

### is_job() -> bool
- Returns `True` if `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` env var is set
- This means the script is running as a scheduled job via jernerics runner
- Returns `False` when running standalone (e.g., `python trial.py`)

### trial_config(defaults: dict | None = None) -> dict
- **Job mode** (`is_job()` is True): reads JSON from `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` env var, returns parsed dict
- **Standalone mode** (`is_job()` is False): returns the `defaults` dict as-is
- Raises `RuntimeError` if job mode but env var points to missing/unreadable file
- Raises `ValueError` if standalone mode and `defaults` is None

### trial_tracker() -> Tracker | ConsoleTracker
- **Job mode:** returns a real `Tracker` configured from env vars (same env vars the runner already sets for the current tracker — check `tracking/trial_environment.py` for what is available)
- **Standalone mode:** returns a `ConsoleTracker` that prints to stdout

### ConsoleTracker class
Implements the same protocol as the real Tracker:
- `log_param(key: str, value: str) -> None` — prints `param: key=value`
- `log_value(key: str, value: float, step: int) -> None` — prints `[step N] key=value`
- `log_text(key: str, value: str) -> None` — prints `[text] key=value`
- `finish(results: dict[str, Any]) -> None` — prints a summary block with all results

### TrackerProtocol (for type annotations)
```python
class TrackerProtocol(Protocol):
    def log_param(self, key: str, value: str) -> None: ...
    def log_value(self, key: str, value: float, step: int) -> None: ...
    def log_text(self, key: str, value: str) -> None: ...
    def finish(self, results: dict[str, Any]) -> None: ...
```

## Env var contract

The runner (in a future task) will set `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` before executing the trial script. For this task, just implement the reading logic — do not modify the runner.

Check `tracking/trial_environment.py` to see what tracker env vars already exist. The real tracker in job mode should be constructed the same way the current `trial()` function receives its tracker.

## Exports

Export from `jernerics/__init__.py`:
```python
from .trial_context import is_job, trial_config, trial_tracker
```

## Tests

Create `packages/jernerics/tests/unit/test_trial_context.py`:
- `is_job()` returns True/False based on env var presence
- `trial_config()` reads JSON in job mode
- `trial_config()` returns defaults in standalone mode
- `trial_config()` raises when standalone and no defaults
- `trial_config()` raises when job mode but file missing
- `trial_tracker()` returns ConsoleTracker in standalone mode
- `trial_tracker()` returns Tracker in job mode (mock env vars)
- ConsoleTracker prints to stdout for all methods
- ConsoleTracker.finish prints summary

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `trial_context.py` module created with all functions
- [ ] `ConsoleTracker` implemented with same interface as Tracker
- [ ] `TrackerProtocol` defined for type annotations
- [ ] Functions exported from `jernerics/__init__.py`
- [ ] Tests pass
- [ ] No existing code modified (purely additive)
close_reason: Completed: commit 35c3466. trial_context.py with is_job, trial_config, trial_tracker, ConsoleTracker. 10 tests, 626 total passing.

title: Make grid a self-contained deterministic sweep mode
description:
Context: sweep configs using `grid` must also define a `search_space` that re-declares every grid axis via suggest_categorical. Downstream evidence (pyrimel experiments/configs/roberts2024_f*.py, 21 files): each value list appears twice (grid + suggest choices) plus two name sets (grid key vs config key).

MECHANISM (current):
- config.py load_config stores grid; backend/local_backend.py and backend/command_builders.py enqueue every cartesian combo via study.enqueue_trial; runner.py run_trial reads params ONLY via `params = sweep.search_space(trial) if sweep.search_space else {}`. With grid but no search_space, enqueued values are never read and every trial runs plain base.
- grid keys must match suggest names exactly; drift fails silently.

VERIFIED FAILURE MODES (optuna 4.x, journal storage, public API only):
1. Grid axis never suggested: 6 enqueued combos, 6 asks, only 2 distinct configs. Silent duplicates - grid stops deduplicating, the exact bug it exists to prevent.
2. Explicit n_trials != product: loader auto-adjusts only when n_trials == 1 (config.py lines 364-369). n_trials=9 with 6 combos: 3 extra asks are freely TPE-sampled -> duplicates.
3. Suggested name absent from grid: that axis escapes the grid entirely (free sampling).

JUSTIFICATION FOR CURRENT DESIGN (steelman, for triage):
- search_space is the single declaration of the param surface; grid is a sweep strategy symmetric with `sampler`. One consumer in run_trial.
- Rename (n_kde -> model__n_kde) and derived params are user code; not auto-generatable.
- Mixed mode (grid axes fixed + unsuggested axes sampled) comes free via enqueue_trial semantics.
- Mirrors the optuna enqueue_trial + suggest pattern.

PROPOSAL:
1. In load_config, when grid is set and search_space is None, synthesize an identity search_space: {k: trial.suggest_categorical(k, unique(v)) for k, v in grid.items()}. Config keys become grid keys. Verified viable: 6 asks -> 6 distinct configs. Explicit search_space still wins, so rename/derivation/mixed mode are preserved. The existing base/params overlap guard in run_trial already catches key collisions.
2. Error (not silent) when grid is set and explicit n_trials != product - over-run currently samples freely, truncation silently drops combos.
3. When both grid and search_space are present, validate coupling at load time: call search_space once against a spy trial recording suggest names; error if set(grid) != suggested names (both directions).

BREAKING CHANGE: none required; synthesis is additive. Downstream configs can then drop the duplicated search_space.
close_reason: Completed: grid is a self-contained deterministic mode — load_config rejects grid+search_space and any explicit n_trials != Cartesian product (new ConfigValidationError mapped to CONFIG_ERROR exit 3); runner synthesizes suggest_categorical from grid keys so enqueued values are read into trial configs; enqueue paths unchanged. Breaking: configs with both must delete search_space and align n_trials. Proofs: 4992702; 129 targeted tests, full suite 1937 passed.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Triage: proposal 3 conflicts with the documented mixed-mode behavior. Should coupling require grid keys to be a subset of suggested names (preserving extra sampled axes), or exact equality (disallowing mixed mode)? Also, should n_trials below the grid product remain a supported partial grid while only overruns error, or should every mismatch fail? Resolve these semantics before implementation.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Decision confirmed: grid is a separate deterministic sweep mode, not a partial strategy layered onto search_space. Jernerics synthesizes the Optuna categorical suggestions internally; grid keys are the final trial-config keys; grid + search_space is rejected. n_trials defaults to the Cartesian-product size, and any explicit mismatch is rejected so every combination runs exactly once with no sampler escape.

title: Overview roll-up: only the failed pill is interactive yet all pills look clickable, and the failure view has no explicit way back
description:

- The failure view is an additive html.Details panel (failed_view_section, workspace.py:1159), not a scope change: the roll-up and sweeps grid remain unfiltered. - Existing coverage in tests/unit (test_dashboard_views.py, test_dashboard_poll.py) still passes; the failed-view open path is updated where it asserts open=True.

title: stream_client discards ingest error bodies (logs only HTTP status)
description:
## Problem

`StreamClient._ship_batch` (packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/stream_client.py:179)
reduces every non-2xx response to `detail = f"HTTP {response.status_code}"` and
discards the body. The server's ingest errors are informative — `http.py`
returns an `IngestError` with `error_code`, `event_index`, and a message
(e.g. FK failure vs `(project, name)` reuse vs immutability conflict) — but
none of it reaches the logs, so any live ingest conflict is undiagnosable
without replaying events by hand.

This directly blocked root-causing the slurm live-tracking failure
(companion issue): the 409 body would have named the rejecting event and
likely the conflict class on the first flush.

## Reproduce

Run any study against the current server whose live stream hits an ingest
conflict (see companion issue for a concrete setup). stderr shows only:

```
Failed to ship batch (HTTP 409); retry 1 in 0.5s ...
```

while the response body (visible via a manual replay, which does parse it)
contains the specific error.

## Proposed

Include a truncated `response.text` in the per-batch failure log line, at
least on the first failure for a given batch (avoid log spam on retries).
One line change in `_ship_batch`.
close_reason: Implemented in stream_client.py (_ship_batch): first failure per batch includes up to 400 chars of the decoded response body, later retries log the bare status. Verified: new unit test test_first_failure_logs_error_body_once plus 21 existing stream tests pass; full suite 1394 passed with only the pre-existing jernerics-31q failure (verified identical on stashed clean tree). Fix immediately surfaced the 409 root cause of jernerics-31q, recorded there.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Design locked: include truncated response body in _ship_batch failure detail on the first failure per batch only (retry_count == 0), decoded from response.content (TransportResponse protocol exposes bytes, not .text) with errors=replace. Subsequent retry lines keep the bare HTTP status to avoid spam.

comments.author: jerry
comments.text: Fixed in e0fe36f per commit message (log ingest error bodies on ship failure). Code-level verification only: no subsequent run has produced a ship failure, so the error-body logging path has not been observed at runtime yet. Re-open nothing; noting for the record.

title: HPC/slurm: live event shipping dead-ends in 409 retry loops; submission rows never pre-landed
description:
## Problem

Since the tracking server update (stricter ingest), HPC/slurm container jobs ship
zero events live: every batch is rejected HTTP 409 from its first attempt and
retried until drain timeout. Events reach the server only via manual
`jernerics tracking replay -b hpc`.

Observed on symlab study `symlab_constant_loss_weight_20260827-151514`
(job 27858237, 4-task sbatch array, container image built from main@655e897):

- 33 `Failed to ship batch (HTTP 409)` lines per array task; 6,618 events
  buffered in `<study>/events/{0..3}.jsonl`.
- `<study>/submission/89f0fdf8a0174c43a538513f3af859c6.jsonl` (sweep /
  submission / job rows) sat unshipped for the whole run.
- Zero `immediate ship` lines in any task stderr — the deploy-time
  `ship_events_file` hook appears never to have run on this path.
- Replay of the same 5 files from a local single stream: **0 failures**,
  6,618/6,618 events accepted. The events are valid; the failure is
  live-stream state, not payload or auth.
- Pre-update control: job 27849157 (same backend, older server) shipped
  6,086 events live with 0 failures.

Working model (NOT confirmed — see open questions): the updated server enforces
referential ordering strictly; trial-stream batches reference sweep/submission
rows that are supposed to be pre-landed by the deploy-time immediate ship
(`batch_sync.ship_events_file` docstring names exactly this mode: live streams
"409-retrying until the post-hook replay" when they are not). On the slurm path
those prerequisite rows never land, so every trial batch fails from the start,
and because a rejected batch is retried with identical composition, it can
never succeed.

## Reproduce

1. Server at current version; submit any multi-trial study to the slurm
   backend: `jernerics run -b hpc <trial>.py <config>.py` with `n_trials >= 1`.
2. Watch task stderr: `Failed to ship batch (HTTP 409); retry N ...` from the
   first flush onward.
3. `curl` the server query endpoint: no `sweeps` row for the study.
4. Recover with `jernerics tracking replay -b hpc --study <study>` — 0 failures.

## More investigation needed (explicitly open)

- **Why does the immediate-ship hook not run (or not succeed) on slurm?**
  Candidates: not wired into the container runner at all; invoked before the
  submission file is written (docstring says missing file is a silent no-op);
  or invoked without credentials. No log line exists to distinguish these —
  a silent no-op is indistinguishable from "never called" in current logs.
- **Exact ingest rejection reason for the first live batch** (FK on missing
  sweep vs `(project, name)` reuse vs other): unobservable today because the
  client discards 409 response bodies (companion issue).
- **Is concurrency an independent failure mode once prerequisites land?**
  All post-update HPC evidence is 4-way concurrent; there is no post-update
  single-task HPC run that shipped live. A 1-trial verification submission

title: job logs resolves wrong log path for array jobs with project-scoped cache
description:
Symptom: 'jernerics job logs 27842844_1 -b hpc' inside a project using cache_dir with {project_name} template (symlab: /scratch/qiy18011/jez21005/jernerics/{project_name}) looked for /jernerics/logs/27842844_1.out instead of /jernerics/symlab/logs/27842844_1.out.

Root causes (compounding):
1. SlurmAdapter.get_logs looked up job meta only at jobs/<job_id>.json. Submit saves one meta per array job under the BASE id (27842844.json); asking for an element (27842844_1) missed the meta and fell into the pattern-less fallback.
2. That fallback used adapter.cache_host, which SlurmAdapter.from_config derives via strip_project_template() — the {project_name} segment was stripped, so even non-array fallbacks pointed one directory too high.

Fix:
- packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/slurm/adapter.py: new _find_job_meta() tries jobs/<id>.json then jobs/<base>.json for array elements (mirrors Backend.list_jobs); fallback patterns use meta['cache_host'] when present.
- packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/backend.py: Backend.get_logs passes cache_host=self.paths.resolve_cache() (project-substituted) in meta.

Verified: reproduction against real symlab config now cats /scratch/qiy18011/jez21005/jernerics/symlab/logs/27842844_1.out (matches actual log location); meta-less fallback also project-scoped. Unit tests: test_slurm_adapter.py TestGetLogs (array element via base meta; fallback cache_host), test_backend.py test_get_logs asserts meta cache_host.

title: Script-as-trial: migrate all symlab trial files from functions to scripts
description:
## Scope

Mechanical migration of all symlab experiment trial files from the `def trial(config, tracker)` pattern to flat scripts using the new API.

## Depends on

- `jernerics-rs5` (trial context API)
- `jernerics-7q7` (runner subprocess execution)

## What changes

Each trial file (`experiments/*/trial.py`) gets rewritten:

### Before
```python
def trial(config, tracker):
    torch.manual_seed(config["seed"])
    ...
    for step in range(config["n_steps"]):
        ...
        tracker.log_value("loss", loss.item(), step=step)
    return {"final_loss": loss.item()}
```

### After
```python
import jernerics

config = jernerics.trial_config(defaults={
    "lr": 3e-4, "n_steps": 100, ...  # pulled from each config.py
})
tracker = jernerics.trial_tracker()

torch.manual_seed(config["seed"])
...
for step in range(config["n_steps"]):
    ...
    tracker.log_value("loss", loss.item(), step=step)

tracker.finish({"final_loss": loss.item()})
```

## Per-file steps

1. Remove the `def trial(config, tracker):` wrapper, unindent the body
2. Add `import jernerics` at the top
3. Add `config = jernerics.trial_config(defaults={...})` — pull sensible defaults from the corresponding `config.py` base dict (use small n_steps like 100 for standalone)
4. Add `tracker = jernerics.trial_tracker()`
5. Replace `return {...}` with `tracker.finish({...})`
6. Ensure all `tracker.log_param()` / `tracker.log_value()` calls work unchanged (they will — same interface)

## Trial files to migrate

- `experiments/coupled/trial.py`
- `experiments/skeleton/trial.py` (symlink to coupled)
- `experiments/diagnostic/trial.py`
- `experiments/inspect/trial.py`
- `experiments/overfit/trial.py`
- `experiments/probe/trial.py`
- `experiments/scale/trial.py`
- `experiments/train/trial.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All trial files rewritten as scripts
- [ ] `python trial.py` works standalone for at least coupled/trial.py (short run)
- [ ] No `def trial(config, tracker)` remains anywhere
- [ ] All tracker calls use the tracker from `trial_tracker()`
close_reason: Still relevant, but owned by symlab. Recreated with current scope as symlab-h7b; closing this cross-project tracker rather than maintaining a jernerics bead for symlab experiment files.

title: Chained retry submission crashes checker: _validate_job_id rejects StdoutHost's empty stdout
description:
## Problem

Reproduced on hpc2 (diag job 28092796, 2026-08-30) and deterministic in code:

The retry checker composes resubmissions through StdoutHost (retry_checker.py:156), whose run() prints the script and returns returncode=0 with EMPTY stdout. In SlurmAdapter.submit_sweep's chained branch (post_hook_command present, adapter.py:381-399), the composed 'ARRAY_ID CHECKER_ID' line is parsed from result.stdout and passed to _validate_job_id — which rejects the empty string and raises SlurmSubmitError. The checker's post-hook exits 1; the cluster wrapper discards its stderr ('2>/dev/null' in command_builders.py:171), so the checker job just shows FAILED in ~13s with zero logs.

At the pre-e85887f pin (9c7e1a9) the chain branch took parts[0] unvalidated: StdoutHost's empty job_id passed silently and the real submission happened via the wrapper's outer 'bash {retry_script}'. e85887f added _validate_job_id (correct for real hosts) and broke the emission path. Broken on main since 2026-08-28; the 2026-08-30 remote e2e (first run on a post-e85887f image) caught it as test_retry failing: the crashed checker never replays, the sweep row never lands, run_sweep discover times out.

## Fix direction (needs decision)

StdoutHost is a script emitter, not an executor: submit_sweep must not validate its synthetic stdout. Either (a) detect emission hosts (dry-run flag through submit_sweep) and skip validation/parse, or (b) validate leniently when stdout is empty AND returncode==0 (the outer bash is the real submitter), or (c) make _validate_job_id's empty case a warning. Also worth fixing while here: the checker wrapper discards ALL post-hook stderr — field failures are invisible (0-byte checker logs).

## Acceptance criteria

- e2e_remote test_hpc test_retry passes on a post-e85887f image.
- Unit test: submit_sweep with a StdoutHost-like host and post_hook_command returns successfully (emission semantics) instead of raising.

## Fix direction (LOCKED 2026-08-31)

Emission-host marker: add `emits_scripts = True` class attribute to StdoutHost (host.py, alongside the existing `is_local` attribute). In SlurmAdapter.submit_sweep, when `getattr(self.host, "emits_scripts", False)`, skip the stdout parse and _validate_job_id in the chained branch and return empty-id JobSubmission(s) — shape parity with the non-chained branch (adapter.py:382 already passes unvalidated stdout through). Real hosts keep strict validation. Scope ALSO includes the checker wrapper stderr swallow: command_builders.py:171 sends post-hook stderr to /dev/null (0-byte checker logs) — redirect to a log file instead so checker failures leave evidence.

Note: the earlier triage comment recommended the lenient empty-stdout heuristic; SUPERSEDED — a real host returning rc=0 with empty stdout is exactly the failure class e85887f guards against, and the heuristic cannot distinguish it from emission. The only emission caller (retry_checker.py:188) discards the SubmitResult, so empty job ids have zero downstream consumers.
close_reason: u2m: emits_scripts marker on StdoutHost + emission bypass in submit_sweep chained branch + checker stderr un-swallowed (2>/dev/null dropped from post_hook wrapper). Merged as 3419711 (commits 47f285b..c64fe47). Verified: 356 backend unit tests green against worktree code, full suite 1831 passed on merged main. Field check: e2e_remote test_hpc test_retry on next remote run.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Triage: confirmed still broken at adapter.py:400-403 on HEAD (b970729); nothing fixed since filing. Fix decision needed among (a) dry-run/emission flag threaded through submit_sweep — no discriminator exists on the Host protocol today (StdoutHost is duck-typed, host.py:61), so this costs protocol surface; (b) lenient path when stdout is empty AND returncode==0 — restores pre-e85887f emission semantics (outer bash wrapper is the real submitter) while keeping the guard for real hosts; (c) warning-only empty case — loses the guard where empty stdout on a real host is a genuine failure. Recommendation: (b), plus fold in the command_builders.py:171 '2>/dev/null' stderr swallow (0-byte checker logs) in the same fix — it is why this crash was invisible in the field.

title: Post-hook: replace optuna-failed deterministic trials from journal facts
description:
## Problem (verified against main @ 258fe0e)

In-runner trial failures (trial code raises -> runner calls `study.tell(FAIL)`, runner.py:182) are invisible to retry accounting: `plan_retry` (retry.py:71-170) has no `TrialState.FAIL` branch, so `remaining_needed` (retry.py:157) refills every FAIL's slot with an unlineaged fresh trial that bypasses the `max_retries` ledger entirely.

For grid sweeps this is worse than wasted compute: grid enqueues the cartesian product once per study (sentinel file, command_builders.py:40-47), so fresh replacements are free-sampler draws, not the failed combo — silent duplicates, grid dedup broken (the exact pathology s27 warned about), churn bounded only by `chain_depth_cap` (default 20 cycles). The ledger could not cap these even in principle: fresh draws have different param keys than the failed combo.

## Locked design

Deterministic FAILs flow through the existing per-combo `max_retries` budget with lineage, replacing today's ledger-less fresh refill:

1. Determinism predicate: `sweep.grid is not None` (config.py:360-365 — grid is self-contained and mutually exclusive with `search_space`). `run_checker` already loads the sweep (retry_checker.py:95); pass the flag into `plan_retry`. No new config field.
2. `plan_retry` gains `deterministic: bool`. New FAIL branch (deterministic only): `param_key(trial.params)` ledger lookup —
   - under `max_retries` -> re-enqueue the SAME params with retry lineage (`study.enqueue_trial(params, user_attrs=retry_lineage_attrs(...))`, mirroring `_enqueue_retry` at retry_checker.py:70-85 but WITHOUT `study.tell` — the trial is already FAIL); ledger[pkey] += 1.
   - at/over `max_retries` -> terminal: the FAIL occupies its slot, no replacement.
3. Accounting: `remaining_needed = n_trials - complete - fresh_running - waiting - stale_retries_enqueued - failed_retries_enqueued - failed_exhausted`. Exhausted FAILs occupy slots so nothing refills them; `is_complete = total_array_size == 0` (rule unchanged).
4. Stochastic sweeps: byte-identical behavior (FAIL stays invisible -> fresh exploration, per bead: no heuristics on stochastic).
5. Fast-fail breaker: unchanged globally. Deterministic fast-marked-FAIL trials enter the FAIL branch next cycle -> same-combo ledger-capped retry (grid is exhaustive; "let optuna try different params" is meaningless there).
6. Surfacing: already exists — FAILED trial snapshots (optuna_mirror `_STATE_MAP`) + `execution_end(failure_kind, failure_summary=repr(exc))` (runner.py:257-283). No new surfaces.

## Out of scope

Stochastic FAIL handling; deliberate re-run CLI (follow-up bead, filed); artifact API (bmo).

## Acceptance

1. Unit, plan_retry deterministic=True: FAIL under budget -> same-params retry with lineage attrs + ledger increment; FAIL at budget -> exhausted, occupies slot; `remaining_needed` excludes exhausted; deterministic=False -> current behavior unchanged (FAIL -> fresh refill, no ledger write).
2. Unit: a permanently failing combo stops being re-enqueued after `max_retries` total attempts, ledger persisting across cycles via `.retry_ledger.json`.
3. E2E: grid sweep with one permanently failing trial -> exactly `max_retries` same-combo lineage retries (family renders as generations), then sweep terminal; no free-sampled duplicate combos appear in the study; server completeness flips with the failure visible in Failed executions.
4. E2E: stochastic sweep with a failing trial -> behavior identical to today.
5. `just lint`, `just format-check`, `just test` pass.
close_reason: Implemented per the locked design in the issue: determinism predicate sweep.grid is not None; plan_retry deterministic FAIL branch (same-params lineage retry under max_retries with ledger increment, exhausted FAIL occupies its slot; settled FAILs with an existing retry_of replacement never re-planned); accounting subtracts failed_retries_enqueued and failed_exhausted; total_array_size includes failed retries; stochastic byte-identical; fast-fail breaker untouched; surfacing pre-existing. Two documented deviations: (1) settled-FAIL guard so exactly 1+max_retries attempts per combo (pinned by multi-cycle unit test), (2) reconcile_study skips WAITING trials — a pre-existing identity-squatting bug on main's stale path (fallback-id snapshot 409-conflicted the live runner identity) found by the new e2e; post_hook/asktell suites re-run green. Merged from agent commit 32186ec after independent verification (unit 122 passed, e2e 32 passed in worktree; full gates 1970 passed / 6 skipped).

title: Deliberate re-run CLI for failed grid trials
description:
Deferred from jernerics-u32 design session (2026-09-01): u32 makes deterministic grid FAILs ledger-capped lineage retries that terminate at max_retries. Once terminal, there is no recovery path that reuses a study's completed compute — recovery today means a new sweep re-running every combo.

SCOPE: a command (e.g. jernerics retry --failed --reason '...') that re-enqueues FAILED grid combos of an existing study with retry lineage plus a recorded reason user_attr, through the existing submit chain (chain_depth, backend). Use case: infra/jernerics bug fixed after the sweep wound down (the bmo 64KiB finish cap is the canonical example), same deterministic work re-run to recover compute.

Depends on u32 landing first (its FAIL accounting and lineage machinery are prerequisites).

title: Slurm post-hooks omit GPU-partition resource requirements
description:
## Problem

`SlurmAdapter.render_sweep()` renders the array and post-hook from the same `SweepSubmissionParams`, but applies scheduler overrides asymmetrically. `_render_array_script()` passes `_render_overrides(params)` into `_format_array_script()`; `_format_checker_script()` receives only `partition=params.overrides.get("partition", self.partition)`.

On a GPU-only Slurm partition, this produces a CPU-sized post-hook in the GPU partition with no `gres`/`gpus` request. Slurm leaves it pending forever with `QOSMinGRES`, so the sweep's post-hook never runs.

## Reproduction

Observed on symlab's `hpc` backend (`general-gpu`, account `qiy18011`, A100 trial overrides):

- Primary array job `27884175_1` requested `cpu=8,mem=32G,gres/gpu=1`, ran on `gpu21`, and completed `0:0`.
- Dependent post-hook `27884176` requested only `cpu=1,mem=1G`, retained `partition=general-gpu`, and became `PENDING (QOSMinGRES)` after the array completed.
- Five historical post-hooks had the identical condition: `27858194`, `27858209`, `27858238`, `27860922`, and `27861511`.

A targeted render reproduction from this repository shows the mismatch deterministically. Given primary overrides for `account=qiy18011`, `gres=gpu:1`, `cpus-per-task=8`, `constraint=a100`, and `exclude=gpu14`, the array contains all of those directives; the post-hook contains only:

```text
#SBATCH --partition=general-gpu
#SBATCH --time=0:10:00
#SBATCH --mem=1G
```

Relevant source:

- `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/slurm/adapter.py:123-177` renders every allowlisted override into the array.
- `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/slurm/adapter.py:180-210` hardcodes the post-hook's resources and accepts only `partition`.
- `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/slurm/adapter.py:315-344` shows that only the array calls `_render_overrides(params)`.

## Impact

The post-hook is not optional bookkeeping: `post_hook.run_pipeline()` performs retry detection, Optuna-journal reconciliation, tracking replay, and pending artifact upload. A permanently pending post-hook leaves completed sweeps without their completion pipeline; `jernerics job wait` can still report the array complete.

## Required behavior

- Give the Slurm post-hook an explicit, scheduler-valid resource profile instead of inheriting only the trial partition.
- Support a CPU-compatible post-hook location/profile for GPU sweeps. Do not require a GPU allocation merely to run the CPU-only post-hook.
- Keep `afterany` dependency semantics so failed array tasks still trigger the post-hook.
- Preserve the current 10-minute / 1 GiB defaults unless a post-hook resource profile overrides them.
- Add focused rendering coverage proving that GPU-array overrides do not generate a post-hook stuck in a GPU-only partition without the required GRES.

## Scope

This is distinct from `jernerics-build-job-exclude-hh5`, which fixed node exclusion for container-build jobs. It concerns post-hook resource selection for Slurm sweeps.
close_reason: Slurm post-hook now carries an explicit resource profile: post_hook_partition/post_hook_time/post_hook_mem on SlurmConfig ([tool.jernerics.backends.<name>.slurm]), threaded through SlurmAdapter.from_config into _format_checker_script. Defaults preserve 0:10:00/1GiB and trial-partition inheritance; post_hook_partition lets GPU sweeps land the CPU-only post-hook on a CPU partition instead of pending QOSMinGRES. afterany unchanged. Rendering coverage in TestPostHookProfile (GPU overrides stay out of the post-hook) + loader tests. Note: unrelated pre-existing flake jernerics-kj9 filed separately.

title: Prevent replay from deleting active tracking journals
description:
## Problem
TrackingWriter keeps an append descriptor open (tracking/jsonl_io.py:81-104), while successful replay unconditionally unlinks every scanned JSONL and cursor (tracking/batch_sync.py:260-266). Replay during a live trial can reach current EOF, unlink the path, and lose later writes in the orphaned inode. write_cursor also shares one fixed .cursor.tmp across shippers (jsonl_io.py:33-46), permitting cross-process replace failures or cursor regression. Existing overlap coverage is sequential. Distinct from jernerics-79i, which is a StreamClient join flake.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Keep TrackingWriter and the live shipper open for a trial.
2. Run batch replay until it reaches the current EOF.
3. Append another event through the still-open writer.
4. Observe that replay removed the pathname and the later event exists only in an unlinked inode; concurrent cursor commits can also race on the shared temp path.

## Proposed Change
define explicit writer/shipper ownership or a closed marker before deletion; serialize cross-process cursor commits, use unique temp files, and commit monotonic offsets.

## Acceptance Criteria
a barrier-controlled live-writer + replay test appends after replay reaches its first EOF and proves every event reaches the server, the source remains reachable until close, no shipper errors, and the final cursor never regresses.
close_reason: Completed: TrackingWriter holds a lifetime SH flock via open->lock->inode-recheck (bounded retries); replay_tracking deletes shipped journals only under held EX lock with cursor==EOF; write_cursor serialized via .cursor.lock sidecar, unique mkstemp temps, monotonic (recreated-file aware). Orchestrator reproduced the original loss scenario end-to-end (live writer survives two replays, append-after-EOF ships, deletion only after close). Merged as 17f0786; just check: 1298 passed, 6 skipped.

title: Container build doesn't provision external method dependencies
description:
## Problem
The container.def only runs `uv sync --no-dev --no-editable` for the main project. Methods that use external dependencies not in pyproject.toml (e.g., separate venvs, data caches) are invisible inside the container.

## Example
PySIPS originally ran as an external subprocess in a separate Python 3.12 venv with its own dependencies (pysips, bingo-nasa, smcpy). The container (Python 3.13) had no access to this venv or the SRSD data cache. This required extensive manual provisioning: venv copying, bind mounts, path overrides.

## Resolution
In this case, resolved by adding pysips/bingo-nasa/smcpy as project dependencies so they install in the container venv. But the general problem remains for any method with external dependencies.

## Suggestion
1. Document that all method dependencies must be in pyproject.toml for container builds
2. OR provide a mechanism for post-build provisioning scripts in container.def
3. OR support custom bind mounts via config (e.g., `[tool.jernerics.backends.hpc.apptainer]\nextra_binds = [...]`)
close_reason: Closed on the same user-ownership boundary as jernerics-jdu (2026-08-30): provisioning external venvs/data caches is the user's container.def edit, not a harness feature. Concrete symlab case was already resolved by declaring pysips/bingo-nasa/smcpy as project dependencies. Boundary recorded in docs/vision.md Non-goals.

comments.author: jerry
comments.text: 2026-08-22 validity sweep: the only concrete PySIPS incident recorded here is resolved by declaring its dependencies in pyproject.toml. Current starters are deliberately user-owned container.def/Dockerfile files, so post-build provisioning is already expressible without a Jernerics hook. No active consumer for generic extra_binds was found. Remaining work is a product-scope decision, not a locked implementation.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Triage verification (2026-08-30, at HEAD): confirmed. Starter python.def %post provisions only main-project deps (uv sync --frozen --no-dev); no mechanism exists for external venvs or data caches. Gap as described.

title: Login drops the deep URL: authenticated users land on /dashboard/ instead of the page they opened
description:
Confirmed on atlas (2026-08-21): opening https://atlas.taile454b.ts.net/dashboard/project/symlab unauthenticated redirects to /dashboard/login (correct), but after submitting a valid API key the user lands on /dashboard/ — the original deep URL (workspace/sweep/trial/execution/artifact-view/analysis?sel=...) is lost. Shared-link recipients who are not yet logged in never reach the shared artifact/analysis view they were sent.

Note the ?sel= token must survive (query included).

Orchestrator browser-verified on worktree harness: deep URL + ?sel= round-trips through login exactly and stays stable on /analysis; wrong-key retry preserves next and lands on the deep URL; unsafe next dropped from the form (9 parametrized attack values covered server-side).
