title: jernerics sync times out pulling tracking data from HPC
description:
## Problem
`jernerics tracking replay -b hpc` consistently times out while syncing tracking data from HPC (previously reproduced at 120s and 300s). SSH itself is fast and the tracking directory is about 66 MiB. The current path is commands/tracking.py -> Backend.sync; backend.py:478-483 also contains a brittle SSHHost/LocalHost command-shape FIXME that should be resolved in the same change.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure the affected Slurm backend with its scratch cache directory.
2. Run `jernerics tracking replay -b hpc`.
3. Observe `Syncing tracking data from HPC...` and no completion after at least 300 seconds while direct SSH remains responsive.

## Impact
Blocks the normal tracking replay/sync workflow. Direct rsync of selected project directories is the current workaround.

## Acceptance Criteria
The current replay command completes against the affected approximately 66 MiB tracking directory within a bounded timeout; failure reports the blocking remote command and exit state; Backend.sync no longer branches on concrete Host types for shell command shape; focused unit coverage exercises local and SSH host behavior.
close_reason: Completed: Backend.sync now implements the documented pull — remote tar (--exclude tracking/env) -> scp -> local extract (filter=data) -> local replay_tracking; bounded (tar/scp 600s), failures raise with the exact blocking command + exit state; Host gains shell()/is_local, all isinstance(SSHHost) command-shape branching removed (sync + clean); API key never leaves the local machine for sync. Integration-verified with a real server: full event chain (sweep/trial/execution/25 values) shipped via the pull pipeline; remote journal deletion deliberately omitted (live-writer safety, vzv). Merged as cc3a553; just check: 1322 passed, 6 skipped.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Maintenance audit 2026-08-22: the original `jernerics sync --backend hpc` surface is stale. Current reproduction path is `jernerics tracking replay -b <backend>`, which calls Backend.sync in packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/backend.py. That method also contains the FIXME at lines 478-483 for brittle SSHHost/LocalHost isinstance dispatch; fold host command-shape ownership into the timeout fix rather than creating a duplicate issue.

title: Missing input file causes infinite retry with no fast-fail
description: When a config references a file (e.g. pool .pkl) that doesn't exist on the remote, jobs fail instantly and retry infinitely. The retry system treats each fast failure as a crash (not a permanent error), so it resubmits indefinitely with no backoff. Two problems: (1) no pre-flight validation that referenced files exist before dispatch, (2) no detection of repeated instant failures (jobs dying within seconds) to mark as permanently failed instead of retrying. In practice this means a missing pool file burns retry attempts silently and the user only discovers it by checking logs after hours of waiting.
close_reason: Completed: commit c257b7c. Circuit breaker trips after repeated fast failures to stop infinite retry on missing files/bad configs.

title: Shared ?sel= token cold start: auto-pick the token's project (or prompt) for fresh sessions
description:
Confirmed on atlas (2026-08-21) with a fresh browser context: opening /dashboard/analysis?sel=<token> while logged in but before any project is picked shows empty grids ("No Rows To Show" x2), tray "0 sweep(s) · 0 trial(s) · 0 family/families", and the header picker still reading "Project…". Hydration only fires once the recipient manually picks the project in the header picker (jhe.3 design: hydration re-fires when project-store settles — after picking symlab the tray shows 1 sweep, the sweep checkbox restores, and the family grid populates; all verified working).

A recipient has no on-page cue that a project pick is required. The token itself already carries selection.project ("symlab"), so two candidate behaviors: (a) on analysis hydration with a ?sel= token and empty project-store, auto-set project-store from the token's project (picker follows); (b) keep manual pick but render an explicit hint ("Pick a project to load the shared selection") in place of the empty grids. Decide (a) vs (b) at design time — (a) is the better recipient experience but changes project-store semantics (token now mutates global state); (b) is the conservative hint.

## Decision (locked 2026-08-21, user): option (a) auto-pick from token

On analysis hydration with a ?sel= token present and project-store EMPTY, write the token's selection.project into project-store (picker label follows; hydration re-fires per the jhe.3 settle design). Guard: fires ONLY when project-store is empty — never overrides a deliberate project pick. Fallback: if the token's project is unknown to the recipient (not in the workspace catalog / no data), render the explicit hint naming the token's project instead of silently empty grids.
close_reason: Fixed in 012b535 (merged to main), option (a) as locked: picker callback _show_current_project gains Input url.search — with project-store empty it adopts cold_start()'s decoded token project via the picker's own plain write, running the exact manual-pick settle chain (picker -> project-store -> hydration re-fires); 'if project: return project' is the never-override guard; unknown project renders the hint naming it; malformed tokens keep the decode error. A hydration-side project-store write was tried first and rejected by wire-trace: Dash 4.4.1 delivers allow_duplicate outputs under @hash-suffixed keys that don't notify plain-input observers. Orchestrator browser-verified on a virgin-origin harness: deep link through wh2 login auto-labels the picker 'ops' with zero clicks, sweep checkbox restores, tray '1 sweep(s)', ?sel= survives; ghost-project token keeps picker and shows the naming hint (no adoption); malformed token keeps the error; zero console errors leaving analysis. Gates green: 1268 passed, 6 skipped.

comments.text: Implemented on fix/xbx (worktree /tmp/wt-xbx), pending review/commit push: cold start now adopts the token's project through the picker callback (_show_current_project gains url.search input; returns the token's project only while project-store is empty), so adoption travels the manual-pick settle path (picker -> _remember_project -> project-store -> hydration re-fires) — a plain primary write, because an allow_duplicate store write does not notify plain-input observers in Dash 4.4.1 (picker label never followed; verified by wire trace). New analysis.cold_start() decodes the token pre-project and gates on service.projects(); unknown project renders the hint 'selection token targets project X, which this dashboard has no data for; pick a project to analyze.' hydrate_tray's empty-project branch only surfaces cold-start errors. Browser-verified on headless Chromium: fresh-context cold start (4+ runs: picker shows project with zero clicks, grids populate, sweep checkboxes restore, tray non-zero, ?sel= survives), picked-project + foreign token (kept, cross-project error — byte-identical to main), unknown project (hint), invalid token (malformed error). title: Ground-up dashboard rewrite to the approved prototype (page-per-entity IA)
description:

still renders the Browse-scope sidebar (include-archived/include-invalid checkboxes + sweep-checklist grid), dual grids, trial/retry picker, and inspector region — none of which exist in the approved design. The prototype's architecture is page-per-entity ("Sweep detail owns the center"), tabs Overview·Investigations·Exceptions, Series/Points/Search/Optuna scoped to sweep or investigation, Open-in-Python as an action. The old routing model (everything in one persistent workspace with a view-doc `focus` inspector) is replaced wholesale. # Resolved decisions (locked with user 2026-09-03) - Optuna view: SWEEP-SCOPED sub-view on the sweep page (sub-nav Overview·Series·Points·Search·Optuna, shown where data supports), NOT a project tab. - Old-shell affordances: NOTHING survives. No include-flag checkboxes, no always-visible inspector, no project-scope retry-root picking. Prototype as-is. (Retry-root picking ports to the sweep page as behavior, not as a project-scope affordance.) - Landing /dashboard (project catalog): functional behavior kept (projects table), restyled to the prototype stylesheet/topbar. The prototype's index.html is proto meta-only, not a production design. - Artifact viewer /dashboard/artifact-view/: kept, restyled. - Sweep page URL: /dashboard/project//sweep/ with ?via= crumb back (project-scoped nested route). - Exceptions page: /dashboard/project//exceptions — Active/All, group by cause/sweep/host, working selection, "Failures in this sweep" deep link lands pre-expanded (per proto index walkthrough). - Stylesheet: prototype styles.css is ported to become THE dashboard stylesheet (adapt class names as needed); old dashboard.css classes coexist only until the demolition task deletes them. - Cutover discipline: PAGE-BY-PAGE. Each task lands the new page AND deletes the old surface it replaces in the same change. Acceptance includes "composition matches the prototype section-for-section; zero old chrome on that page". NO backward-compat shims, NO legacy fallbacks, NO "keep it in sync with the old machinery" ambiguity resolutions. If prototype and old code disagree, the prototype wins. If a behavior has no prototype home, port it into the nearest prototype surface and note it in the bead close reason. - Scope boundary: NO store/schema/HTTP changes. UI layer only (dashboard package + its tests + e2e journeys). service.py gains read methods only where a prototype surface needs facts existing methods can't express (prefer existing; raw SQL only in queries.py/store.py/ingest.py). - Tests: each cutover rewrites the page's view tests for the new composition and updates any e2e journey it breaks, in the same change. # Prototype page inventory (the layout contract, from build.py) overview(active/all) · failures_page(active/all) · sweep_page(id) (Executions/Trials/Params + artifact chips + sub-nav) · series_page/points_page (sweep-scoped, parcoords inside points) · investigations_page · investigation_edit_page · compare_page + inv_series/inv_points/inv_search/inv_python · shared: tab_bar, page_shell, sweeps_table, scroll_table, tiles, segments, status_dot, failure_signal, art_chips, inv_nav, inv_crumbs. # Survivors (port as behaviors, do not redesign) auth/sessions, live polling, artifact download/chips, selection tokens, python token flow, Create-Investigation seeding from overview selection, exact-signature Compare, member editor with real-coverage preview, member scope across views, via-crumbs, retry-root picking (sweep page), Open-in-Python disclosure. # Task graph (waves) R1 shell foundation → {R2 overview, R3 exceptions, R4 sweep page, R6 investigations re-skin, R7 landing+artifact restyle} (parallel) → R5 sweep analysis sub-views (after R4) → R8 demolition + final verification (after all). # Acceptance bar (every task) - just lint / just format-check / just typecheck green; targeted pytest green; full `just test` green at epic end. - Orchestrator browser-verifies per page: composition matches prototype section-for-section, zero old chrome, zero console errors and zero 5xx on FULL page loads (goto, not client-side nav) of every touched route. - Delivery via herdr worktree dispatch; agents never commit/push/run br — orchestrator merges, verifies, closes.

title: Reuse the tracking v3 E2E scenario
description:
## Problem
`tests/e2e/test_tracking_v3.py` describes one scenario but declares it class-scoped. Eight test classes therefore rebuild the same uvicorn server, two runner trials, retry lineage, event shipping, and post-hook pipeline. The measured setup cost is 1.71-1.79 seconds per class, about 14 seconds total; seven rebuilds are redundant. `_start_server` also leaves daemon server threads running. In `test_asktell.py`, the in-process mocked conflict test duplicates both the unit exception contract and the stronger real-subprocess conflict journey; reconstructability repeats most of the post-hook repair pipeline.

## Proposed Change
Make the tracking-v3 scenario module-scoped with explicit uvicorn teardown. Keep read-only assertions shared. Make TestIdempotence self-relative and isolate or self-base TestLiveReplayOverlap so order cannot affect counts. Delete the weaker mocked conflict E2E test. Consolidate the mixed-success/failure reconstruction assertions into the post-hook repair journey only if its failure-state and idempotence assertions remain explicit.

## Acceptance Criteria
`test_tracking_v3.py` performs exactly one scenario setup and remains order-independent; all existing observable assertions remain represented; no daemon server survives teardown. Removing seven measured setups saves about 12.2 seconds. The real subprocess conflict journey and unit ReconciliationConflictError test remain. Any reconstruction consolidation retains completed/failed state, objective, parameter, distribution, and second-pass idempotence assertions. Record before/after E2E durations in the close reason.
close_reason: Completed in db16f36. Tracking-v3 now has one module setup (1.77s) instead of eight 1.70-1.81s setups, with explicit uvicorn thread/Store teardown; tracking+asktell focused suite is 20 passed in 6.44s, and reversed Idempotence/LiveReplayOverlap order passes 2/2. Mixed completed/failed reconstruction and real subprocess conflict facts remain. Full just check: 1343 passed, 6 skipped in 46.51s.

title: run --set keys are unnamespaced: trial-config keys leak as raw sbatch directives
description:
## Problem
`--set KEY=VALUE` on `jernerics run` merges every key into `cli_overrides` (packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/commands/execution.py:154-163), which flows into `params.overrides` (backend/submission.py:203-213 merges it with `experiment_overrides` from the config file's `backend_overrides`; only `max_parallel` is popped) and is rendered verbatim as sbatch flags by `_render_overrides` (backend/slurm/adapter.py:257-266) and `_format_array_script` (adapter.py:88-142). There is no classification of backend/sbatch keys vs trial-config keys, so config values such as `--set target=3200` produce:

    #SBATCH --target=3200
    #SBATCH --jobs=8

sbatch rejects the script (unrecognized option) and no job is queued — and per companion issue jernerics-l6r, that rejection is currently swallowed (exit 0, empty ids). Additionally, keys that collide with real sbatch flags are silently consumed as directives (`--set output=...` is shadowed by the adapter's own `--output` log redirect), so the user cannot override trial output paths this way either.

Note: config-file `backend_overrides` flow through the same render path, so validation must live at the render layer (adapter), not only at CLI parse time.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `jernerics run -b <slurm> trial.py config.py --set target=3200 --set jobs=8 --dry-run` — script shows `#SBATCH --target=3200`.
2. Drop `--dry-run`: sync runs, monitor lines print with EMPTY job ids, `squeue` shows nothing, exit code 0.

## Locked Design (confirmed with user 2026-08-27)

Decisions: full split (allowlist + new `--set-param` flag); param overrides merge last over base, overlap with search_space keys rejected; exception mapping handled by jernerics-l6r.

1. **Sbatch allowlist** — module-level constant in `backend/slurm/adapter.py`:
   `SBATCH_OVERRIDE_KEYS = frozenset({"partition", "time", "mem", "account", "cpus-per-task", "gpus", "gres", "constraint", "exclude", "nodes", "ntasks", "output", "error"})`
   - `_render_overrides` validates every key of `params.overrides` against it; unknown key → `ValueError` naming the invalid key and listing valid keys. This covers `--set`, config-file `backend_overrides`, and makes `--dry-run` fail loudly (dry-run renders the script via backend.py:132-153).
   - `run_remote` (execution.py) also validates `--set` keys at parse time (import the same constant) → `ExitCode.CONFIG_ERROR` with the same message, so CLI users get exit 3 not exit 1.
2. **New flag `--set-param KEY=VALUE`** (long option only; repeatable, same parse rules as `--set`: reject missing `=` and empty key with CONFIG_ERROR).
   - Values coerced via `json.loads`, falling back to the raw string ("3200"→3200, "true"→true, "foo"→"foo").
   - `run_local` is a non-goal: only `jernerics run` gets the flag.
3. **Plumbing** (follow the existing grid-b64 pattern in `command_builders.py:36-44`):
   - `SweepSubmission` (backend/models.py): new field `param_overrides: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)`
   - `run_remote` populates it; `backend.prepare_and_submit` / `submission.submit_sweep` pass it through
   - `build_trial_command` (command_builders.py:53-87): when non-empty, append `--param-overrides <base64 json>` to the runner args
   - runner (`runner.py`): new CLI arg `--param-overrides <b64>`; decode; merge as `{**sweep.base, **params, **param_overrides}` at runner.py:93; if `set(param_overrides) & set(params)` (search_space-sampled keys) raise `ValueError` mirroring the existing base∩search_space overlap error style (runner.py:85-91). Overlap with `base` is allowed — overriding base keys is the feature.
   - `RetryContext` (retry.py / submission.py:240-255): new field `param_overrides`; the retry/post-hook re-submission path restores it so retries keep the overrides.
4. **Cleanup**: no backward-compat shims — `--set` with unknown keys fails from now on.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `--set bogus=1` → exit `ExitCode.CONFIG_ERROR`, message names valid keys (CLI test, tests/unit/commands/)
- config-file `backend_overrides` with a key outside the allowlist → `ValueError` at render (adapter test); `--dry-run` with such a key fails loudly instead of printing the script
- `--set partition=debug` still renders `#SBATCH --partition=debug` (allowlist pass-through unchanged)
- `--set-param target=3200` reaches the trial config: runner-level test asserts `trial_config()` sees `target == 3200` (int)
- `--set-param lr=0.1` where `lr` is a search_space key → `ValueError` naming the overlap
- retry-context round-trip test: `param_overrides` survives `RetryContext.to_json` → re-submission
- `just lint`, `just format-check`, `just typecheck`, `just test` all pass

## Scheduling
Land after jernerics-l6r (both edit adapter.py; l6r touches `submit_sweep` validation, this touches `_render_overrides`). Logically independent — no beads dependency.
close_reason: Implemented: SBATCH_OVERRIDE_KEYS frozenset (13 keys) + shared unknown_sbatch_override_message; _render_overrides raises ValueError on unknown keys (covers --set, config backend_overrides, dry-run); run_remote pre-validates --set to CONFIG_ERROR(3); new --set-param KEY=VALUE (json.loads+raw fallback) plumbed SweepSubmission.param_overrides -> build_trial_command b64 --param-overrides -> runner merge {**base,**params,**overrides} with search_space-overlap ValueError; RetryContext carries param_overrides, retry_checker restores it. Verified live: --set bogus=1 exit 3 (multi-key names all), config-file bad key fails dry-run loudly, partition=debug renders, --set-param target=3200 -> runner CLI -> configs/trial_0.json target==3200 (int), dry-run shows --param-overrides b64. 25 new tests; 922 unit tests pass; lint/format/typecheck pass.

title: Harden the raw query read-only guard for CTE writes
description:
## Problem
server/http.py:39-41 classifies SQL only by first word and allows WITH. A CTE-prefixed DELETE therefore passes the intended guard and is stopped only by Store.query's mode=ro connection, producing a generic SQLite error. Existing tests cover only bare INSERT/DELETE/DROP/UPDATE and do not pin the actual last line of defense.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. POST a raw query beginning with `WITH` whose final statement is DELETE.
2. Observe that _is_read_only accepts the first word and SQLite mode=ro supplies the only rejection, using a generic database error rather than the intended guard response.

## Proposed Change
reject CTE-prefixed mutations cleanly while retaining valid read-only CTEs, and add a contract test that also fails if the mode=ro defense is removed. Avoid a home-grown full SQL parser unless necessary.

## Acceptance Criteria
WITH ... DELETE receives the documented read-only rejection, valid read CTEs work, and mutation remains impossible even if one defense regresses.
close_reason: Completed: read-only query connection now installs a write/DDL deny-list authorizer (QueryNotAuthorizedError -> documented 400 guard body); valid read CTEs keep working; mode=ro pinned by a monkeypatched-authorizer regression test. Code commit follows this closure. Focused: 78 passed; full gate: 1343 passed, 6 skipped.

title: Failure view invalidates one sweep per click — no batch path for parallel sweeps sharing a bug
description:
## Problem

The quick-flag entry point (overview roll-up failed pill -> "Failed executions" view) only offers per-sweep invalidation. When many parallel sweeps fail from the same shared bug — the exact case the reason field exists for — each sweep needs its own click, callback dispatch, panel re-render, and grid refresh.

## Verified live (atlas, project pyrimel, 2026-09-01)

- 18 failed sweep groups rendered, **18 separate "Mark sweep invalid" buttons**, **0 checkboxes**, **0 batch/select-all/bulk controls** in `#failed-trials-panel`.
- Each button applies to exactly one sweep: `apply_curation(service, "invalid", [str(value)], ...)` (dashboard/callbacks.py:1042-1043), single-element list.
- Only shared affordance is the reason input (`failed-reason`, workspace.py:1165-1170); it persists across clicks, but nothing marks more than one sweep per action.

## Batch capability exists but is disconnected

The Browse path already does batch: `sweep-grid` has multiRow checkbox selection (workspace.py:1473-1476, callbacks.py:866-868) and the collapsed "Curation…" panel's Mark invalid applies to all selected rows (callbacks.py:900-951); `selection_transitions` is any()-gated (workspace.py:160-170) so mixed selections work. But nothing links the failure view to it: no checkbox column on failed groups, no "select these failed sweeps in the browser" affordance (verified absent in live DOM).

## Proposed

Give the failure view a batch affordance, reusing `apply_curation` (it already loops and reports per-sweep failures):

1. A select-all checkbox on the failed view plus one "Mark selected invalid" button, or
2. Per-group checkboxes + a single action, or minimally
3. An affordance seeding the Browse `sweep-grid` selection with the failed sweeps so the existing Curation panel acts on them.

The shared `failed-reason` input should feed whatever batch action lands.

## Related

jernerics-iiv (curation gating reliability), jernerics-j9s (scope bar stacking one warning line per invalidated sweep — compounding with one-at-a-time flows).
close_reason: Failure view now supports batch invalidation: controls row (select-all checklist + 'Mark selected invalid' button) above the groups, per-group checkbox beside each existing per-sweep button; batch applies apply_curation once over all checked ids with the shared failed-reason (reason enforcement and per-sweep failure report surface verbatim); select-all writes derive from the request's mounted ALL-input ids so a fresh failure between render and click cannot desync the wildcard output; stray checklist re-fires PreventUpdate. Merged from agent commit fb50502 after independent verification (121 + 757 server tests passed in worktree, full gates 1952 passed / 6 skipped).
